Market Recap 	
Week of May. 11 through May. 15, 2026 	
The S&P 500 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrack.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fycharts.com%252Findices%252F%25255ESPX%2FOaA%2FBGjIAQ%2FAQ%2F46f7ba79-fcd8-42dc-85c9-9b1df61e2a4d%2F4%2F0UCnVG_HiJ&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8d8edf2bc859445fd4d408deb4e0a08f%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639147074054160189%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=s6b1sTgIXUsF9KGyW5%2FK%2FsVuQnZNFAk24uRWUi7%2F4dY%3D&reserved=0>  index edged up 0.1% this week, its seventh consecutive weekly gain, as a strong advance in energy stocks helped outweigh declines in other sectors.

The S&P 500 ended the week at 7,408.50, up slightly on the week but down from the new closing high it reached Thursday at 7,501.24. The market benchmark also hit a new intraday high on Thursday at 7,517.12.

The seven-week win streak is the index's longest since a nine-week run that ended in December 2023. The S&P 500 is now up 2.8% for the month and has climbed 8.2% in 2026.

The week's advance was driven by gains in only four of the S&P 500's 11 sectors, led by energy amid surging oil prices on the back of renewed Middle East worries. Consumer staples, technology and health care also rose this week.

Declines across the remaining seven sectors came amid inflation concerns.

US annual consumer inflation accelerated in April to the fastest pace in almost three years as energy prices surged amid the near-complete closure of the Strait of Hormuz, data released this week showed. Another report showed US producer prices in April rose at the fastest pace in four years as broad-based increases in services and goods signaled intensifying inflation pressures.

The energy sector jumped 6.8%, followed by gains of at least 1% each in consumer staples, technology and health care.

Fragile peaces


There was a three-day truce last week in the Russia-Ukraine war. A cease-fire in the Iran war continues, though President Trump said it was on “massive life support.” Israel and Hezbollah are still firing on each other despite their cease-fire. Nothing seems to move the needle toward peace.

Cease-fires in the age of Trump “have become a tool of performative diplomacy, stand-alone commodities used to manage media cycles while the machinery of war grinds along,” writes Marc Santora <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2FS-H7mNZTUsfOW_b37MPJeQ~~%2FAAAAARA~%2F2MA2AsCbRrJDXSx_mkomtqgOo7i5Ps7AnG8vqyWRHSFOKB-CQ7tBWHriI7oKGZcoA9T-EvwUm5jZi3vwqFB9S7jj94T6nTQdVypkmfNcO62lkMnMCKsh92I5_rS01YUWJDK_Msa11f78aqZsYgi2lCldn_x9ijCTP0xQXnF6VdvZPChim2A6yh1MZBD3118DWCZpdY3ZqYnyoSRXQ2P_CGnjxbjGMfEHOOrrwHG1IEGvJRJtcqwKBoIpjyHhbqDzWf9HdVWfNoGLQOw3ZugMjsl6eh1P-iJX-fkzzsiFla8SwNhGET5xsTMxAMPhxoG4bCNZSjvJzKPPk0-J3h4D7O3jRcbZ2d7w0ehYEfGCKmfs57eQ9ElE44nodVmMChFg&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C53218fdf18cb41427b9008deb4cb9b56%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146983758407988%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=m6Qw187HePw0aa9lEQBcSOAFBOVC5p166mCAOtZw7Ys%3D&reserved=0> , who covers the Ukraine war. A cease-fire looks like peace, and it’s good for headlines. And it’s better when fewer people die. But it doesn’t solve the underlying conflict.

And is peace even the goal for leaders in these conflicts? Linda Kinstler wrote about that <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2FRQVanmMTvvjSCjwMx5eH-Q~~%2FAAAAARA~%2FUGr_gcU3kwhtYQrQOWUtImeTqn4wpQY3zRdZrgJDFAfALrAsn1-7mgVfXkFZ1jx3cziyvQeZxc63NtggiP94SLAJcQlXoEYDAzilOtTzsjwctEWFDnEIWDIAn8yorLHYAwAPCe3p4vi2hq_By24o3O-1rIh-RqIb5MGaOCW0m8ocKupUF8f8rMz9ph2ev9YIVDnVTzWYyFXpK-AO2kqHmh0Wikv_Pe7Xni-Sn7OMygO2crgbwn-iuE8AYfresIZhHgem4eDFfkFJtmy-KuDE8d-Ifirv5TZEI9zFZyZMegt6uZgnbok3qsfqXqBK5AlxjipA6f7dASjv5itLQYWYHcTAg1F4zLh1KoBnUNNv361qImYWq9SKb1YXbGrftvLZHPvcDPt8QR8oLjdsxAHphg~~&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C53218fdf18cb41427b9008deb4cb9b56%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146983758423077%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=JNjocW5EMss3BzWHGAL%2B%2F29pF6UOGP296m8jTob%2FW%2BM%3D&reserved=0>  for The New York Times Magazine last year. By using cease-fires, she asked, “have world leaders avoided difficult conversations about the origins of wars and the possibility of justice, and left the entire world less stable?”


Peace on the ground?


So how seriously should we take these stopgaps? I asked Marc if cease-fires were helping in Ukraine. Here’s what he told me:

 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2FS-H7mNZTUsfOW_b37MPJeQ~~%2FAAAAARA~%2F2MA2AsCbRrJDXSx_mkomtqgOo7i5Ps7AnG8vqyWRHSFOKB-CQ7tBWHriI7oKGZcoA9T-EvwUm5jZi3vwqFB9S7jj94T6nTQdVypkmfNcO62lkMnMCKsh92I5_rS01YUWJDK_Msa11f78aqZsYgi2lCldn_x9ijCTP0xQXnF6VdvZPChim2A6yh1MZBD3118DWCZpdY3ZqYnyoSRXQ2P_CGnjxbjGMfEHOOrrwHG1IEGvJRJtcqwKBoIpjyHhbqDzWf9HdVWfNoGLQOw3ZugMjsl6eh1P-iJX-fkzzsiFla8SwNhGET5xsTMxAMPhxoG4bCNZSjvJzKPPk0-J3h4D7O3jRcbZ2d7w0ehYEfGCKmfs57eQ9ElE44nodVmMChFg&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C53218fdf18cb41427b9008deb4cb9b56%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146983758436883%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=UArU6ipcefKHGFKithSh8MYLRj%2FQMpd92o2ePCSVGUQ%3D&reserved=0> 	
Ukrainian soldiers training in April. Brendan Hoffman for The New York Times	

The fighting at the front never stopped, and at midnight Monday, as the truce technically expired, Russia resumed its bombardments of towns and cities across Ukraine. Ukraine also resumed its strikes aimed at the Russian oil industry and military production facilities.

Russia’s bombardments often combine attacks on military targets with strikes aimed at purely civilian targets. It blew up an apartment building in Kyiv last week and by Friday, rescue workers had recovered the bodies of at least 24 people, including two children.

Same as it ever was. Dread continues in Israel, where I tracked down David Halbfinger, our Jerusalem bureau chief. Life there is precarious right now, he said:

In Israel and Gaza, it’s hard to talk about cease-fires with a straight face, or at least without an ironic tone, given that Israeli airstrikes are killing Palestinians almost every day in Gaza, Hezbollah drones are targeting Israeli soldiers and one Israeli division said it killed 60 Hezbollah militants in Lebanon just over the past week. Trump has watched with frustration as a Boeing project to replace the two jets used as Air Force One has dragged. (They won’t be ready until at least 2028.) An Air Force spokeswoman declined to say how much it would cost — it is at least $400 million. The plane has been inspected to find hidden devices that might be used to spy on the president, and it needs to be painted with a new design Trump picked out. It’s unclear what typical protective measures — such as hardening the electrical systems against the pulse from a nuclear attack — the Air Force might decide to do without. Gas versus refunds

 

In recent years, retailers have faced endless supply-chain challenges. Now comes the Iran war.  

 

Retailers are starting to report results for their fiscal first quarter, which spans February through April. That means it included two full months of the conflict. The disruption will be a test early into the tenures of the newly minted CEOs at Walmart and Target, both of which report this week. 

 

Both executives are longtime employees who have taken the helm at pivotal moments. Target is in the middle of a turnaround effort <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45756597.489321%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9idXNpbmVzcy9yZXRhaWwvdGFyZ2V0LXRndC1lYXJuaW5ncy1xNC0yMDI1LWQ4MDBjODY0P2VhZnNfZW5hYmxlZD1mYWxzZSZtb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBc07fa1a7&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C437f1af13fac4a0d692e08deb4c89cfd%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146970899224474%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Whm%2BchlXCm5WptjAP4jmXZk8kABt1%2BIxRdBQCHSciHc%3D&reserved=0> ; Walmart is proving out <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45756597.489321%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9idXNpbmVzcy9yZXRhaWwvc2hvdWxkLXdhbG1hcnQtcmVhbGx5LWJlLXRyYWRpbmctbGlrZS1hLXRlY2gtY29tcGFueS04NjMyOTM0OD9lYWZzX2VuYWJsZWQ9ZmFsc2UmbW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBafcc423e&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C437f1af13fac4a0d692e08deb4c89cfd%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146970899239563%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=H56mXE1VWI9drYwHQPSBBqqdsNXmO%2F3pKaLfcBSFwZ8%3D&reserved=0>  tech-like growth. Investors like the stories. Target and Walmart shares are up 24% and 18% this year, respectively, outpacing the market. 

 

Gas prices could get in the way, though. Walmart executives, speaking at a Citi sector conference in March, said gas prices close to $4 a gallon cause consumers to trade down to cheaper options. Prices at $5 a gallon become more of a shock, according to a note from the bank. 

 

Nationwide retail gas prices have hovered close to $4 a gallon since April and have been closer to $4.50 since May.

 

But there is a counterweight. Tax-refund season was particularly generous because of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Americans in aggregate received 18% more in refunds than they did a year earlier, according to Steven Shemesh, equity analyst at RBC Capital Markets. This translates to roughly $50 billion of additional dollars circulating in the economy.

 

In other words, retailers’ top lines for the quarter aren’t likely to show much damage from the Iran conflict. 

 

The bottom line might be different. In aggregate, retailers in the S&P 500 have expanded margins over the past few years, even during stretches of high inflation. Last year, the group’s operating margins were at their highest levels since S&P Global Market Intelligence started tracking the data in 2006.

 

Now, prices are rising for everything from fertilizer, plastics, aluminum and fuel, potentially squeezing margins. 

 

For Walmart, the bottom line matters because its tech-like growth story, which has helped catapult its share price to 43 times forward earnings, is predicated on growing operating profits faster than revenue. Much of this is thanks to high-margin revenue sources such as advertising and membership fees.

 

Rising costs could undermine that growth. Last week, Walmart said it would cut or relocate about 1,000 corporate workers. 

 

Retail giants like Walmart, Target and Costco, which reports later in the month, are better positioned than most in a rising price environment. They tend to have bargaining power with suppliers, sell necessities and are seen as value destinations. Target’s decision to invest in groceries seems prescient. 

 

Still, the longer the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, the harder it will be for retailers to hold the line on margins.

As millions flock to GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic, Mounjaro and Zepbound, doctors warn the drugs can cause rapid and significant muscle loss <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-guiuldl-hrkusddg-yd%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cc36b20be9baa47b5e47508deb4c6f942%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146963843622769%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=SZ5By8arXbfBzDNwf834O0tV0mB%2BuUhQ5Svjy96ASag%3D&reserved=0> . Natasha Dangoor reports:

A: GLP-1 drugs have been a success for public health and the pharmaceutical companies that make them. Taking them has improved health and happiness for millions of people. But for at least some of the 13 million Americans who use the drugs, losing muscle along with fat is an unexpected downside that isn’t broadly discussed or immediately apparent.

The drugs can cause rapid and significant loss of lean muscle mass, up to 10%, comparable to a decade or more of aging, according to an analysis published by the American Diabetes Association.

The loss of lean tissue is similar to weight loss from dieting, but the magnitude over a short period can lead to frailty, instability and lack of coordination, doctors and researchers say. Another concern is that losing muscle could slow down patients’ metabolism, leading to weight regain.

Drugmakers say weight-loss drugs should be taken only on the advice of a physician and as part of a long-term plan that includes diet and exercise.

Hi Graham,

 

I hope you’re having a nice week!

 

I’m reaching out today to share a few important updates and reminders with you about preparing for your upcoming program with the University of Sydney:

 

*	Upcoming annual leave
*	Next steps before you can apply for a student visa
*	Units of study
*	Next steps in June and July

 

Upcoming annual leave

I will be on annual leave starting from 21 May and I will be back at work from Monday 1 June.  Emails received close to or during my time away will be responded to as soon as possible after I return to work.

 

Next steps before you can apply for a student visa

You are strongly encouraged to complete all of the below steps as soon as possible between now and Friday 15 May (Sydney time <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.timeanddate.com%2Fworldclock%2Faustralia%2Fsydney&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbfd2a236c38c4acd91a208deb4a211df%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146805639663128%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=X3Qpotak48A2eBxC1uACfH5vzHrBhA4ODGyMiNx6ynI%3D&reserved=0> ) for the best possible chance of me being able to issue your eCoE before my time away:

 

*	Accept your offer and arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) – Access the “respond to offer” task by logging into your Sydney Student Portal <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsydneystudent.sydney.edu.au%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbfd2a236c38c4acd91a208deb4a211df%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146805639684368%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=qrnmMCMEqt8GPBNlNgjbJWxQvIePbOgmDmg2hIejnVM%3D&reserved=0>  using your 9-digit USYD student ID# 560803615 as the username.  Once logged in, click the “My Applications” tab.  The system will then take you through a series of screens related to the process of accepting your offer and paying your AUD$12,600 tuition fee.

	*	Are you using financial aid? If you plan to use US financial aid (like federal loans/FAFSA or private student loans) to pay your University of Sydney fees please let me know before you make a payment so I can tell you the slight variations to the standard acceptance process for you. 
	*	OSHC is specific type of compulsory health insurance policy that the Australian Department of Home Affairs requires all student visa applicants to have, regardless of any other health/travel/life/etc type of insurance policy students may have from their home country.  You may choose from the following options for your OSHC policy: 

		*	OPTION #1: Pay to USYD to arrange your OSHC with Allianz Care 

			*	If you choose this option, when completing the “respond to offer” task indicate your preference accordingly and ensure that you make the necessary AUD$380 payment to USYD.

Subject: What would you sell?
Body:
A ProFellow newsletter from Dr. Vicki Johnson
 ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ 
 <https://d11n7da8rpqbjy.cloudfront.net/profellow/1231864671884DVJ_Newsletter_Header.png> 

 

To those of you recently subscribed to this ProFellow newsletter by Founder Dr. Vicki Johnson, welcome! Each Sunday, you'll receive application tips and insights on how to apply successfully to the world's most competitive opportunities.

 

Dear readers,

 

On Wednesday, I launched a brand-new idea that came from a stroke of inspiration. It’s ProFellow’s first Creator Incubator <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FylTVZRQ23pCp%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb609f4b62d524e37e96108deb4101973%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146178419747334%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=5PPqKtRB7v%2F6XsbUHNmjsNdqlbiO%2FXttNYW8hjXsDys%3D&reserved=0> —a FREE, 8-week entrepreneurship program for aspiring content creators. In this selective program, a group of 10 people will have an opportunity to learn how ProFellow works as a content business and learn strategies to build and launch a revenue-generating content platform. (Check it out and apply soon if it interests you! <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FylTVZRQ23pCp%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb609f4b62d524e37e96108deb4101973%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146178419772220%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=X9EB%2FAL3PL4Sr3kZu%2BzWhmqC5Vz6Wmb3t7KsJp15nLI%3D&reserved=0> )

 

I was inspired to host this program because I see so many people in my network struggling to get a job. I also noticed that few people stuck in a long-term job hunt don’t try out entrepreneurship. When I ask why, people tell me it’s too hard to get started, or it would take up too much time, or it just isn’t what they trained for.

 

But when employment options are scarce (and they may be for the next several years), it can be life-saving to have more options for making money. This is why learning how to create your own products and services to sell is a valuable skill that everyone should develop. And today there are so many free and low-cost tools to launch a business, you don’t need a lot of money to start one.

 

Building a profitable, salary-sustaining business is hard and can take some time. But getting started in entrepreneurship is pretty simple.

 

🍎 The key to success in entrepreneurship is to leverage the assets, perspectives, and talents that are unique to you.

 

My daughter Liv, who is 8, is a budding entrepreneur. She loves to make origami and decided to start selling origami door-to-door with her older brother. I loved that they would be outdoors practicing their pitch skills and getting to know their neighbors, but I didn’t feel too confident they would make much money selling folded paper animals. I thought they would face a lot of rejection and come home disappointed (but a lesson worth learning, I thought). 

 

Boy, was I wrong! An hour later, they came home with $38 to split between the two of them 🤯.

 

The next time they went out, I accompanied them so I could take a peek at what they were doing. Their primary customer was not the busy mom or teenager who answered the door, but retired people. One gray-haired woman who opened her door couldn’t help but exclaim how cute they are and what a pleasure it was to meet two children from the neighborhood. She patiently listened to their pitch and product presentations, then went inside to find her wallet. “What can I purchase for $10?” she said, smiling. Liv cut her a package deal and gave her 3 of her best pieces that she had priced at $5 each. The woman thanked them profusely and invited them to come by again anytime. She told them, “You remind me of my grandchildren.”

 

That’s when it occurred to me. My kids weren’t selling origami, they were selling joy.

 

 <https://d11n7da8rpqbjy.cloudfront.net/profellow/467733776033Liv_Origami.jpg> 

My daughter Liv manning an origami stand on our block.

 

Now, if I tried to sell origami door to door, it wouldn’t work. I just don’t have the cuteness factor that would bring a retired person joy.

 

But there are other things I could sell that might work. I could sell a creative writing class for seniors. Or sell postcards with my original watercolor paintings.

 

I won’t know what works until I try — and I will probably face a ton of uncomfortable rejection in the process — but I will be doing, learning, and improving until I get it right. 

 

And let's face it — there's no good excuse not to try. If an 8-year-old can do it, so can anyone!

 

If you’re curious about entrepreneurship, ask yourself: What could I sell? What product or service would leverage my unique talents, skills, and ideas? And what is holding me back from pitching my product or service to someone who needs it?

 

Even if your new business doesn’t make much money to start, the exercise of starting a business helps you build skills in product creation, design, marketing, and sales, which are skills valuable in any industry. It also helps you meet people and build networks in your local community. And best of all — you now have something to put on your resume other than a gap.

 

If you're curious about media and online content business models (for education, storytelling, journalism, and more) apply for ProFellow’s Creator Incubator <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FylTVZRQ23pCp%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb609f4b62d524e37e96108deb4101973%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146178419787348%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0z0ZspqeWzJvBPjt%2Fc0CZCZhDX%2FgIEYwZMLrk5rI%2B0M%3D&reserved=0> ! 

 

In just 5 days I have already received 83 applications — I’m thrilled by the demand! I know it’s going to be very hard to pick just 10 people, so I’m thinking now about how I can serve more people with this knowledge. I might turn the 8-week live sessions into a newsletter, e-book, course, video series, or a much larger live program. If you apply to the Creator Incubator <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FylTVZRQ23pCp%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb609f4b62d524e37e96108deb4101973%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146178419802137%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0A8DmTSImskjRImJcPCvK9%2Foi0bvAVDb43%2F4fbgF22A%3D&reserved=0> , I’ll know you're interested in this subject.

 

I hope you’ll be inspired to try out entrepreneurship. And if you want to learn more about how to pitch yourself, don’t forget I have a great book on this: Pitch Your Potential <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FHMoCAyBQsYXc%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb609f4b62d524e37e96108deb4101973%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639146178419816140%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Hx5buDhuV%2B3fLAXfl6PoV9zdDM%2BUwR9BIRHNopHpscI%3D&reserved=0> .

 

Here's to your entrepreneurial success!
 

Warm regards,

 

Vicki

This year, that question sounds like a dare. Neither the manicured grass nor the dignified tune of “Pomp and Circumstance” can mask the sour vibes. Inflation is accelerating. Hiring is glacial. Businesses are petrified by wars, tariffs and artificial intelligence.

Gather the evidence, and the verdict seems clear: These poor graduates are screwed. A small army of internet essayists promotes this view, and young Americans subscribe to it. Held back


In 1965, the Who sang “The Kids Are Alright.” Thirty years later, a California band called the Offspring recorded its own take, “The Kids Aren’t Alright.” For my generation, the second song is more resonant. Its title has become a Gen-Z rallying cry.

Commencement speakers are in the unenviable position of having to acknowledge these issues without bumming everyone out. The Morning analyzed 50 graduation speeches — half from this year, half from 2018 — to see how their messaging has changed. While many of the 2018 speeches focused on gender and racial inequality, this year’s focused more on generational inequality and grit.

A third of the 2026 speakers explicitly mentioned “resilience,” but only one said that word in 2018. James Talarico, the Democratic Senate candidate in Texas, told graduates at Paul Quinn College this month that the economy simply isn’t built for Gen Z. “Young people can’t afford to buy a home,” he said. “Young people can’t afford to fill up their gas tank.”


Brain fog


When things get hectic, people tend to delay big decisions. Businesses do the same, which helps explain what’s happening in the labor market.

“Think about young college grads like an investment: You pay now and you get the full benefit later,” David Deming, a Harvard economist and undergraduate dean, told me. “Companies are much less likely to make those investments when the environment is so uncertain.”

Executives don’t know whether they’ll wake up to a huge trade deal with China or a complete decoupling. They don’t know whether energy prices will rise or fall.

Throw A.I. into the mix, and things get even hazier. Experts can’t agree on how this technology might change the economy, but it menaces the white-collar professions that so many students were told to pursue. Commencement speakers this year couldn’t stop talking about it. “The Calamity Club” by Kathryn Stockett: In this long-awaited follow-up to “The Help,” Stockett tracks a plucky orphan and a resourceful spinster doing whatever it takes to survive the Great Depression in Mississippi. Both yearn for family and find it in unexpected places. One devises an ingenious plan to open a brothel with a “slapped-together band of misfits,” while the other proves unsinkable under the most trying circumstances. At more than 600 pages, “The Calamity Club” is a commitment — but, as our reviewer wrote, “It’s all about plot, baby.”

This week’s subject for The Interview is Maine’s presumptive Democratic Senate nominee, Graham Platner, a progressive 41-year-old military vet and oyster farmer who is pitching a working-class revolution. He is poised to take on the incumbent, Susan Collins, in November.

You grew up in a small town, didn’t graduate college, became a bartender. But also your father was an attorney, your grandfather was a Cornell-educated architect, quite well known. How do you think about class? Is working-class how you grew up or how you live now?

I work with my hands. I don’t make a lot of money. My wife and I work incredibly hard and we probably make, like, $60,000 a year combined. We don’t have money left over. We’re not saving for retirement. I was lucky. I got to buy my house in 2017, and I could not afford my house today. My house has gone up almost three times in value.

Do you have family money?

My father gave me the mortgage, except, of course, because he’s my dad and he’s an attorney, he gave me a significantly higher interest rate than the bank would have. I could have used a V.A. home loan if I had wanted to, but at that point it was just easier to do it that way. But I could never get that today because I couldn’t afford the monthly mortgage if it was three times what it is. My income hasn’t gone up three times. But you know, in this day and age, you are working class if you make your money from work and wages. The world of wealth disparity has become so intense that there are just so many people now who are sitting on so much money who do not work. They make money off their investments. I know it’s an expansive definition of “working class,” but I think you need to have an expansive definition when we have the most expansive margin of wealth inequality in the history of the country.

Q: Tax-loss harvesting is the hottest thing on Wall Street. How does it work? 


The stock-market surge has helped popularize a new strategy to secure gains without all the taxes. Reporter Miriam Gottfried broke it down.

A: With the stock market near record highs, it isn’t enough to be winning anymore. Wealthy investors are now obsessed with losing, too. The hottest investment on Wall Street promises a magical-sounding mix of both: index-beating performance that also comes with losses to offset capital-gains taxes.

Millions of investors are sitting on big gains in concentrated stockholdings, be they shares of Magnificent Seven tech giants, plain-vanilla index funds or employee shares of hot tech companies.

The traditional move would be to turn to direct indexing, a form of tax-loss harvesting that has been an investing mainstay since the early 2000s. There is now $1.1 trillion invested in that strategy, according to research firm Cerulli Associates.

But for many investors who have ridden this ebullient stock market, direct indexing is no longer generating the losses it once did. So financial advisers are trying to turn up more losses for their clients by employing strategies that use leverage. Over $150 billion has flowed into this newer breed of tax-loss harvesting, known as long-short tax-aware, or tax-aware alpha, according to Brent Sullivan, who writes about the industry on his Substack, Tax Alpha Insider.

The strategy comes with some risks for investors. ✏️ Things got messy in the courtroom showdown over AI’s biggest breakup. The three-week trial was technically about Elon Musk’s allegations that he was snookered into fronting OpenAI millions. But the proceedings also revealed the mythmaking behind the AI industry <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-guiujht-hrkusddg-i%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C3213a857de07443d62b908deb33f0aac%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639145280530414282%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=zdDGpGxjfvhTUeYUFqQs2srSLj81ngHYTKiQJgDuwBc%3D&reserved=0> —and exposed the financial anxieties, short tempers and personal vendettas that have shaped it. Musk has pushed for Sam Altman’s removal as CEO, among other things. The changes he's pursuing would greatly complicate OpenAI’s path to a potential IPO.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

Q: The global oil map is being redrawn. Who are the winners and losers? 


Disruptions from the war in Iran are rewriting the geopolitics of energy everywhere. Jason Bordoff, a professor at Columbia University and the founding director of the Center on Global Energy Policy, breaks down how the global fault lines are shifting.

A: The crisis in the Strait of Hormuz is forcing governments to redefine energy security for an age of geopolitical fragmentation—one in which resilience depends not only on how much oil the world produces, but also where it flows, who can get it and which countries are able to absorb the shock when it’s interrupted.

But while the oil market is global and rising costs are felt everywhere, the consequences are not evenly distributed.

Asia has been hit first and hardest. Last year, the region relied on the Middle East for roughly 60% of its imported oil. The disruption has been particularly severe not just for crude but for refined products like diesel and jet fuel, which have doubled in price since January.

In wealthier countries, pricier oil generally shows up first as inflation and weaker growth. In lower-income importing countries, it manifests as shortages: Bangladesh has limited air conditioning to 77 degrees. Laos has shortened its school week and Sri Lanka made Wednesday a public holiday. In Pakistan, cricket teams are playing to empty stadiums.

So far, shale production has shielded the U.S. But the most consequential effects of the crisis may not be the immediate price spikes around the world but the strategic policy shifts they prompt.

Just as nations dramatically rethought energy policy after the oil crises of the 1970s, a disruption of this scale will force governments around the world to adapt. The best graduation speeches, I think, are the ones grounded in personal experience, the ones that ring not only sincere, but also profoundly felt. Effortlessness is a myth.” Yes! Anyone can see that Taylor Swift tries hard, that her success has come via fist-clenching, teeth-gritting effort. “The people who wanted it the least were the ones I wanted to date and be friends with in high school,” she continued. “The people who want it most are the people I now hire to work for my company.” If a billionaire is going to genuinely connect to an audience of debt-saddled grads, she has to show that she came by her wisdom honestly. She has to truly mean it.

In George Saunders’s speech, he tells a story about a girl in his seventh-grade class who was “mostly ignored, occasionally teased,” and how he could tell this hurt her. He wasn’t mean to her, he says, but, 42 years on, he regretted that when he witnessed her suffering he responded “sensibly, reservedly, mildly.” The oft-quoted line is, “What I regret most in my life are failures of kindness,” but the line that I like even better is more direct: “What’s our problem? Why aren’t we kinder?” He goes on to propose some theories, and some solutions. I love this speech because it emerges from a relatable personal experience, and it dwells in specifics rather than conceptual oratory. Every person present has their own failures of kindness. Everyone present is implicated.

It has one more line that I love, that, if I must receive life advice via Instagram quote card, I would be delighted to see in my feed. She tells the graduates that the most useful suggestion she can make is that they go on being students for the rest of their lives, and then says, “Don’t move to a mental slum.”

I don’t know exactly what that means, to move to a mental slum, but I find her admonition witty and hyperbolic and inarguably wise. And, like the most enduring speeches, it still has impact. Sontag wasn’t optimistic about the world into which her audience was graduating, but she felt it urgent that they not abandon their education when they exited the halls of knowledge. She concludes by telling them if they stop reading or looking at art or “whatever feeds your head now,” then they’re getting old. I think about this a lot — what feeds my head. And her sign-off was appropriately encouraging: “I wish you love. Courage. And fantasy.” I wish that for us, perpetual students all, no matter what we’re commencing this spring.

May 16 	

Hey team!  <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/smile.png?v=15> 

We want to share some feedback with you about the 260417-website-generation-v2 project.  <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/down_arrow.png?v=15> 


CE1: Insufficient interactivity validation in the video


 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/cross_mark.png?v=15> Unacceptable
Recordings often scroll quickly and don’t show cursor/hover/click behavior, so, it’s unclear whether menus/buttons/cards work or, have hover states.

 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/white_check_mark.png?v=15> Recommendation

*	When recording the screen, Do interact with your website to give a demo of its features, such as buttons, animations, footer navigation, and links.
*	Ensure the demo clearly shows functionality and interactivity.


CE2: Capture / completeness issues in documentation


 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/cross_mark.png?v=15> Unacceptable
Low count of screenshots, less coverage (not all required areas are snipped), and recordings contained freezing/lags.

 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/white_check_mark.png?v=15> Recommendation

*	For Recordings: Please re-record if the video does not show a perfectly clear view of your website or if there are obstructions/unclear content, which includes freezing or lags.
*	For Screenshots: Ensure completeness by capturing the initial state of the website, different pages or sections, the results of user interactions (e.g., adding to cart), different states after scrolling or interacting with elements, and any dynamic content or animations in action.


CE3: Prompt adherence


 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/cross_mark.png?v=15> Unacceptable

*	Sites sometimes don’t follow key prompt constraints (wrong brand name, wrong color, font, missing required details).
*	Prompts described as vague/underspecified (e.g., “Gen-z vibe,” “single page HTML”)

 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/white_check_mark.png?v=15> Recommendation

*	To Improve Adherence, spend time writing a detailed first prompt to clearly describe the site, attach references, and set the direction you want.
*	For Branding, the model should invent its own name and mark, taking inspiration from any visual language but Do not copy logos verbatim.
*	Use targeted follow-up prompts to address specific color or font fixes (“swap the palette to warmer tones”).


CE4: Visual design / layout / readability concerns


 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/cross_mark.png?v=15> Unacceptable

*	Hero section issues (text hard to read, dull image, doesn’t fit screen etc.).
*	Alignment/spacing/whitespace problems (designs feel dull/generic).
*	Contrast/readability issues.

 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/white_check_mark.png?v=15> Recommendation

*	Do not submit cramped or misaligned layouts (elements overlapping or too close together).
*	Fix low-quality images and ensure the site is visually appealing during the refinement step.
*	Verify against quality issues like inconsistent UI elements or poor sizing before submission.


CE5: Watermarks / asset quality


 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/cross_mark.png?v=15> Unacceptable
Broken image links, low quality images, copyrighted materials, etc.

 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/white_check_mark.png?v=15> Recommendation

*	Do not ignore broken images or broken media; all images and media must load properly.
*	Fix any missing or error images using a follow-up prompt to ensure the final submission is high quality.

Subject: New Task Type Coming Soon to Aether – Egocentric Physical Understanding QA
Body:

Hi Graham,




A new task type will be available in Aether platform soon: vs-1777054010-egocentric-physical-understanding-qa-v0. These tasks are designed to help improve how robots understand and reason about the physical world by creating challenging, image-dependent multiple-choice questions based on first-person perspective scenes.





🎯 Your Objective


The images show everyday environments from the user’s point of view, often with one or both hands visible.

Your goal is to carefully analyze the image(s) and create questions that require:

*	Physical reasoning
*	Spatial understanding
*	Task interpretation
*	Scene awareness





✅ What To Do


*	Focus on physical reasoning (movement, space, stability, interactions).
*	Carefully inspect the full image(s), including small or partially hidden details.
*	Use zoom and compare both frames in multi-frame tasks.
*	Ensure the question depends on the image and cannot be answered through general knowledge alone.
*	Match the assigned category appropriately (e.g. spatial reasoning, safety, task progress).
*	Create questions that require multi-step reasoning (observe → interpret → infer).
*	Write realistic and plausible answer choices, including strong distractors (“near misses”).
*	Use annotations only when they genuinely improve reasoning or clarify spatial relationships.
*	Base questions on real-world physical constraints such as clutter, collisions, fit, balance, and stability.





❌ What To Avoid


*	Do not ask questions that are obvious or answerable without the image.
*	Do not ignore or force-fit the assigned category.
*	Do not create unrealistic or silly answer choices.
*	Do not use “None of the above” or “All of the above” as options.
*	Do not rely on only one frame in multi-frame tasks when both frames are provided.
*	Do not overuse annotations or make the answer obvious through annotations.
*	Do not overlook subtle but important visual details such as occlusions, small changes, or partially hidden objects.
*	Do not create purely descriptive questions that lack reasoning or inference.
*	Do not include distractors that are immediately and obviously incorrect.
*	Do not skip careful scene analysis before writing the question.




Thank you all for your continued effort and attention to quality.

The Outlier Team

Duke Rewind


You made it through the semester, Blue Devils!  

The month of May celebrates Asian American and Pacific Islander heritage and is a time to reflect on the perseverance and joy of these groups and individuals. Beginning in the early 2000s, The Asian American Studies Working Group (AASWG) called out the lack of opportunity to study Asian American and Asian culture at Duke, and in turn asked Duke to establish an Asian American studies program. During the time, they were in contact with student organizations at peer universities, who were in the process of establishing their own Asian American studies programs and departments, helping to inform the movement at Duke. AASWG also participated in the nationwide Abercrombie and Fitch protests, calling out the unwillingness of the corporation to recognize the consequences of including racist graphics on their merchandise. Included below are some print materials showcasing the activities of the Asian American Studies Working Group in 2002.  

Despite the efforts of the working group, a department of Asian American and Diaspora Studies wasn’t established at Duke until 2018, which today offers a minor in Asian American and Diaspora Studies. Reestablished in 2016, AASWG has been working on expanding the offerings of the department and representation of the Asian and Asian American student experience at Duke as a whole.  They are still active in doing so. You can find more information about the working group here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fduke.campusgroups.com%2Fclick%3Femail_links_id%3D484212%26member_id%3D26313612&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce95529452ffb4e9ac70a08deb2aae3df%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639144644205536942%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=s9%2B0HSvz5Z5cYq1wgCAsQKbOiBCC1SjdHolTM3g%2FIxc%3D&reserved=0> , or in the Asian American Studies Working Group records <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fduke.campusgroups.com%2Fclick%3Femail_links_id%3D484213%26member_id%3D26313612&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce95529452ffb4e9ac70a08deb2aae3df%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639144644205549468%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=4Y%2Fyh0IevdvEgDpjieV4Cn398M2lHW%2Bt5YcSaaWrFOE%3D&reserved=0>  at the Rubenstein Library. Subject: Reminder about accepting your offer + USYD adviser on leave 21-30 May - Graham Heath MILLS (SID 560803615)
Body:
Hi Graham,

 

I hope you’re having a nice week!

 

I’m reaching out today to share a few important updates and reminders with you about preparing for your upcoming program with the University of Sydney:

 

*	Upcoming annual leave
*	Next steps before you can apply for a student visa
*	Units of study
*	Next steps in June and July

 

Upcoming annual leave

I will be on annual leave starting from 21 May and I will be back at work from Monday 1 June.  Emails received close to or during my time away will be responded to as soon as possible after I return to work.

 

Next steps before you can apply for a student visa

You are strongly encouraged to complete all of the below steps as soon as possible between now and Friday 15 May (Sydney time <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.timeanddate.com%2Fworldclock%2Faustralia%2Fsydney&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb09a10922d2c4035b3e708deab181e4b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639136317582713889%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=iWLc%2FF%2BTn6RY4BLLPyqthaSvexZcINlDIzgPGlVvE2s%3D&reserved=0> ) for the best possible chance of me being able to issue your eCoE before my time away:

 

*	Accept your offer and arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) – Access the “respond to offer” task by logging into your Sydney Student Portal <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsydneystudent.sydney.edu.au%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb09a10922d2c4035b3e708deab181e4b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639136317582739143%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=PGqHhBKBzbi2OMTEPB2DQqU1joUUncbhAxndeCulRIU%3D&reserved=0>  using your 9-digit USYD student ID# 560803615 as the username.  Once logged in, click the “My Applications” tab.  The system will then take you through a series of screens related to the process of accepting your offer and paying your AUD$12,600 tuition fee.

	*	Are you using financial aid? If you plan to use US financial aid (like federal loans/FAFSA or private student loans) to pay your University of Sydney fees please let me know before you make a payment so I can tell you the slight variations to the standard acceptance process for you. 
	*	OSHC is specific type of compulsory health insurance policy that the Australian Department of Home Affairs requires all student visa applicants to have, regardless of any other health/travel/life/etc type of insurance policy students may have from their home country.  You may choose from the following options for your OSHC policy: 

		*	OPTION #1: Pay to USYD to arrange your OSHC with Allianz Care 

			*	If you choose this option, when completing the “respond to offer” task indicate your preference accordingly and ensure that you make the necessary AUD$380 payment to USYD. 

		*	OPTION #2: Arrange your own OSHC policy directly with a DHA-approved provider 

			*	Regardless of which provider you choose, ensure the insurance type is “Overseas Student Health Cover” and that your policy has a start date 27 July 2026 or earlier and an end date no earlier than 9 January 2027.   
			*	Visit the website of your preferred OSHC provider directly for more information on how to arrange an OSHC policy: Allianz Care <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.allianzcare.com.au%2Fen%2Fstudent-visa-oshc.html&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb09a10922d2c4035b3e708deab181e4b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639136317582758269%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=s9DOG39o5iFIbtyDj1V4R8A2FlzU0G3wZoF2AokUQrc%3D&reserved=0> SEMESTER DATES   

As you are planning and preparing for your program, please keep the following key dates for the USYD Semester 2 2026 program in mind:   

   

Recommended arrival: 20 to 24 July 2026 (we recommend students aim to arrive during this week) 

**Welcome (Orientation) Week: 27 to 31 July 2026 (compulsory day on Mon 27 Jul) 

Classes begin: 3 August 2026 

Mid-semester break: 28 September to 2 October 2026 

Classes end: 6 November 2026 

Study vacation (STUVAC): 9 to 13 November 2026 

Final exam period: 16 to 28 November 2026 

Earliest departure date: Sunday 29 November 2026

 

**It is a requirement of the Duke Study Abroad office that all Duke students arrive to Sydney in time for the start of the official Welcome (Orientation) Week.  For Semester 2 2026, the official Welcome Week begins from Monday morning 27 July which means arriving to Sydney no later than Sunday 26 July.  

 

As you are planning your travels, keep in mind the international date line and its impacts on which flight itinerary you might choose.  If you are travelling directly from the USA to Australia you ‘skip’ a day due to crossing the international date line on the way.  This means you would need to depart the USA no later than 24 July USA time in order to arrive to Sydney by 26 July Sydney time.

Buzzer Beater

 

If you just finished doing your taxes, good for you. No, not because you beat the IRS deadline: It’s a sign you’re well-off.

 

Americans with high incomes and substantial savings tend to file closer to April 15. Those living paycheck-to-paycheck often file as early as possible because refunds are a spending lifeline.

 

That matters more than usual this year. About $335 billion in refunds will be paid out in the first half of this year, up by about 11.2% compared with 2025, according to S&P Global. Most of that has been received <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45211137.464339%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2Uvc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LXRvZGF5LWRvdy1zcC01MDAtbmFzZGFxLTAzLTEzLTIwMjYvY2FyZC9zNW9SNEc4UVQyT21ZZE5WYkFCbD9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB0b98aead&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ca0806f86a2b14018315508de9adce5a7%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118470727181882%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=CrCjh6Y0TKCXecxpMJfa2vSkkzfcdKfefHwxoquiGYM%3D&reserved=0> . The way the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was implemented, economists flagged a turbo boost to income early in the year. The tax cuts are retroactive, but paycheck withholding mostly changed in January.

 

That means both benefited households around the same time. In the past, about a fifth of any increase in refunds showed up during tax season in general merchandise spending.

 

It’s a shame about the war, though. Another difference between wealthy households and those closer to the edge financially is the impact of higher gasoline prices on their finances.

 

While that hasn’t entirely offset OBBBA’s boost to income, it will if crude oil stays above $100 a barrel for the remainder of the year, according to S&P’s math. And it disproportionately hits poorer people who were most likely to make discretionary purchases with part of their refund check.

 

Leaving pump prices aside, the propensity to spend refunds rather than to save them or to pay down past borrowing is also affected by how recipients feel financially. Delinquency rates as a share of U.S. household debt hit a nine-year high in the fourth quarter and were concentrated in lower-income zip codes, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45211137.464339%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubmV3eW9ya2ZlZC5vcmcvbmV3c2V2ZW50cy9uZXdzL3Jlc2VhcmNoLzIwMjYvMjAyNjAyMTA_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBe7c21755&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ca0806f86a2b14018315508de9adce5a7%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118470727259205%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=HJRNwvicCM0aVl5YU%2B87i%2FHsvtXKoZUqijOs0ldinGA%3D&reserved=0> . And last week’s report <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45211137.464339%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9lY29ub215L2NvbnN1bWVyLXNlbnRpbWVudC1oaXRzLXJlY29yZC1sb3ctcGVyLW1pY2hpZ2FuLXN1cnZleS0wMWFiODVmZT9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBd872a065&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ca0806f86a2b14018315508de9adce5a7%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118470727331512%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=z6UIk6q3sZElheEoDMElYBsuPMwwMZqIcrwInNHe%2Bzo%3D&reserved=0>  on consumer sentiment from the University of Michigan hit the lowest level in its 74-year history.

 

Government statistics, private-sector surveys and even knowing to the penny how much was paid out in refunds can only tell us so much about what people will do with their money. A lot more nuance will be offered by executives of retailers, hotels, cruise lines, auto dealers and restaurant chains in the coming weeks.

 

That could include companies that did well by capturing share from competitors—McDonald’s getting business from pricier fast-casual or full-service chains, for example, or Walmart attracting more middle-class customers.

 

Sending people money is easier than getting them to spend it.

✏️ Never mind that one of the world’s most-important energy chokepoints remains closed <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkizit-hrkusddg-h%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C443f7ba56ceb4356f9b508de9ad8796b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118451715739815%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Lgtx%2Fvn6rYAFGCGc64FLlA%2BVv14796wHTiQWRRmzLXo%3D&reserved=0> —markets are roaring back anyway. Oil prices have retreated, Wall Street banks just posted blockbuster earnings and CEOs are touting a resilient U.S. economy. That combination has stocks back on the brink of records <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkizit-hrkusddg-k%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C443f7ba56ceb4356f9b508de9ad8796b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118451715766519%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=E5GXjUySuqxoKFMmPpR9Cj%2FagrLu9IRMHTat4dB0mJw%3D&reserved=0> , with some investors betting a strong earnings season could power them even higher. To be clear, worries over the Iran war haven’t disappeared. Our foreign correspondents find the U.S.-Israeli attack has fast-tracked the ascent of hard-liners and apocalyptic religious followers within Iran’s new regime <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkizit-hrkusddg-u%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C443f7ba56ceb4356f9b508de9ad8796b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118451715790842%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Gid9KCWYguKckpPhL9mqeXUxh0jzKfiw%2BigKnZ3r88k%3D&reserved=0> , raising doubts about a lasting peace. Follow our live coverage of the conflict here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkizit-hrkusddg-o%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C443f7ba56ceb4356f9b508de9ad8796b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118451715851901%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=lAKfEQSaxDW92RgImMVGhnxH%2Bhlxhwlsi%2FS2UiPU%2BRw%3D&reserved=0> .

Q: How are airline passengers being hit by the jet fuel crunch? 


The U.S. war with Iran is driving up jet fuel prices, and airlines are leaning on passengers to foot the bill <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkizit-hrkusddg-yh%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C443f7ba56ceb4356f9b508de9ad8796b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639118451716342209%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=LtYBH3IwPRW9cIUfLdTd%2FrXXIJg2CO%2B7IA5Sy2TCpL4%3D&reserved=0> , explain WSJ’s Amira McKee, Alison Sider and Stephanie Stamm. 

A: Skyrocketing jet fuel prices are jolting the aviation industry, and airlines are bringing travelers along for the ride. Airlines have increased baggage and other fees, pledged to cut back on flights and raised fares since late February. Ticket prices for some routes have doubled from a year ago.

Airline executives say higher jet fuel costs are feeding steeper fares, though demand for certain routes and the health of the economy also factor into prices. Some international airlines have introduced fuel surcharges on customers’ tickets.

The U.S. is a significant producer of jet fuel, and American carriers are more insulated from volatility in the Middle East. Still, because aircraft fuel up locally, U.S. airlines can be subject to the squeeze on some international flights. And with no signs of a reprieve on the way, carriers have begun trimming their schedules.

Subject: U.S. FCC's 1-year Honors STEM program opportunity
Body:
Hi Econ Majors:
The U.S. FCC Federal Communications Commission has established an Honors STEM program (1-year career development program) that includes economics, comp sci, data science, engineering, OR, etc.  The Office of Engineering and Technology is building its data division, with AI and analytics opportunities, and seeking recent graduates and seniors graduating in May 2026 as candidates.   For application and program info, see https://www.fcc.gov/workforce-jobs/honors-stem-program <https://www.fcc.gov/workforce-jobs/honors-stem-program> . 

This STEM program was developed by UNC Prof. of Economics Jonathan Williams, who is currently leading the FCC's Economics and Analytics Office and shared the info.
Prof. Kim

INTRODUCING THE US CHESS ACADEMY

IMC Trading and Team Liquid have officially launched the US Chess Academy — our flagship student chess competition, open to all college students across the US and Canada regardless of skill level.

This isn't just for chess experts. Whether you are a seasoned competitor or just love the game, the US Chess Academy is a unique opportunity to compete, connect with one of the world's leading trading firms, and potentially come face-to-face with World Chess Champion Magnus Carlsen.

Here's how it works: 

*	Students apply and compete in a virtual qualifier via Chess.com (May 19 or 20).
*	The top player from each qualifier earns a spot at the Championship Finals at IMC's Chicago office on July 12–13, 2026.
*	Finalists will compete in a live tournament, take part in a showmatch with Magnus Carlsen, tour IMC's Chicago office, and network with our teams across trading, research, and technology.
*	All travel and accommodations for finalists are fully covered by IMC.

Thank you so much for your continued partnership. We hope to see you in the qualifier!

Subject: SportsMedia Technology (SMT) Data Challenge Opportunity
Body:
Hi All,

 

We wanted to share this cool opportunity from Sam Sanger at the Duke Career Center:

 

 

“My name is Sam Sanger and I recently started at the Duke Career Center as our Career Specialist for Data & Technology. I  wanted to share information on a Data Challenge <https://datachallenge.smt.com/>  from local company SportsMedia Technology <https://smt.com/>  (SMT) that students can register for. 

 

The Data Challenge website has all the information on their MLB case study and how to register. This would be a great opportunity for members of the Sports Analytics Club to form a team or register as individuals. I've added the event to our Data & Technology Career Community in Career Hub, but having it directly shared with the club members would be amazing!”

 

Best,

DSAC Exec

Subject: IFSA | Brand-new housing option for Fall 2026
Body:
Dear students,

 

We have the rare opportunity to offer you a brand-new housing option for Fall 2026 that is very close to the UNSW campus. 

 

Scape Lachlan is located in Kensington, directly across the road from a light rail stop, with a direct 5-minute trip to the UNSW stop.  Alternatively, it only takes 15 minutes to walk to campus.  The same tram line will take you to Sydney Central Station, and the Sydney CBD in 18 minutes.  Also outside the building is a bus stop with frequent buses to Coogee Beach, Bondi Junction and Sydney Airport. 

 

Scape Lachlan features a range of communal spaces available to all residents where you can rest and relax or socialise with friends. These include the swimming pool, games room, cinema room, communal kitchen, and a social lounge.  With a karaoke room, social spaces and a more outdoor, poolside setting, Scape Lachlan gives students a lighter mix of amenities beyond the usual common room formula. There’s room for group hangs, easy downtime and more open-air living built into the property. Please see photos of the common areas here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.scape.com.au%2Fsydney%2Fscape-lachlan%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C82da200fc1d8459745e808de9a60453d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639117935495111702%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=p%2FwWsptKiAiPDRfHkxUVwgdNt4D5Rf36dPLBh0BHtck%3D&reserved=0> 

 

The rooms that IFSA has access to are the two-bedroom apartments. The 2-Bedroom Shared Apartment combines social living with personal privacy. Each private bedroom includes a flat-screen TV, dedicated study area, wardrobe, comfortable double bed, unlimited high-speed Wi-Fi, and air conditioning (heating and cooling). The shared spaces with the apartment feature a modern kitchen, small dining area and a bathroom. Please see photos of the rooms- 2 Bed Apartment at Scape Lachlan | Scape <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.scape.com.au%2Fsydney%2Fscape-lachlan%2F2-bed-apartment-scape-lachlan%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C82da200fc1d8459745e808de9a60453d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639117935495141894%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=YGfrCNzNpKrzZ5MKlu%2FdqW5L5XIRvsFPMkj6JFWN2SM%3D&reserved=0> 

 

As this is a new and more premium accommodation, the supplemental fee for this option is US$2,800.

 

Benefits to Scape Lachan compared with other IFSA housing options

Brand new accommodation (UNSW Village is very basic and older-style accommodation & other Scape options are quite modern but well-used)

Equipped with Airconditioning- both heating and cooling (UNSW Village does not have heating or cooling)

Only sharing bathroom with one other person (UNSW Village has three students per bathroom)

Double bed (All other options have single beds)

Much closer to campus than the other Scape options, which are a 30+ minute commute by public transport

Much closer to the beach than other Scape options

 

If you would like to take up this option, reply to this email as soon as possible. *Note: Housing form is only visible to students who have completed their initial application items*

 

We only have up to 20 beds available, and they will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.  If you and a friend would like to share one of these apartments, please list who you would like to share with as well.  Both students need to confirm this choice and roommate request individually, in writing. 

 

Please note that your home institution may not pay for supplemental housing fees, so if you are unsure, please check first.

 

If you choose this option, you are agreeing to a supplemental fee of US$2,800.  If you have already completed your housing preference form in the student portal and want to be in this option, respond to me by 22 April, and this will become your first preference.

 

Thank you,

DANIELLE JONES

Enrollment Counselor

Subject: Bain & Company: Interview logistics
Body:
Graham,
   
We look forward to meeting with you for your Atlanta <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fbain.avature.net%2Fltrk%2FeyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6NTk0Nzc4MSwiaGFzaCI6IjVmNWNkYmU5YmJkMDliODZhNjBmMzJiZmUwMjdkNjBjYTIyZWNkOTVjZWJjZDk2NTJhMjMwZjFjM2I1MWRkZDcifQ.PaAwQC98oMBwvpz84wIdG5G621GypdnfjTUMs1A4WoA&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9b1093a0620f416aa9e908de9a5b1a0f%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639117913283660556%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=a5Ll6fVd0EHTH5hNblKezIG9CZWWiqqh361u8vnmI84%3D&reserved=0>  interview with Bain & Company. 
 
Interview details

	*	Date/Time: Please reference your confirmed interview date and time in your recruit portal <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fbain.avature.net%2Fltrk%2FeyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6NTk0Nzc4MSwiaGFzaCI6IjI4ZGQzNzM0ZDgwNWU1ODgxMGFiMzI4ZTliYzRjYjgyMTM4MjMxMGY3ZTdhMDRmNzJlYWUxODEyYWQ5MjQ2NjIifQ.nSNgG6bSFqPeNv1tnzhimpI5joSBfZ9aeQb1mSg9H38&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9b1093a0620f416aa9e908de9a5b1a0f%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639117913283685436%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=4h3XvHdkI5ZlWGiplo9DprEegWgOn8PL6A6wbE2k7l0%3D&reserved=0>  under the "My Meetings" section.
	*	Format: Two 30-minute case interviews (1 hour total).
	*	Zoom Links: Access the Zoom links in your recruit portal (there is one link per interview). Click “Join Meeting” for each session.
	*	Interviewers: Interviewer names will be visible in your portal 24 hours before your start time.
	*	Attire: Business professional.

Day-of Logistics (Zoom)

	*	Please join each interview ~3 minutes before your scheduled start time.
	*	At the end of your first interview, click “Leave Meeting” and join your second interview using the separate Zoom link in your portal.
	*	Interviewers use a virtual waiting room, so you may not be admitted immediately — thank you for your patience.
	*	We recommend having paper and a pen available. Calculators or other electronic devices (e.g., phones, calculators, iPads) are not permitted.
	*	For tips on preparing for a virtual case interview, please review this overview <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fbain.avature.net%2Fltrk%2FeyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6NTk0Nzc4MSwiaGFzaCI6ImFjZjEyMGNiNWVmMTQyODg1MTczMTNmN2NiODg5N2NmNWQwOTVkY2E4NGU2MTI3MGIzNmE5OGNkY2E4YmUyMWYifQ.cgj9Wy4nlprqtx62JLosz1DXwLHGOX1fRBe_1eUwZCg&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9b1093a0620f416aa9e908de9a5b1a0f%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639117913283699377%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=44dtCIhtLjItHmg8h3rS9ycWywQ%2BGBH4yCEVZpMjE5I%3D&reserved=0>  of what to expect.

For scheduling questions or technical issues with Zoom or the Recruit Portal, please contact the Interview Scheduling team <mailto:Bain.RecruitingInterviews@Bain.com>  and include the position and recruiting office in the subject line.


Interview Expectations & Confidentiality


Bain’s case interviews are confidential and should not be disclosed outside of the interview discussion. Please ensure you are in a private space where others cannot overhear your conversation.

	

	*	Case content may not be recorded, screenshotted, transcribed, or shared.
	*	AI tools may not be used at any point during the interview process.
	*	Electronic devices for calculations or note-taking are not permitted.
	*	If you have previously seen the case introduced during your interview, you must inform your interviewer immediately. 
	*	Sharing case information, including the case topic, is not representative of the integrity we expect of our employees and may result in offer withdrawal.

Graham, we’re here to support you throughout the process — please don’t hesitate to reach out with any questions. We look forward to speaking with you soon!  
   
Best,

Subject: Spring Orientation on April 18 🌸
Body:
<https://duke.campusgroups.com/read/505b5127-3815-11f1-bd1c-025c6e3d0caf.png> 

Hello! 

This is a reminder that all RA/CA student staff members for the 2026-2027 academic year are expected to attend Spring Orientation on Saturday, April 18th from 1:00–5:30pm. Please plan to arrive at White Lecture Hall by 12:45pm so we can start right at 1:00pm. 

The L&D team worked hard to make this orientation a half-day because we value your time and commitment to the role. Please plan to be present and ready to participate during our time together. We will wrap up around 5:30 PM, and boxed dinners will be available for you to pick up on your way back to your communities. 

Additionally, we will announce the Summer Training theme during Spring Orientation! It may be too late to cast your vote for the theme, but if you have gut feeling or a theory based on evidence please fill out this form <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fduke.campusgroups.com%2Fclick%3Femail_links_id%3D482999%26member_id%3D26414878&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C0bf0070aa6b9486d779808de9a393fd8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639117767839544957%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Gj7bPKY%2BS4i6rj1pd5l8wV%2FKt8zyXjKYEyV91O6iJmI%3D&reserved=0>  with your guess for the Summer Training theme! Subject: Re: Interinstitutional Course Approval Request
Body:
Hello Mr. Mills,




thanks for the note.  I'm willing to give FECON 300 credit for Bus 474 because of the focus on optimization and Bus 358 because of the use of advanced statistical analysis tools.  But I won't accept Bus 470; it doesn't have enough econ or finance content.




Keep this message and let me know what you want to do.




CFullenkamp




On 4/14/2026 9:28 AM, Graham Mills wrote:


	Dear Professor Fullenkamp,
	I hope this email finds you well. I am a Duke undergraduate currently studying abroad, and I am in the process of finalizing my course schedule for my return to Durham in Fall 2026.
	I am hoping to take an interinstitutional course at NC State that will count toward my Economics/Financial Economics (FEcon) elective requirements. I have found three potential courses and have attached their syllabi to this email. Because undergraduates can only take one interinstitutional course per semester, I have ranked them in my order of preference:

	1.	
		Top Choice: BUS 474: Logistics Management
	2.	
		First Backup: BUS 458: Analytics: Data to Decisions
	3.	
		Second Backup: BUS 470: Business Process Management

	Could you please review my top choice (BUS 474) to see if it would be approved specifically as an Econ/FEcon elective? If it is not a match, I would greatly appreciate it if you could evaluate the backups.
	I have also attached a partially filled Interinstitutional Approval Form. Once we confirm which course is approved, I would appreciate your digital signature on the form so I can route it to my Academic Dean.
	Thank you so much for your time and consideration.
	Best,
	Graham Mills

The first-quarter confessionals now rolling in aren’t just a way for America’s shareholder class to focus on regularly scheduled programming instead of the Middle East—they’re likely to be excellent overall. The only fly in the ointment might be what executives say about the rest of this year.

 

First, the numbers. At the start of the week, S&P 500 earnings-per-share growth was forecast to rise 13.2% year-over-year, according to analyst estimates compiled by FactSet.

 

That’s probably too conservative. FactSet says actual earnings have exceeded estimates for 37 of the past 40 quarters to the tune of around seven percentage points.

 

The first quarter could be a real standout when the numbers are all in—the fastest growth since 2021 when profits were rebounding from the pandemic shock. It’ll almost certainly be the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit EPS growth, making for the longest streak since 2011.

 

What’s not to like? One quibble is that growth is narrow, with tech carrying basically the entire load. Consumer staples, consumer discretionary and industrial stocks are seen expanding per-share profits in the low single-digit percent range. Healthcare probably will be an outright drag.

 

Energy and materials stocks, both a small part of the S&P 500, are seen having a decent quarter, getting a late lift from the war. Analysts have bumped up expectations for the remainder of the year for that group. They’ll benefit even if peace breaks out tomorrow.

Trump’s erratic behavior and extreme comments in recent days and weeks have turbocharged the crazy-like-a-fox-or-just-plain-crazy debate that has followed him on the national political stage for a decade.

It’s a debate you can see in the polls. A Reuters/Ipsos poll in February found that 61 percent of Americans think Trump has become more erratic with age. Just 45 percent say he is “mentally sharp and able to deal with challenges.” That’s down from 54 percent in 2023.

Trump’s language fuels the fire. “He uses more profanity, speaks longer and regularly makes comments rooted in fantasy rather than fact,” Peter writes:

He wanders off into odd tangents — an eight-minute ramble at a Christmas reception about poisonous snakes in Peru, a long digression during a cabinet meeting about Sharpie pens, an interruption of an Iran war update to praise the White House drapes. He has confused Greenland with Iceland and more than once boasted of ending a fictional war between Cambodia and Azerbaijan, two countries separated by nearly 4,000 miles. (He evidently means Armenia and Azerbaijan).

Still, part of Trump’s base loves it. A Princeton historian put this question to Peter: “What can be more anti-establishment than someone who is willing to be out of control?”

✏️ Harvard University President Dr. Alan Garber is no stranger to being in the Trump administration’s crosshairs—so much so that I asked if he had been texting Pope Leo advice over the weekend. During our conversation at the 92nd Street Y last night, one thing was clear: Despite the pressure, Garber remains a staunch optimist. Questions from the audience (and you!) reflected anxieties about everything from grade inflation to AI in classrooms. He didn’t dismiss those fears, warning that tightened immigration and funding cuts put the U.S. at risk of ceding its lead in math and science to China. Yet he maintains an unshakeable faith in Harvard’s commitment to the pursuit of truth and knowledge.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

A: Washington kicked off the operation yesterday by positioning more than 15 U.S. warships, according to a senior U.S. official.

Placing resources and warships near Iran’s coast could make U.S. assets susceptible to attack, officials said, so the U.S. will likely try to intercept or quarantine commercial vessels on either side of the Strait of Hormuz to prevent them from entering or leaving Iranian ports.

Any warship can approach a tanker suspected of violating the blockade, but if a ship doesn’t comply with a request to board, specially trained Marines and special-operations forces, such as Navy SEALs, would be needed to conduct a contested boarding.

The Navy has significant firepower in the region that could support the blockade, according to officials.

Iran’s “shadow fleet” will likely sit out the fight, but Iranian-flagged ships are more likely to attempt to transit the waterway, said retired Vice Adm. John Miller, a former commander of U.S. Naval Forces Central Command. Those vessels may be guarded by a detachment of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces, he said.

If the U.S. takes control of tankers, it may need a captain, crew (if the existing crew doesn’t comply), and a place to park the vessels, according to former officials.
