Subject: Upcoming Events on Pluralism, Free Inquiry and Belonging
Body:
<https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fnas2aj%2Fr5qhzpw%2Fbpfxxy&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2ffce14b4ec1427005a008de730ee1db%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074704927272858%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=LngndmrL79HkvDP1igWSWk02hT5aoRwdsCZV%2FkbYEd8%3D&reserved=0> 
 <https://d31hzlhk6di2h5.cloudfront.net/20260223/6e/31/11/95/ec43b935cda05338a54636c7.png> 

Please join us for these upcoming events from the 

Provost's Initiative on Pluralism, Free Inquiry and Belonging. 

 

 

Mar. 3 | Author Rick Atkinson <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fnas2aj%2Fr5qhzpw%2Frhgxxy&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2ffce14b4ec1427005a008de730ee1db%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074704927315084%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=sM3FuGwHHL6%2BJbkRPTOWNvxHaZW9oX8e1EsEdYQSmxU%3D&reserved=0> 

Join us for a conversation with bestselling author and Pulitzer Prize-winner Rick Atkinson titled "What Do We Need to Remember About the American Revolution ... But Have Probably Forgot?" This event is free and open to the public, but tickets are required.

 

Mar. 3 | Former U.S. Poet Laureate Joy Harjo <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fnas2aj%2Fr5qhzpw%2F79gxxy&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2ffce14b4ec1427005a008de730ee1db%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074704927331097%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=IsCL9o07JBMxlVaJ0MW8A42rPT5LQa%2FXhnuMhM6ia10%3D&reserved=0> 

Joy Harjo, the U.S. Poet Laureate from 2019 to 2022 and the first Native American to hold the position, will give a poetry reading and hold a public conversation at Duke Chapel. Titled “Poetry and Spirituality,” the event is the Chapel’s 2026 Pluralism Lecture.

 

Mar. 5 | Arthur Brooks <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fnas2aj%2Fr5qhzpw%2Fn2hxxy&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2ffce14b4ec1427005a008de730ee1db%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074704927351437%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=pAAd0qt8PBiw7DDSnFKdR%2BZ2aAFtyE9jUWjoq%2B4izKU%3D&reserved=0> 

We all want to find happiness through a life lived with purpose. But how do our ways of thinking help or hinder us from finding meaning in our lives? How can conscious awareness of one’s emotions—a practice called “metacognition”—open up new possibilities for true flourishing? Join us for a lecture by Arthur Brooks, Professor at Harvard Business School, and a conversation with Nita Farahany (Duke Law) and Iain McGilchrist (Oxford). 


Mar. 5-7 | Cognitive Liberty: Interdisciplinary Perspectives <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fnas2aj%2Fr5qhzpw%2F3uixxy&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2ffce14b4ec1427005a008de730ee1db%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074704927372230%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=jG2QUFi14RlmGYbDQ8iuqox%2FrtjKSYyqzKg3BuOauRg%3D&reserved=0> 
New developments in neuroscience and technological innovations are putting increasing pressure on the fundamental legal notions of moral autonomy, self-determination, liberty, and conscience. This trans-disciplinary meeting will bring together neuroscientists, philosophers, theologians, lawyers, and engineers to consider moral deliberation, neurorights, and what it means to be free to think and believe in the digital age.

 

 

The Provost’s Initiative on Pluralism, Free Inquiry and Belonging <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fnas2aj%2Fr5qhzpw%2Fjnjxxy&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2ffce14b4ec1427005a008de730ee1db%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074704927394358%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=cAdEjxNuLOXMj4oZ7DnKJT9Lr%2FP6fk3TB%2FFPNXrpBrE%3D&reserved=0>  creates new opportunities for all Duke students, faculty, and staff to maximize learning and growth in a pluralistic academic environment and society.

Subject: DFE Student News & Events for the Week of February 23, 2026
Body:
Hi students! Please see below for this week’s DFE Student News and Events newsletter.

 

DFE News & Events:

 

Demystifying Finance: A Series <https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/demystifying-finance>  for First-years
Everything Investment Banking
Tuesday, February 24, 6:30-7:30 PM, 107 Friedl Building, East Campus – REGISTER <https://dukefinance.wufoo.com/forms/zrbmt8r0y7oakc/> 

Learn from upperclassmen what investment banking is, what analysts do day-to-day, and how to effectively prepare for investment banking recruitment. All questions and levels of knowledge about finance are welcome.

 

Markets Discussion Group with Mike Aguilar <https://www.fuqua.duke.edu/faculty/michael-aguilar> 

Thursday, February 26, 5-6 PM in Gray 228 - open to all class years, all majors  REGISTER <https://dukefinance.wufoo.com/forms/z16qju7b0qimyd0/> 

Participate in lively discussions on current events and how they impact financial markets and the broader economic environment. Learn how to watch the markets and formulate informed views about economic and business trends. Previous knowledge of the markets is not required. You’ll get something out of it whether you’re a first-year or a senior. Stay informed using the following resources available to all Duke students at no cost: The Wall Street Journal <https://education.wsj.com/?s=Duke&user_type=students&cat=2&page_type=searchresults&search_type=b> , Bloomberg for Education <https://guides.library.duke.edu/c.php?g=289830&p=1931454> , and The New York Times <https://www.nytimes.com/activate-access/edu-access> .

AmplifyME Finance Simulations
Explore roles in banking, markets, and Quant while building real-world skills, tracking performance, and accessing potential recruiting opportunities with top firms. AmplifyME’s live, virtual simulations are open to all Duke undergraduates and will be available through April. Learn more at econ.duke.edu/dfe/finance-simulations-amplifyme <https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/finance-simulations-amplifyme> .
Create an account <https://pathways.amplifyme.com/uni/signup/S58GKIE>  on the AmplifyME platform with verification code 779495 and your Duke email address. Onboarding instructions <https://econ.duke.edu/sites/econ.duke.edu/files/documents/Pathways%20Onboarding%20Instructions%20PDF_0.pdf> 
View the schedule of upcoming simulations <https://amplifyme.com/hubfs/Pathways%20Weekly%20Finance%20Simulations%20-%20w_c%2023rd%20Feb.pptx.pdf?utm_medium=email&_hsenc=p2ANqtz-8ys_fgtYj02H4ewmGX8HreSupI57IITSsyWYcIlLoG3R5FzXlviBcm4Iex4fEofXY4MUieaNqjdaXe9Gzew8rV335XUIpdS9klfFplvqjwv4jKtTw&_hsmi=404536506&utm_content=404536506&utm_source=hs_email> .

Dzialga Women in Finance Initiative – Class of 2029: the application form is now open

Sophomore through senior year, Dzialga Fellows engage with dozens of alumni in the finance space, are mentees and mentors, and develop professional skills within a supportive cohort. Sophomores take a trip to NYC over fall break to network with alumni at a variety of firms. Read more about the benefits of being a Dzialga Fellow and the application process at econ.duke.edu/dfe/dzialga-women-finance-initiative <https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/dzialga-women-finance-initiative> . The deadline to apply is March 4 at noon. 

 

DFE Advising Opportunities:

 

DFE Peer-to-Peer Advising for Sophomores

As a resource for your finance recruitment-related questions, five upperclassmen are offering drop-in office hours weekly on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday in Soc Sci 228A. For the student advisors’ schedules and bios, go to econ.duke.edu/dfe/eichel-finance-advising-network <https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/eichel-finance-advising-network>  under the Other Advising Opportunities heading.

Career Everywhere Drop-In Advising – open to undergraduates and graduate students
Tuesday, February 24, 1:00-3:00 PM in the DFE Conference Room (Social Sciences 228A)

Meet with Duke Career Center for 15-minute Drop-In Advising for quick questions, document reviews, etc. Time slots will be on a first-come, first-served on-site basis, the day of the event. NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED. Available to all undergraduate students and graduate students from the Duke Graduate School, Duke’s Pratt School of Engineering (PhD only), Duke Divinity School, Duke Medicine School’s Master of Biostatistics and Population Health Sciences programs. Visit Handshake <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/duke.joinhandshake.com/login__;!!OToaGQ!sk-RdI6xAUFbKi-pEqMVGqNWp8LL5pL2orS6SxyEUOAXo0Iq48WBf43IsyVW9CEwTsrDWji9b5r4hTNSWpo5$>  or CareerHub <https://careerhub.students.duke.edu/>  for additional information on the Duke Career Center.

Alumni Advising with Mark Augusti – open to all undergraduates  REGISTER <https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0F44ABAE29A7F5CF8-59754216-finance> 

Mondays, 12:00 – 1:00 PM, in the DFE Conference Room (Social Sciences 228A) 

Mark Augusti ‘87 holds weekly in-person advising hours for undergrads. This spring, Augusti teaches FMKT 390S-04: Financing Health Care Companies. Read his bio below:

Mark Augusti, MBA, is Founder and Managing Owner of Kenmore Advisors, an advisory and consulting firm focused on compliance, governance, and commercial strategy in the medical technology sector. Previously, Mr. Augusti was President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors at Conformis, Inc., a public orthopedic device company. Prior to leading Conformis, Mr. Augusti was Integra LifeSciences Corporation’s Corporate Vice President and President of Orthopedics and Tissue Technologies. Mr. Augusti served as Chief Executive Officer at Bioventus LLC, and was a member of the Bioventus’ Board of Directors. Prior to that Mr. Augusti spent nine years with Smith & Nephew, in a series of leadership roles within the orthopedics and biologics businesses. Prior to that, he spent 13 years at GE Medical Systems, where he held various sales, marketing and strategic management roles, both in the U.S. and internationally. Mr. Augusti serves as a director of the Massachusetts Health Policy Forum and has served as a director of the AdvaMed Accel Board. Mr. Augusti received his M.B.A. from the UCLA Anderson School of Management, and his B.S. in Computer Science and Economics from Duke University.

 

Student Club News & Events:

 

Energy and Climate Ventures Summit sponsored by Duke Energy and Climate Club
Tuesday, February 24 at 4:30PM in Gross Hall - open to  all class years  REGISTER <https://www.eventbrite.com/e/energy-and-climate-ventures-talks-and-reception-tickets-1982197234287?aff=oddtdtcreator> 

Join us for a networking reception, lightning talks, and other opportunities to meet leading alumni investors and entrepreneurs in energy and climate at this exciting half-day event! The summit is open to Duke students, faculty and staff, and non-Duke affiliated community members. Space is limited, so RSVP now to secure your spot!  Lightning talks include: Fernando Saavedra, Vice President at Decarbonization Partners  Haroon Inam, Co-Founder and CEO at DG Matrix Hazel Horvath, Founder and CEO at Ecolytics Keila Aires Diamond, Managing Director and Head of ESG at Quantum Capital Group Marcelino Alvarez, Founder and CEO at Photon Marine Sarah James, Partner at NGP Energy Capital. For more information, see the attached flyer, visit our website <https://www.dukeenergyandclimateclub.com/home> , or contact tyler.ratcliffe@duke.edu <mailto:tyler.ratcliffe@duke.edu>  with questions.

Students interested in reading up-to-date information about M&A deals, IPOs, and the markets as a whole, can SIGN UP <https://forms.gle/Y8DWBkHDrebZq6Ze7>  to receive BOW's Finance Newsletter. This is a great resource for prepping for interviews or just for staying current on financial news. For more information, reach out to dukebow.assoc@gmail.com <mailto:dukebow.assoc@gmail.com> .

Subject: 26-27 Housing Process: Study Away Status
Body:
Hello Graham,

Our records indicate you have submitted an application to study away for the fall '26 semester. Please submit the decline housing form <http://mercuryadmin.studentaffairs.duke.edu/page/housingportal>  as soon as possible. You will apply for spring '27 housing when the application is available in October.

 

Should your plans to study away for the fall '26 semester change, you will apply for housing when the application reopens in June as you will be required to live on campus.

 

If you believe you do not have a study away application on file or wish to cancel it, please contact the global education office directly at globaled@duke.edu.

 

Thank you.

📣 Announcements

1. Data Mini #1 Winners! 🎉
The Competitions and Opportunities Committee is happy to announce the winning team and honorable mentions from Data Mini #1! Congratulations to Stephen Yoon, Kaixiang Loke, Erica Lin, and Boram Shim on winning a Nasher/Commons meal and feature on the Statistical Science website! Honorable mentions went to the presentations by Wendy Wang, April Ren, and Fanghao Liu, as well as by Eileen Zhang, Lex Gu, and Charles Zheng.

1. SSMU Seminar - Galen Reeves 💡
The Research Committee is excited to welcome Professor Galen Reeves for an upcoming (in-person) seminar! Prof. Reeves is an Associate Professor of ECE and Statistical Science at Duke who uses information theory to analyze machine learning, high-dimensional inference, and signal processing tasks. He will give an overview of his work and its applications to engineering, physics, and more. Snacks will be provided! 5. Register for ASA DataFest 2026! 📊🏅

ASA DataFest 2026 at Duke, organized by the Department of Statistical Science, will take place in Perkins Library on Duke University West Campus, Friday March 20 through Sunday March 22.

DataFest is a data analysis competition where teams of up to five students attack a large, complex, and surprise data set over a weekend. Your job is to find and communicate insights into these data. The teams that impress the judges will win prizes! The event is open to all undergraduate students at Duke and beyond, regardless of level of programming experience.

The S&P 500 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrack.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fycharts.com%252Findices%252F%25255ESPXTR%2FOaA%2Fwo-GAQ%2FAQ%2F25ac630f-ba57-48c1-b02d-455ae8ba3c42%2F3%2FQniymFgELz&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C33f4910706d24bc0e8fc08de72e77159%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074535562836459%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2FHaN9vQ%2FoYE2KBggLSvT7NF3c3h6g0JqIEdiqjEV8R8%3D&reserved=0>  index rose 1.1% this week, led by communication services, as investors digested changes to US tariff policy amid a Supreme Court ruling.

The S&P 500 ended Friday's session at 6,909.51. Still, the weekly gain - which came in just four sessions as the market was closed on Monday for Presidents Day - wasn't enough to move the market benchmark into positive territory for the month. The S&P 500 is down 0.4% for February but up 0.9% for the year.

US President Donald Trump said on Friday he will sign an order imposing additional 10% global tariffs, under Section 122, after the Supreme Court invalidated his reciprocal tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

"We are also initiating several Section 301 and other investigations to protect our country from unfair trading practices," Trump wrote in a social media post.

The developments came as official data showed US economic growth was well below Wall Street's expectations in the final three months of 2025 as federal spending contracted due to the longest-ever government shutdown. Real gross domestic product rose at an annual rate of 1.4% in the December quarter, the slowest pace in three quarters; the consensus estimate was for 2.8% growth, according to a survey compiled by Bloomberg.

A delayed release of economic data also showed US consumer spending growth unexpectedly held steady in December, while the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation metric accelerated more than Wall Street's estimates to 3% year over year.

Communication services had the largest percentage increase of the week, climbing 2.3%, followed by gains of 1.7% each in consumer discretionary and industrials. Financials and technology added 1.5% each. Energy and real estate also eked out small gains.

Omnicom Group (OMC) <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrack.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fycharts.com%252Fcompanies%252FOMC%2FOaA%2Fwo-GAQ%2FAQ%2F25ac630f-ba57-48c1-b02d-455ae8ba3c42%2F4%2FnK8Qxve1il&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C33f4910706d24bc0e8fc08de72e77159%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074535562859005%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=RqP%2FlLP%2FmhPC%2FWwpMyO%2FoldBP685juSKjM1EpvqZZnw%3D&reserved=0>  led the gainers in communication services, jumping 21% as the company reported Q4 revenue above analysts' mean estimate and unveiled a $5 billion share-repurchase program, including $2.5 billion under an accelerated buyback. Omnicom also maintained its quarterly dividend rate.

Garmin (GRMN) <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrack.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fycharts.com%252Fcompanies%252FGRMN%2FOaA%2Fwo-GAQ%2FAQ%2F25ac630f-ba57-48c1-b02d-455ae8ba3c42%2F5%2FNtvjBD0yh9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C33f4910706d24bc0e8fc08de72e77159%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074535562884400%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2FkMA1aGV9k1XQE6HQkj%2FCaEDHi0Of%2BXsYk%2B1bqfUCGQ%3D&reserved=0>  shares led the climb in consumer discretionary as the company reported fiscal Q4 pro forma net income per share as well as net sales above analysts' expectations. Garmin also forecast 2026 pro forma earnings per share and revenue above Street views at the time. Shares rose 16%.

Deere (DE) <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrack.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fycharts.com%252Fcompanies%252FDE%2FOaA%2Fwo-GAQ%2FAQ%2F25ac630f-ba57-48c1-b02d-455ae8ba3c42%2F6%2F2YFnBi6scD&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C33f4910706d24bc0e8fc08de72e77159%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074535562907804%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=d8WijcXalwgdkKGCQ2UAb%2B2u5a%2FEnu4E%2BhD79TKy37o%3D&reserved=0>  was the top performer among industrials, climbing 9.9% as the company reported fiscal Q1 earnings per share and net sales above analysts' mean estimates.

On the downside, consumer staples fell 2.3%, followed by a 0.6% decline in health care and a 0.5% loss in utilities. Materials also edged lower.

Walmart (WMT) <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrack.pstmrk.it%2F3s%2Fycharts.com%252Fcompanies%252FWMT%2FOaA%2Fwo-GAQ%2FAQ%2F25ac630f-ba57-48c1-b02d-455ae8ba3c42%2F7%2FAuPTNvtPZC&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C33f4910706d24bc0e8fc08de72e77159%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074535562930005%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=zpmrQBwRzCzGdrsUDGKQKNk6q%2FrL%2BWyEqsyXXUU5yGs%3D&reserved=0>  was among the hardest-hit stocks in consumer staples, falling 8.1%. We'’re excited to announce that we will be hosting Abhi Kolli, former DREC President, tomorrow (February 24th) at 7:00 PM via Zoom.

Abhi is currently an Analyst at Starwood Capital Group, a leading global private investment firm focused on real assets. Dear Graham,

As a reminder, part of your Blackstone campus program application, is completion of the pymetrics online games. We cannot further consider your application until you complete the games within the 3 day timeframe. If you do not complete the games within this timeframe, we will assume that you are no longer interested in opportunities at Blackstone and we will withdraw your application.

Please note that even if you have played the 12 games already, if you have applied to multiple roles at Blackstone, you will need to release the results for every application by clicking on the unique link contained in each email you receive. - Work through the games steadily and complete in one-sitting; estimated completion timing is 25-30 minutes for all the games

- Please note there are no right or wrong answers in the games; they simply give us some insights on how you would react in certain situations

- Completion for the games is within 3 days of submitting your application; your application will not be complete until you complete the games

Please click the following link to complete the pymetrics assessment: https://www.pymetrics.com/invite/sc.3a2e6c1b91d540ff8ae83ace1bad6ee3/

1.	pymetrics can be accessed on either your mobile phone or computer (please note that pymetrics cannot be played on a tablet).

If you completed the games already using a different email address, please reach out to support@pymetrics.com to have your gameplay submitted for this application.



If you experience technical difficulties, please contact support@pymetrics.com

We hope you enjoy the games and the insights they provide. Have fun!

Best,

The next conflict


Is the United States about to wage war on Iran?

American forces have taken positions across the Middle East, with two aircraft carrier groups and dozens of fighter jets, bombers and other planes poised within striking distance of the country. President Trump said Friday he might use them in a limited strike to pressure Iran to end its nuclear program.

Trump badly wants that deal, which his predecessors chased — and never realized. He blew up nuclear enrichment sites in Iran last year. In talks last week, he pushed Iran for an agreement, but so far it has not assented. “Bad things will happen” if Tehran doesn’t sign a deal, Trump said last week. “You’re going to be finding out over the next probably 10 days.”

Now he has arrayed a force in the region to support a major conflict — one that could potentially last longer, and be deadlier, than last year’s 12-day war on Iran or the commando attack that removed Venezuela’s president in January. What justification does the White House give for a possible attack? Trump aides have mentioned a desire to protect protesters there, after the government killed thousands of them last month, and a wish to knock over the regime by removing the supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

That would certainly bolster what still seems to be the main motivation: atomic weapons. Last year, Trump said his attacks had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear program. Intelligence reports, however, cast the strikes more as setbacks. There have been signs recently that Iran is hardening its bunkers and getting ready to enrich more uranium.

Despite these drumbeats of war, Trump hasn’t sought approval from Congress, nor has he directly addressed the American people. Tomorrow is the annual State of the Union address, and perhaps we’ll learn more when he delivers it.

In the meantime, though, I wondered how Iranians are feeling about all of this. So I reached out to Erika Solomon, The Times’s bureau chief for Iran and Iraq, to ask. Erika told me there’s a sense of overwhelming grief in the country right now and a belief that the die has already been cast. An attack, many Iranians feel, is a near certainty. As she put it:

There are three major themes to the mood right now in Iran:

Mourning and division. Many Iranians are still wrestling with the shock and pain of seeing thousands killed in the crackdown on nationwide protests early this year. They are weary. The opposition is also fractured about what the future should look like. Others still support the government to varying degrees — or are simply wary of the alternatives. Many Iranians we speak to say they’ve never seen Iran as polarized as it is now. The economic crisis that first drove people to the streets in December has not ended. It’s only getting worse. We talk to middle-class families who have long since stopped buying meat for their meals. Now they’re choosing between paying rent or buying food. Iranians are bracing for the possibility of U.S. strikes at a moment when they are emotionally and materially devastated.

Anticipation and fatalism. The biggest question looming over every Iranian right now is: Will America strike? Many Iranians we speak to are extremely worried for their safety and don’t think American bombs can solve their problems. And yet a few tell us they welcome a strike because they’ve lost hope that there is any other way to get rid of the government and are willing to take a chance on foreign intervention — despite having seen how it went for their neighbors in Iraq and Afghanistan. No matter how they feel, there is a growing sense that strikes are inevitable, and the only option for them now is to prepare.

Those who can afford it are stocking up on canned goods and batteries. One blogger posted tips for how to organize two weeks’ worth of supplies. In the replies, Iranians asked how they were supposed to gather food for an extended war when they couldn’t feed themselves today.

Trump is limited in what he can do. Under the law he has now invoked, Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, tariffs may last only 150 days unless Congress extends them. And they’re capped at 15 percent, so the president can’t lift them again.

Now that the old tariffs have been deemed illegal, do the businesses that paid them get their money back? ✏️ Tariffs are a wild card again. The Supreme Court’s ruling has upended <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkjty-hrkusddg-h%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb5e577550dcc4d43574e08de72ce9d94%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074428932207519%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=BFTGI2z2GB6327fdBBXPz33HPD3kuzqd6Oc9ttQLmhQ%3D&reserved=0>  what appeared to be a somewhat-settled U.S. tariff regime. Now President Trump is doubling down on the levies—even though they have so far failed to rebalance global trade <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkjty-hrkusddg-k%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb5e577550dcc4d43574e08de72ce9d94%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074428932224793%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=QvFuCZX%2BP3txZ31lDKsLBL9xUL7qx7X%2BBCXhgYeinO8%3D&reserved=0> . On the contrary, recent data shows the tariffs that he has vowed to reimpose are cementing the trade imbalances. 

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

AI startups are using a novel fundraising tactic to juice their valuations. 


Serval closed a private deal with Sequoia at a valuation below $400 million. Days later, it announced another funding round—at a valuation above $1 billion. The surge highlights an increasingly popular tactic, reports Angel Au-Yeung. A startup sells a stake to a leading investor at one valuation and, soon after or at the same time, offers shares to other backers at a higher valuation <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkjty-hrkusddg-a%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb5e577550dcc4d43574e08de72ce9d94%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074428932352886%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=yF%2Fbp9XXByxpHMPuAUMi%2BmuOIRDWrdSmAvv34XoyL8s%3D&reserved=0> . The result: The leading investor books a massive gain, at least on paper, and the startup can publicize a higher value. Startups have long commanded lofty valuations. But several VC investors and outside accounting professionals said back-to-back deals are novel and raise questions about how much startups are really worth.

4


Venezuela’s leaders ran the economy into the ground—and they’re still in charge. 


After U.S. commandos removed former President Nicolás Maduro, Vice President Delcy Rodriguez was left in charge as interim president. She, along with Maduro and other insiders, had ruled an economy the International Monetary Fund estimates contracted nearly 70% from 2013 to 2025. Trump is now betting those same officials can resurrect Venezuela’s economy and make it safe for the $100 billion in private investment that he’s trying to coax from U.S. oil companies. It’s a tall order given the regime’s 27-year record <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkjty-hrkusddg-f%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb5e577550dcc4d43574e08de72ce9d94%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074428932365274%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=K9cpMe1QmO9gMWfdbJky27RlsgFun0%2BUx9O9uEj%2FF7k%3D&reserved=0>  of corruption, lawlessness and the hyperinflation that has led to food shortages, reports Paul Kiernan.

Q: How did a school photography company get caught in the Epstein files frenzy? 


Online sleuths poring over government files have drawn a tenuous connection between Lifetouch and Leon Black <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkjty-hrkusddg-w%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cb5e577550dcc4d43574e08de72ce9d94%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074428932415689%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=z5VjV6zuEdCnRrU9g11UrubAO%2B68yQjyxukfSX0GO0c%3D&reserved=0> , the former CEO of its private-equity owner, Apollo Global Management. Reporter Hanna Krueger wrote about the backlash, which has prompted school districts to cancel their contracts with the 90-year-old company.

A: The blast radius of the Epstein files has toppled C-suite executives, shamed financiers and led to the arrest of a former British royal. Now, school picture day is in the crossfire: A social media-led boycott has homed in on Lifetouch, the photography company hired by thousands of U.S. schools each year to take portraits of students.

But unlike Epstein’s cozy messages with business leaders, there are no exchanges with Lifetouch executives in the Epstein files. Its parent company, Shutterfly, was acquired by Apollo one month after the convicted sex offender’s death in 2019. And it’s one of nearly 200 companies in Apollo’s vast portfolio, which Black hasn’t overseen in five years.

The controversy over Lifetouch was caused by an army of amateur detectives looking for hidden links in the Epstein files. Any line of connection—no matter how thin or dotted—is setting off alarms.

Lifetouch maintains that neither Black nor any of Apollo’s directors or investors ever had access to Lifetouch photos.

Memory Lane

 

South Korea’s stock market was closed for three days last week in observance of the Lunar New Year, which is celebrated across much of Asia. It was a well-deserved break for the world’s best performing major market.

 

The MSCI Korea index rose a blistering 92% in 2025. It has rallied a further 40% this year versus a basically flat performance for the S&P 500. So what will the Year of the Fire Horse bring for Korean equities?

 

Somewhat disappointingly for American investors looking for diversification, it largely depends on the U.S. AI boom.

 

The Korean market is dominated by electronics exporters, and in particular makers of memory chips that go into AI data centers as well as personal computers and smartphones. There is now a global shortage <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F44277092.460403%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS90ZWNoL2FpLWlzLWNhdXNpbmctYS1tZW1vcnktc2hvcnRhZ2Utd2h5LXByb2R1Y2Vycy1hcmVudC1ydXNoaW5nLXRvLW1ha2UtYS1sb3QtbW9yZS04ZGQxNTE5ND9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBecc85fea&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C44631de82791486a2e7708de72ce5e76%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074427852896693%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=8fnEnzENihdqYOMNymWIz4Fkorpjt5M95rPxX%2B7lKvc%3D&reserved=0>  of these chips, causing a surge in pricing and profits.

 

Just two companies in this space, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, accounted for over half of the MSCI Korea index as of Jan. 30. Samsung’s memory business accounted for about a third of its revenue in 2025, while SK Hynix is a memory pure-play.

 

That has been nothing but good news for the Korean market lately, but it does carry risks. The memory-chip market is famously prone to boom and bust cycles, so much so that memory makers are moving only cautiously to add capacity in the current shortage.

 

This time could be different, of course, given the huge amounts of investment being poured into AI, with no end in sight. The problem is that this is effectively the same bet that investors in the U.S. are making in their own technology-heavy market.

 

For U.S. investors, buying into Korea isn’t diversifying, it’s doubling down. The MSCI Taiwan index has a similar problem, with a massive 59% weighting in chip-making giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. 

 

Investors looking to spread their bets into Asia might do better to look at Japan.

 

Like Korea and Taiwan, Japan is an AI beneficiary with many companies supplying needed hardware, often in niche spaces. Stocks there have also been on quite a run <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F44277092.460403%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS93b3JsZC9hc2lhL3doeS1qYXBhbnMtc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LWNhbi1rZWVwLXJpc2luZy1lZWJhY2M4ZD9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB79db9ad1&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C44631de82791486a2e7708de72ce5e76%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074427852912729%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=x%2FEhFPA2b9FIeVMF0uden0TqzNEF2rIzOJSTZddm8oc%3D&reserved=0> ; the Japanese market in 2025 notched its third consecutive year of 20%-plus gains.

 

But, unlike Korea and Taiwan, Japan’s stock market has ample other themes driving it, from autos to financials and consumer goods. Information technology is only the fourth largest sector in the MSCI Japan index with a 15% weighting, compared with 56% and 85% for South Korea and Taiwan respectively. 

 

The case for diversifying into markets outside the U.S. is strong. But not all markets offer the same degree of diversification.

Invest in Self-Care


Hatha Yoga in the Wellness Center


This free yoga class focuses on Asana (physical movement), Pranayama (breathing exercises), and Dhyana (meditation). Each class will include mindfulness & breath control techniques, warm up movements to activate the body, a sequence of postures to maintain balance, flexibility and strength, and finally a deep relaxation experience.

Date: Monday, February 23, 11:00 am – 12:00 pm 
Location: Student Wellness Center, Room 148

Duke Groups <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2F46o6qi%2Fw0yzscmd%2Fslcxmnb&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C52313e0f046e4f704e5008de72c516d0%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074387989200084%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=EJ7XO3vwqXHOEDrr5DQKEhh2FINTVlijJm7gWlVFHuc%3D&reserved=0>

In partnership with Duke CommuniTEA, this wellness experience allows you to gain a deeper understanding of wellness through tea culture. You will have the opportunity to interact through the medium of tea appreciation in a space that promotes relaxation and self-care.

Date: Thursday, February 26, 5:00 pm – 6:00 pm 
Location: Student Wellness Center, Oasis West

Duke Groups <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2F46o6qi%2Fw0yzscmd%2Fo6dxmnb&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C52313e0f046e4f704e5008de72c516d0%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074387989233881%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=q5WFq%2F8YEViGv91HlFWrETOR7kfX7IEH76L0YsWQXyk%3D&reserved=0>

Take a break and spend some time outside, practice embodied work, and experience profound community with plants, soil, and humans! Duke Campus Farms welcomes you to join in for their community work day with no farming experience necessary. You can coordinate carpooling at the link provided.

Date: Friday, February 27, 1:00 pm – 4:00 pm 
Location: Duke Campus Farm

Sign Up List <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2F46o6qi%2Fw0yzscmd%2Fkrfxmnb&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C52313e0f046e4f704e5008de72c516d0%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639074387989270441%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=DPZyt7nM9ZOgvKt%2BYxly6ckEE2RbaQbt%2BDIkIpmntMw%3D&reserved=0>

Subject: Internship Opportunities & Conference Sign-up!
Body:
Hey DECC,

Hope you all are having a great weekend! We have two exciting internship opportunities to share: 


*	
	North Carolina Utilities Commission Public Staff Internship

	Undergraduate utility policy interns will be assigned one main research project culminating in a report and presentation to members of the Public Staff. Projects will address pressing policy issues such as affordability, electric system reliability and resource planning. Applications are due tomorrow (2/23)! More information is available through the Nicholas Institute Energy Internship Program <https://nicholasinstitute.duke.edu/energy-internship-program> .




*	
	American Clean Power Internships

	American Clean Power (ACP) is the leading voice of today’s multi-tech clean energy industry, representing energy storage, wind, utility-scale solar, clean hydrogen, and transmission companies. ACP is proud to offer a summer internship program which runs for 8 weeks out of our Washington, DC headquarters. Intern positions include Federal Affairs, Markets & Transmission, Policy & Regulatory Affairs, State Policy and more. Visit the ACP website <https://cleanpower.org/about/work-with-us/#current-openings>  to apply.


Also, mark your calendars for the Sustainable Business and Social Impact Conference on Wednesday, April 8th! This event is hosted by Fuqua's Net Impact Club and will explore how leaders across business, policy, and social innovation can collaborate to turn ambition into action. Details & registration are available here <https://sites.duke.edu/fuquasbsi/> .


Best,
Gabe LaCount

An app on your phone lets you gamble on the timing of U.S. military strikes, on the existence of aliens and on the return of Jesus Christ. (Will he make his second coming before midnight on Jan. 1, 2027? Online speculators think there’s a 4 percent chance.)

Gambling is old — even older than Jesus. Scholars believe that thousands of years ago, the Egyptians bet on senet, a religious board game representing the soul’s path to the afterlife. A couple of millennia later, the Romans bet on life-or-death gladiator fights and chariot races. His latest obsession is Tweem, the platform that let him gamble on my post. “If I’m going to spend time viewing a tweet, I want to leave with something,” said Caldwell, 35, who added that he had “a passion for predictions.” Since creating his account around seven months ago, Caldwell has placed more than 25,000 bets — over 100 bets per day, on average.


What gives?


Online gambling now feels unstoppable, and it’s crossing over into places that once seemed unthinkable. Polymarket this year became “the exclusive prediction market partner” of the Golden Globes, which flashed “probabilities” (read: betting odds) on the screen before revealing award winners.

A side effect: Gambling is getting more abstracted, and more gamified. When betting feels effortless — when it doesn’t feel like betting — it’s easier to get addicted. Since 2018, internet searches seeking help for gambling addiction have increased more than 20 percent. The stakes of a given wager now feel “more like a concept than a reality,” Lia Nower, director of the Center for Gambling Studies at Rutgers, told me.

“From the time you’re 5 years old, you’re being primed to gamble,” Nower said. “It’s part of our culture now.”

Caldwell didn’t bet real money — for now, Tweem deals only in digital “points” — but he hopes that once the platform hits it big, it will shower him with crypto coins for having been an early adopter. In essence, he’s taking another gamble.

As for my post? Caldwell bet that it would reach nearly 378,000 views. It ran out of juice at 274,000. Better luck next time.

At first, it wasn’t clear whether the affair was with his wife’s sister or his brother’s wife, and social media — as well as our little newsletter team — broke into an intense debate over which was worse.

To help parse this moral minefield, we consulted Kwame Anthony Appiah, a philosophy professor who for more than a decade has written the Ethicist column for The New York Times Magazine.

If you sleep with your sibling’s spouse, Anthony pointed out, you’ve not only set off a bomb in your marriage, but also in what he called “your natal family, the people you’re connected to by blood.” Other siblings, parents, nieces and nephews could be collateral damage. You’ve betrayed the two people you’re supposed to be most loyal to. “It’s not just adultery,” he noted, “it’s violating the family relationship you’ve had since birth.”

If you cheat with your spouse’s sibling, it might be easier on your family. But you’re doing all that extra harm to her and her family. As Anthony put it, “You’re denying her the person it would be most natural for her to go to to seek solace.” And if it’s worse for your betrayed spouse, he said, it’s worse overall.

“In thinking about morality, we often make a sharp distinction between harming yourself and harming other people,” he continued. “Since you shouldn’t be doing it at all, what you should be focused on is the harm you’re doing to the other person.”

This week’s subject for The Interview is the wellness influencer Jay Shetty, who went from being a monk to being a wildly successful self-help celebrity with a goal to “make wisdom go viral.”

One of the things that’s unusual about your arc is that it looks like an inversion of a typical monk’s journey. In the typical version, somebody decides to embrace monastic life and then renounces material things. It seems as if you decided to pursue monastic life, and now you’re doing pretty well for yourself financially. You hang out with glamorous people. You’re a successful entrepreneur. Are there any ways in which the spiritual tradition you trained in is in tension with the life you’re living?

There’s a beautiful statement in the Bhagavad Gita that says attachment and aversion are two sides of the same coin. Often in our Western understanding, we see detachment as better than attachment. However, the spiritual understanding is far more refined. Detachment doesn’t mean aversion. Detachment means you can be close to anything in the world and use it for a higher purpose. Now, I’m not saying I’m doing that. I’m saying I’m trying my best. Every day I’m living in the quote-unquote real world, I’m reminded of my flaws. And I would argue that I feel closer to growth in my current life than I ever did in the ashram, because in the ashram I could almost forget or think maybe I’d already found it.

Is there any part of you that thinks that’s an elaborate self-justification?

I have questioned that many times. I think the spiritual philosophy of 5,000 years is pretty clear, so I take that as my authority. However, the other side of it, to be quite frank and honest, is I think it’s also a graduation. I’m married, I have businesses, we have teams, we have companies. I’m not a monk anymore. ✏️ Here comes the scramble for refunds. The Supreme Court resolved one question about President Trump’s tariffs by ruling them illegal. But it left U.S. business leaders awash <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhuhil-hrkusddg-h%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cf0f032ab5f9c49a0de2208de720c080b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639073593174485852%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=BT5iOFJmUZMi0PgLEi0bId24XNCdRQ9FfTyuErMIkf8%3D&reserved=0>  in a flood of others: Are tariff refunds any closer to reality? Could new tariffs prove costlier? Is there a way to proceed without angering the Trump administration—or customers seeking price breaks? For now, uncertainty reigns.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

Q: What can you do to stop feeling bad about your sleep habits? 


It’s hard enough to snooze at night. Now there’s a new source of worry: Sleep shame–the subtle, and not so subtle, ways that people judge and undermine how and when we rest. Columnist Elizabeth Bernstein wrote about how to fight back <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhuhil-hrkusddg-w%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cf0f032ab5f9c49a0de2208de720c080b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639073593174694719%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=XnzMcZT%2BiqTDpIlCy2BA%2FC8QnrOhdqXLqc99bzF9OoM%3D&reserved=0>  and get a good night’s sleep.

A: Sleep shame is driven by the idea that there’s a one-size-fits-all approach, experts say. Yet we all have different sleep needs, both in terms of amount and timing. Some people are natural early birds, others night owls. Many people, like me, also end up shamed by their sleep trackers. This is where our growing obsession with achieving optimal sleep—an issue that researchers call orthosomnia—becomes harmful. So what’s a sleep-ashamed person to do? Some advice from the experts:

*	Own your needs: How much sleep you need—and the timing—is innate. You’ll feel less ashamed if you remember this.
*	Zoom out on your data: Don’t judge your sleep health based on just one night.
*	Respect your partner’s chronotype: Your partner’s early bedtime when you want to stay up isn’t lazy, selfish or a reflection of their love. It’s a biological need.
*	Push back: Labeling sleep shame can help you address it. This is true even when you are the one beating yourself up.

GitHub Education Newsletter


January 2026

	
🚀 From hands-on hackathons to AI-powered tooling and certification prep, this month’s GitHub Education newsletter highlights building real-world skills that carry beyond the classroom and help you jump start your career.
	
What’s inside?

🤖 Code without Barriers - AI Hackathon

Microsoft’s Code Without Barriers program is hosting a virtual Code with AI Hackathon for female university students across Asia who want to explore AI-powered development in a supportive, beginner-friendly environment. Learn from Microsoft technical architects, get hands-on with GitHub, and collaborate with peers and mentors to build real-world applications—no prior experience required.

🗓 March 6, 2025 (multiple Asia-Pacific time zones) 
📍 Virtual | Free | All skill levels welcome 
👉 Register and learn more on the official event page  
	
	
 <http://cdn.mcauto-images-production.sendgrid.net/cc8ddcf649afa5e0/1f7f7d05-1a2c-4972-b658-497c961404b9/1080x1080.png> 	
🚀 Level Up with GitHub Copilot: A 4-Week Series for the Copilot Curious
New to AI coding or ready to build more ambitious projects? This 4-week Copilot learning series combines short Skills modules, hands-on practice challenges, and community Q&A discussions to help you build confidence using GitHub Copilot in real workflows. Learn alongside other student developers, sharpen your AI-powered coding skills, and earn prizes as you complete weekly challenges.

👉 Start the challenge and join the discussion! 
Start Week 1	 
	
	
 <http://cdn.mcauto-images-production.sendgrid.net/cc8ddcf649afa5e0/0ca21868-329a-4ae1-b509-62c536ff0b71/2208x886.png> 	
💻 Virtual CLI Hackathon with DEV.to

Build where developers live: the terminal. The GitHub Copilot CLI Challenge invites you to explore AI-powered coding directly from your command line using GitHub Copilot CLI. Running through February 15, this virtual hackathon is your chance to experiment, build, and learn by turning natural language prompts into real code, workflows, and ideas.

Whether you’re creating productivity tools, fun experiments, or solving everyday problems, this challenge is all about discovering what’s possible when AI meets the CLI. Submit a project to earn a completion badge on your DEV profile—and compete for prizes including $1,000 USD, GitHub Universe 2026 tickets, and GitHub Copilot Pro+ subscriptions.

👉 Join the challenge and start building


 <http://cdn.mcauto-images-production.sendgrid.net/cc8ddcf649afa5e0/356f615b-121e-4d8a-b522-2dfc92448d74/3240x1350.png> 	
👉 Explore Cumbuca Dev and see how open source can be your entry point
🌱 From First PR to Real Experience: Cumbuca Dev

How a Brazilian open source community is helping beginners gain real-world experience — directly on GitHub
Cumbuca Dev is a community-led initiative from Brazil that helps beginners and people from underrepresented groups break into tech by contributing to real open source projects on GitHub. 

Instead of practice exercises, learners work on live repositories—submitting pull requests, reviewing code, improving documentation, and collaborating with maintainers. GitHub becomes the classroom, and mentorship and inclusive practices help turn first contributions into lasting skills.


	
🎓 Campus Expert Alumni Spotlight

GitHub Campus Expert alumnus Rasheed, recently launched TRIGRA, an open source project he built to make Kubernetes deployments simpler and more approachable. Designed as a lightweight GitOps controller, TRIGRA lets developers deploy by pushing configuration to Git—no repetitive manual commands required. Projects like this are a great example of how Campus Experts continue building, experimenting, and contributing to open source long after their time in the program. Dear Blue Devils,

Happy chilly, chilly couple of days! From a snow-day to some grace on K-Ville, we hope everyone is staying warm these next few weeks. Below we have some cool on campus events and updates, and definitely some upcoming heat! 

If you have questions or concerns, feel free to reach out to DSG at dsg@duke.edu and through our Instagram, @dukestudentgovt!

1. Burn some benches & join a key Duke basketball tradition — LAST CALL!


Want to burn some benches when Duke wins against UNC at MBB and WBB home games? Didn’t manage to get a Black or Blue Tent, but still want to be part of a core Duke tradition? Look no further. Join the A-Team!

The sign-up form is NOW LIVE! Complete the form by 1/31 if you’re interested.

In 1986, Duke University sponsored a bonfire, with no idea that it would evolve into a beloved tradition. Since then, Duke students, collaborating with administrators, have burned benches as a way to commemorate home wins in basketball games. The A-Team is the task force in charge of maintaining this tradition.

Each member of the A-Team gets a jacket and the chance to participate in one of Duke Basketball's most famous traditions. Please note that you must complete training via Zoom.

Reach out to Angela Chen, DSG's Vice President of Campus Life, with any questions: angela.z.chen@duke.edu.

Subject: Register for Race to the Secret Spots (White Tenting)!
Body:
Crazies, 

Having FOMO? There is still another chance to secure your spot in Krzyzewskiville for the 2026 season! Registration for Race to the Secret Spots (R2SS) is now open! The race is scheduled for Monday, February 9th at 9pm. Register HERE! <https://airtable.com/appPNvFhk2q8Omcux/shrfOAwJv4vBcmbdB> 

*	You can register a team of up to 12 participants. For the registration to be valid, you must have at least two members. We suggest having 12 tenters in your group regardless, though! Note: you can freely change your tent roster for the first five days after the start of White Tenting.

	*	To fill out the form, you will need to have the names and netIDs of all tenters in your group. One person should be designated the tent captain. You will also be submitting a tent name on the form (if you get a tenting spot, this can be changed later).

*	Registration will close at 12pm on Sunday, February 8th–the day before the race!
*	Want to tent but don’t have a full group? Use this form <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13CWX_yAByyehF5QnQ6g2RGjh6MGQLPg0grXGJmOCpug/edit?gid=634347005#gid=634347005>  to find additional tent members or a tent group!

Competing in the Race to the Secret Spots is the only way to earn a spot as a White or Flex tent in K-Ville. The top 20 teams will earn a White Tenting spot, and the following 30 teams will earn a Flex Tenting spot in K-Ville.

Created by Peter Steinberger <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGfqaayCeE8uth91chlbmPFIzlSJrnnFRc02S3UDa8w7suAjKcJQ8Gjo0ZduO3q77H3-41IkKM%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C1a40b3202f5b4c8ff97508de5f572541%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639053025068858464%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=iWBqNrcs754FSmaqdywfEwfzqDLxgwTXXJILx5rOHhU%3D&reserved=0> , this personal AI assistant runs around the clock and connects to messaging platforms you already use, including WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, and iMessage.

Why run Moltbot on DigitalOcean?

*	Container-based isolation: Moltbot runs inside a dedicated Docker container, isolating agent execution from the host system. If an agent crashes or misbehaves, only its container is affected, which protects the underlying Droplet, files, and credentials.
*	Authentication by default: Each deployment generates a unique gateway token for authenticated access, ensuring only authorized clients can communicate with the agent. This prevents unauthenticated access and reduces the risk of exposed endpoints.
*	Hardened server configuration: The Droplet is provisioned with firewall rules, non-root execution, and locked-down permissions to reduce attack surface from day one. Background internet noise is automatically mitigated using fail2ban, blocking abusive traffic patterns without manual tuning.
*	Private access controls: Device pairing is enabled by default, ensuring that only explicitly approved users and clients can interact with the agent, which limits the blast radius of unintended commands.
*	Flexible model support: Developers can use DigitalOcean Gradient® AI models directly, connect to open-source models or third-party providers while maintaining full control over runtime behavior, data flow, and configuration. Today, Anthropic is supported with more to follow.

Ready to get started? Deploy Moltbot in minutes

 

1.	Deploy your Droplet - Select the Moltbot 1-Click App image from the DigitalOcean Marketplace <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGfqaayCZSwMkWvLUbtzQLn9EF84b429ssbswY2NJOncX2VFyHRhgAxjdoBUmYA79vU6sHHC5k%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C1a40b3202f5b4c8ff97508de5f572541%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639053025068886160%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=x%2BqrhLFqFlxkeGHJd8yG8MsLp7UFLl3xoyOpjn%2FGlug%3D&reserved=0> 
2.	Under Authentication, select your desired SSH Key or add an SSH key <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGfqaayCZLltsHe9NRvBb8IZw3R0q1zpcUSxGy_7GUDpZlQ6sbx3_Sv1fRG-0cz3LpSZROzP3o%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C1a40b3202f5b4c8ff97508de5f572541%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639053025068899877%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=foq1l5CxlQlovFxbUi2DX9VE7nxAZBgAB6bMvWi14y0%3D&reserved=0> 
3.	Open your CLI of choice and run ssh root@your-droplet-ip, using the IP provided for your droplet in the cloud console. Note that droplets may take a few minutes to fully configure so you might need to try this a couple of times.
4.	Once connected, you’ll be shown the Moltbot welcome message. Take note of the Dashboard URL as this is what you will copy and paste into your browser to access the dashboard. Similarly, you can run /opt/clawdbot-tui.sh to access the Clawdbot TUI in your CLI.
5.	To finish configuration, you’ll be prompted to choose your AI provider. Within the terminal, choose Anthropic as your AI Provider. If you have access to Gradient AI, you can select that option.  models will be available soon. Once you select your provider, provide the respective API/Secret key.
6.	After you setup your AI provider, Clawdbot will automatically restart with your new configured Moltbot. You can also run systemctl restart Moltbot at any time to restart your session.

A Wall of Money

 

The stock market behaves a lot like a toddler: a short attention span, active imagination and some irrational fears.

 

It’s also prone to the occasional sugar high. The coming months will see multiple streams of stimulus boost American household and corporate finances all at once—the economic equivalent of Halloween and a visit to Grandma’s house combined. 

 

None of that guarantees the S&P 500 will keep breaking records <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43807815.471327%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2UvZmVkLWludGVyZXN0LXJhdGUtZGVjaXNpb24tMDEtMjgtMjAyNi9jYXJkL3MtcC01MDAtY3Jvc3Nlcy03MDAwLWZvci1maXJzdC10aW1lLUNQTWQwVVJGQ2puV1BjakJiMEJTP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB2ac43ab9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe9f85f4163542e1209408de5f2c4c53%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052841042414565%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=1KL2HJFVioRWlW3hsK4qWgMf992pOa8lxCOrRH3QxvU%3D&reserved=0> , but it sure helps for now. An obvious boost comes from taxes via last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. A lot of household cash flows are front-loaded to early 2026. Personal income tax cuts were retroactive, but few paychecks got adjusted. 

 

Withholding will be lower and refunds higher. Greg Ip, the Journal’s chief economics commentator, writes that the combo could boost annualized economic growth <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43807815.471327%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9lY29ub215L3RydW1wLXdhbnRzLXRvLXJ1bi10aGUtZWNvbm9teS1ob3QtdGhlcmVzLWEtZ29vZC1jaGFuY2UtaGVsbC1zdWNjZWVkLTg1MjQ0ZjIzP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBece11999&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe9f85f4163542e1209408de5f2c4c53%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052841042478202%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rUEwwzeN9BIUjp90SYqxzOoG5D6iZmQVGuj25Lk4uJ0%3D&reserved=0>  in the first half of the year by as much as half a percentage point.

 

Meanwhile, companies are taking advantage of bonus depreciation rules that allow them to get an immediate tax benefit from short-lived investments like machinery. We’re already in the middle of an epic investment wave related to AI. Statements from hyperscalers Meta <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43807815.471327%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9idXNpbmVzcy9lYXJuaW5ncy9tZXRhLW1ldGEtcTQtZWFybmluZ3MtcmVwb3J0LTIwMjUtNDZiNTlkOTA_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB9ec4a8fa&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe9f85f4163542e1209408de5f2c4c53%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052841042512423%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=o3VF2Xiz3VAoc5UZ7w4gYj%2BQYiMAy67lxYdQFTt6OfM%3D&reserved=0>  and Microsoft <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43807815.471327%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS90ZWNoL2FpL21pY3Jvc29mdHMtZWFybmluZ3Mtc3VyZ2UtZWxldmF0ZWQtYnktY2xvdWQtYnVzaW5lc3MtMjUxODI5YzI_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBd9728f25&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe9f85f4163542e1209408de5f2c4c53%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052841042534400%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=TepKfhmpQAR1YW30yPaQavYzl0GGaRg6mgzD51JD7qg%3D&reserved=0>  late Wednesday gave no hint of caution.

 

Carson Group estimates that hyperscalers’ capital expenditures last year were 1.3% of gross domestic product—more than four times the proportion this spending accounted for in 2019. They forecast it reaching half a trillion dollars or 1.6% of GDP in 2026.

 

But isn’t spending lots of money a drag too? Right now, it’s simultaneously boosting the S&P 500’s overall revenue and profit.

 

Corporate results don’t work like your household budget: If company A spends a lot of money on chips and servers, then that capital expenditure only affects reported earnings over many years, even if it’s immediately expensed for tax purposes. But the sellers of those chips and servers at companies B, C and D report the revenue and profit right away.

 

And then there’s monetary stimulus. The Federal Reserve stood pat Wednesday, but it already has cut rates six times during this cycle. That 1.75-percentage-point reduction is still working its way through the economy. Real rates—adjusted for inflation—are already lower than their historical average during economic expansions.

 

What comes after the wall of money? One scenario is something like 2022 when Covid-era stimulus sparked uncomfortably high inflation and a bear market. Sometimes stocks need a good, long nap.

Second thoughts?


The federal government’s response to the killing of Alex Pretti has come in two phases. First there were the justifications. Then came the recriminations.

His usual strategy of blustering his way through a crisis — or creating diversions — could not overcome the optics of a second American dead at the hands of federal agents during the same operation.

The government had said Pretti attacked the federal agents, that he was an “assassin,” a “terrorist.” But videos directly contradict this idea, and Trump could see it plain. “Nobody understands TV better than him,” Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina told The Times. The videos led to a change in Trump’s approach.

He sent Tom Homan, his border czar, to Minneapolis and ordered Gregory Bovino, the aggressive Border Patrol official who was directing operations there, to leave. (“Bovino is pretty good, but he’s a pretty out-there kind of guy,” Trump told Fox News. “Maybe it wasn’t good here.”) He softened his language about the shooting and spoke with Minnesota’s governor, Tim Walz, whom he had falsely accused of inciting violent protests.

He described new bills put forward in Colorado, Delaware and California to hamper the administration’s deportation efforts. The measures would let people sue federal agents for civil rights violations, for instance, or prevent commercial airlines from getting tax exemptions on the jet fuel they use to transport migrants detained by ICE without warrants and due process.

A bill in Washington State would keep federal agents out of day care centers, hospitals and election sites without a warrant or a court order. And in Maryland, David reports, one lawmaker wants to bar ICE agents recruited by the Trump administration from working at any of the state’s law enforcement agencies.

“We are starting to see legislators who, last session, were afraid of being a thorn in the side of an ascendant Trump administration — they were so afraid of poking the bear,” an immigration policy advocate for the American Civil Liberties Union said. “The tide is now turning, and maybe they feel that they’ve got nothing to lose.”

Legislators in states controlled by Republicans, David found, are going in the opposite direction. In South Carolina, a new bill would require county sheriffs to work with ICE. In Tennessee, a proposal would force the government to verify the legal status of residents seeking public assistance and to verify the immigration status of schoolchildren, despite a decades-old Supreme Court ruling that found schools cannot do that.


On the Hill


The unrest in Minneapolis has also emerged as a sticking point in the latest congressional budget battle.

Senate Democrats don’t want to bankroll Trump’s aggressive immigration operations, so they’re threatening a partial shutdown — much of the government runs out of money early Saturday morning — unless Republicans agree to significant changes at the Department of Homeland Security.

They want to regulate the behavior of the agency’s officers. And they want to add restrictions to the no-strings-attached slush fund the Republican Congress delivered to ICE last year, which made it the highest-funded federal law enforcement agency. Democrats at the time warned that the money — $75 billion — would mean growth for the agency, and no checks on its processes.

The Democrats can’t act on any of it alone, though, as my colleague Michael Gold reported. Any changes to the spending measure that keeps the government open would require the cooperation of enough Republicans to allow it to pass.


Moving forward


Although some members of the Trump administration and the political coalition behind it may have second thoughts about the tactics in Minneapolis, the overall strategy there is not in doubt. Pam Bondi, the attorney general, announced yesterday afternoon that she was “on the ground in Minneapolis” and said that federal agents had arrested 16 “rioters” who had been “resisting and impeding our federal law enforcement agents.”

The president was also quick to dismiss the attack on Ilhan Omar, the Muslim American member of Congress from Minnesota, after someone attacked her with a brownish liquid smelling of vinegar at a town-hall event on Tuesday night. Trump, who for years has bashed Omar, a Democrat, said she should be deported and backed a baseless conspiracy theory that she had married her brother to commit immigration fraud. ✏️ After the shooting of Alex Pretti in Minneapolis, President Trump’s advisers followed their boss’s playbook for moments of crisis <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-giuulld-hrkusddg-i%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce5190cc30d56489fc6ce08de5f285d9b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052824135612970%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=wzmqpwOmx8uu0C6jmPS31r9vL4vMU6RskyJP19g5pJQ%3D&reserved=0> : Cede no ground, never admit mistakes and attack. But this time the strategy backfired. Now, the president and his aides are rushing to limit the political damage, pointing fingers and shifting their strategy as they go. The killing has shaken the nation—and provoked a clash in the White House over the future of Trump’s immigration policy. And for Gregory Bovino, the operation that was supposed to be his biggest yet <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-giuulld-hrkusddg-d%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce5190cc30d56489fc6ce08de5f285d9b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052824135632101%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=TAgFEhLCJHJE0AkElvzzrNk%2FScFkfvMmaFCd8gqnesU%3D&reserved=0>  led to his dramatic fall.

Trump’s border chief was a rising star. Then he arrived in Minneapolis. 


For six months, Gregory Bovino was the face of rolling immigration raids that netted thousands of arrests. His Minnesota campaign, “Operation Metro Surge,” was supposed to be his most ambitious mission <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-giuulld-hrkusddg-m%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce5190cc30d56489fc6ce08de5f285d9b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052824135776667%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Ef4WTk6mSC4O1KGPJ8fol2ion5QJLKLVuMIaBxwxXa4%3D&reserved=0>  yet. Instead, it descended into scenes of tear gas, pepper spray and civil unrest. Less than 48 hours after referring to border agents who killed Pretti as “victims,” Bovino was pulled from the field. Q: Why is the dollar sliding? 


The currency’s drop has renewed fears <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-giuulld-hrkusddg-s%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce5190cc30d56489fc6ce08de5f285d9b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052824135867520%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=7TrtdFm%2FnA07zNEQHpqxp9qHCwF4gFu2dlNolKILed8%3D&reserved=0>  that America’s pre-eminent position in global markets is waning, write David Uberti and Chelsey Dulaney.

A: The dollar’s strength over the past decade was propelled in large part by “American exceptionalism,” or the outperformance of the U.S. economy and markets compared with the rest of the world. Political stability and strong rule of law gave overseas investors extra reason to snap up U.S. assets.

Both sources of support are weakening somewhat.

While economists have dialed up U.S. growth projections, stimulative economic policies in Japan, Germany and elsewhere have helped overseas stock markets in recent months outperform their counterparts stateside. At the same time, even after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady yesterday, many on Wall Street expect the central bank to resume easing policy in 2026, as Trump has advocated.

More cuts could narrow the premium that U.S. Treasury yields offer relative to government debt in other countries, drawing investors elsewhere to help shield themselves from the risk of owning U.S. assets like stocks.

That is why much of Wall Street is betting on more dollar weakness to come, potentially ending a yearslong run in which the currency enticed investors the world over to park more money in America.

 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fimbwbt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fuzdku9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C13a7e93f29464155b72508de5f2712bc%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052818599886854%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=4akNYz1X2GW6HAWP1nRCFUmo4EKizUtIFCMy3%2FdUDRA%3D&reserved=0>

 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fimbwbt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fqkfku9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C13a7e93f29464155b72508de5f2712bc%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052818599931518%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=zL%2BEVEqwuWkJiBhqb8qljCqce3%2FL%2Fha0XqtckA2WNQQ%3D&reserved=0>

Web Scraping is Complex. We make it Simple.


Why are some domains difficult to scrape?


In yesterday's email, we explained how you can proactively improve the success of your requests by adding specific parameters. 

But why do you need to do all of that, and why do we need to unblock certain domains? 🤔 


Web scraping challenges


Client-side Rendering 
This is the most common roadblock when scraping JS-heavy websites. Because AJAX calls or JavaScript are executed at runtime, it makes it impossible for regular scrapers to extract the necessary data.

CAPTCHAs 
By redirecting the request to a page with a CAPTCHA, the server creates a challenge our web scraper needs to solve to prove it’s human. 

Browser Behavior Profiling 
Because servers can measure how a client interacts with the site, anti-bot mechanisms can spot patterns like the number and interval of clicks. 

Honeypots 
Honeypots are link traps added to the HTML file that are hidden for humans but can be accessed by web crawlers. When a web scraper accesses the link, the server can determine it is a robot and blacklist the client over time.

Anti-scraping Techniques
A simple example of an anti-scraping method is analyzing the number of requests from the client. If a client makes too many requests within a particular time frame or too many parallel requests from the same IP, the server will blacklist the client.

Hello Graham Mills,

Thank you for your interest in the 2027 Summer Internship, Early Careers – Investment Banking - CA R-512565 at Wells Fargo.

On-Demand Video Interview

Position: 2027 Summer Internship, Early Careers – Investment Banking - CA

You will have until 2/2/2026 8:16 PM Central Time (US & Canada) to submit
	




The next step in the process is to complete a video interview that is quick, easy, and can be done on your own time. To do this, you will need to use a computer, smart phone, or any other camera-enabled device, and a distraction free environment. Completing this step is required to be considered for this position.

You will have until 2/2/2026 8:16 PM Central Time (US & Canada) to submit your video interview. 

After this time, the link will expire, so we recommend you submit your responses today.

We are excited to learn more about you and your qualifications for this position. Please allow yourself approximately 30 minutes to answer the questions presented and to submit your recorded video interview responses.

If you are a candidate or you are assisting someone with that requires accessibility assistance or an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please click this link for instructions on how to submit an accommodation request. <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wellsfargojobs.com%2Fen%2Finclusion%2Fdisability%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8b3e82c71e814db82e8c08de5edc65a3%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052497870375765%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0Z2lXsSsp7SxnusdaYsRNdW62GT3y9hJqP9gosXp0lc%3D&reserved=0> 

DIRECTIONS

1.	Set aside approximately 30 minutes in a distraction free environment to complete your video interview. Although you will be able to complete the interview over more than one sitting, and you will be provided the opportunity to re-record a response, if necessary, your best responses typically result from a single sitting where you can fully focus your attention on your interview.
	
	
2.	Questions will be presented as written text, with one question appearing at a time. Each interview question will remain on the screen while you record your response, so it is not necessary memorize or write down the interview question. A countdown timer will also be present on the screen during your response recording.
	
	
3.	You will be provided a practice or warm-up question, that will not be considered in the hiring decision. Use this question to check your camera settings, voice quality, and to familiarize yourself with the video interview process.
	
	
4.	Click BEGIN to access the Wells Fargo foyer, which is the landing page. To sufficiently prepare yourself, watch the videos and review the additional resources. Please follow the instructions carefully and review each question in full prior to recording your response.
	
	
5.	Ensure your answers are complete, detailed, and include all information requested in each question (e.g., your position or situation, task, your specific actions or contributions, outcome, any results of your actions or contributions, etc.).
	
	
6.	Upon completion, you will have the opportunity to review your response and will be allowed to re-record each response, if necessary. It is important that you replay your responses to ensure your voice can be heard clearly. Once you have submitted your final video responses, you will be unable to view or modify them.
	
	
7.	Once you submit your interview, a notification will be sent to the hiring team at Wells Fargo for review. We will contact you if there is a match between your background and our needs.
