Sophomores: please see the information below about 2027 Summer Analyst internships with Alvarez and Marsal in Atlanta. Note the resume drop deadline is Jan 31.

 

From A&M:

 

In our practice, we advise management teams and boards of underperforming or financially distressed companies, combining elements from consulting, investment banking, and corporate finance. It’s hands‑on, analytical work with real‑world impact such as:

 

*	Build and manage 13‑week cash flow and help with liquidity and waterfall analyses
*	Support company business plans, KPI tracking, and stakeholder materials
*	Work cross‑functionally with attorneys, bankers, and A&M teams on time‑sensitive engagements

 

This is a great role for students who enjoy rigorous problem‑solving, are comfortable in Excel/finance/accounting, and like working on fast‑moving, outcome‑oriented projects.

 

Here’s a link to the posting: https://app.joinhandshake.com/emp/jobs/10368596 <https://app.joinhandshake.com/emp/jobs/10368596> 

 

For students who want to learn more about our work, here’s a short overview of A&M North America Restructuring: https://www.alvarezandmarsal.com/expertise/north-america-restructuring <https://www.alvarezandmarsal.com/expertise/north-america-restructuring> .

Tips & Tricks for a Successful Video Interview

DO your homework, you have a limited amount of time to convey your knowledge, research current deals and initiatives ahead of time
DO treat this like an in-person interview, dress in business attire
DO set up a tidy and quiet space to conduct the interview. While you are being evaluated on what you say keep in mind the reviewers can view your background

DON'T use any examples in your answers that involve any illegal or illicit topics
DON'T share the interview questions with friends or classmates, we want everyone to have an even playing field while completing

Subject: Update on your 2026-2027 Residence Life Application
Body:
Dear Graham Mills,

It is with great pleasure that we offer you the Resident Assistant (RA) position in Residence Life at Duke University for the 26-27 academic year! CONGRATULATIONS! We truly hope that you will consider joining us on the Residence Life team.  

﻿ 

RA Position Information 
Community: Blackwell/Randolph

2026-27 Stipend rate (per year): $1375
RA Meal Allotment (per semester): $1750 + 15 Marketplace Swipes

 

Please note that this offer is conditional upon your continued positive academic and conduct record.

Prior to making your final acceptance decision, please review the following: 

﻿

Placement Information 

While it is highly unlikely, your placement may change based on community needs. Your specific building and room assignment will be provided to you at a later date.

﻿

We will not accept any requests for placement changes for specific campuses or buildings.

﻿

Choosing to decline the RA position due to placement will remove you from further consideration for the RA position for the 2026-2027 year. 

 

If you have an SDAO accommodation requiring a specific placement, please indicate this on the form when you accept the role. Residence Life is not required to alter an RA’s positional assignment based on an SDAO accommodation. However, we will take them into consideration when determining final placement.  

﻿ 

Financial Information 

﻿

The stipend award will be paid to you in four non-compensatory checks at the end of September, November, February, and May. This award will be reported as earned income to the IRS on a 1099 form as required by federal regulation.  

 

The compensation and remuneration for the RA position affect students and their financial aid packages differently. Please contact your financial aid officer to determine if/how your financial aid package may be impacted by taking the RA position. 

﻿

As a part of Duke’s Sustainability Initiative, you must sign up for direct deposit to receive your stipend. 

﻿ 

Spring Orientation and Training 

We will be hosting a Spring Orientation and Training day on Saturday, April 18th, 2026. During this time, we will review important role documentation, you will meet your team for next year, and you will get prepared to arrive ready to go in the fall.

﻿

Fall Training and Arrival 

RAs will be required to move into their assigned community no later than Monday, August 10th, at 10am, with training and opening tasks beginning at noon that day and continuing through August 24th. You will be expected to make arrangements with summer internships, employment, or family obligations to ensure that you are here by and during the above dates. Please review the Leave and Return Date document in the link below for more specifics.

﻿

 

Please CLICK HERE <https://duke.is/RLStudentStaffDatabase>  to review additional documentation and notify us of your decision to accept or decline the RA position for the 26-27 academic year by Monday, February at 12pm (noon). If you have any questions or concerns with the offer or the deadline, please let us know ASAP at RLSelections@duke.edu <mailto:RLSelections@duke.edu> . If we do not hear from you by the above deadline, we will assume that you are no longer interested in the RA role and remove you from consideration. 

﻿ 

We are truly excited to have you on the Residence Life team! RAs are a key part of the QuadEx Residential Experience.

﻿ 

Sincerely,   

﻿ 

The Recruitment and Selection Team   

Residence Life, Duke University

Subject: APPLY NOW to BECOME AN EHS RA for SUMMER 2026!
Body:
<https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cognitoforms.com%2FEHS1%2FEHSResidentAdvisorApplication&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cf4932b974b1045c1262508de5e7e8dd9%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052094855405835%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=NWt2jzE3GRNa8ED3FQKrF2mdFCQG2cYnEZ3fkE%2BLRwU%3D&reserved=0> Dear Graham,

EHS is looking for Resident Advisor’s to work for the Summer 2026 Term! A Resident Advisor is a paraprofessional staff member who is enrolled in a higher education institution, maintains a GPA of at least 2.80, and is in good judicial and financial standing with both their institution and Educational Housing Services! 

Being a Resident Advisor is a challenging position that requires energy, commitment, and dedication! You’ll add new skills (or refine old ones) to your resume which transcend the RA position into your career path. As an EHS RA, you’ll develop leadership, communication, and crisis management skills; just to name a few!  

________________________________


Our Process is Simple:


*	Complete an EHS RA Application <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cognitoforms.com%2FEHS1%2FEHSResidentAdvisorApplication&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cf4932b974b1045c1262508de5e7e8dd9%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052094855436113%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=xhzkCuDizDWcS0Cx%2BkKD90EqgCP92J4XPhgDf4vR3jY%3D&reserved=0>  and submit all requirments by Friday, February 6, 2026 by 5:00 PM.
*	Attend the mandatory Group Process Day on Saturday, February 28, 2026.
*	If selected, attend the mandatory Interview Day on Sunday, March 1, 2026 (invite will be sent via email by 9pm on Saturday, February 28th).
*	Check for the status notification email results the week of March 23rd.
*	Mandatory RA Training (hired RAs) Saturday and Sunday, May 2nd and 3rd.
*	If hired, employment term agreement dates are May 1st - August  15th.

________________________________


Have questions? Attend an Informational Q&A Session <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.studenthousing.org%2Fstudent-life%2Fresident-advisors%2Finfosessions%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cf4932b974b1045c1262508de5e7e8dd9%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052094855450358%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=UDY8NCzSHrEf0MsDzjVnXV5e03YkfuuWrByZEMV0rtw%3D&reserved=0>  at either the St. George Towers, New Yorker, Hudson Yards Residence on:


*	Wednesday, January 28th at 7:00 PM

For more information about our application process, Click Here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.studenthousing.org%2Fstudent-life%2Fresident-advisors%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cf4932b974b1045c1262508de5e7e8dd9%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639052094855464640%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=HxAW6JH6Dw1pFixRgTZkv%2FQyf9oLJtQ%2BellygBsU3ow%3D&reserved=0> . Welcome to Spain


After a military coup in his native Mali in 2022, Sady Traoré said he fled the country for the Canary Islands, a Spanish archipelago off the coast of West Africa. Now 28, he works in the citrus groves of eastern Spain. He hasn’t been able to secure an appointment to apply for Spanish asylum.

Traoré, and hundreds of thousands of other undocumented workers in Spain, got good news yesterday. The Spanish government will give many of them a way to apply for renewable residency permits.

It will turn its illegal immigrants into legal ones <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2FN23ODdbszn4COwpgZTw_Fw~~%2FAAAAARA~%2Fmbq1q10rNCbeEkgfofke8neS4p1wBN3k0wZkCKpBPAqyQqR1qPR5k4_T4HBkG7ar8ixpqusD4RaSqG-uxTChtYGukX57LnLxnxOOWIDK9fCiNpsCojUJBr95jeiCY-5QzBNQqSV-TaftkF6bAyicyl-J66BZqVMF_cZ33e4IvEEjjWajVxmCdACnO3anyQ_VvlgGj-1oDambAm-tUnD831VuTPsMC7pynbQTQ0SEQepoSm30KFBY4p7NtN9GFpXzTlqNhIgQmtN0V-ftnWmvT6CPYs-zAqIWdx0uUeqSMZ6U6UY8DXP4wLSHtGncObFiTI9XnQY5mF0S1mDFq6wYrm76zLSKAoa6cD-Jy0u2fHnKDFF2uKjyx_m2B81MvUkN7hHHK634DYmaMTysem2Hdg~~&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C290978c8456348fdd6ab08de5e630e6d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051976744302158%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=gsM1oaMTZS4KDqliMNnTU5ZV0ASCL8JtJWeHCNgTG%2BA%3D&reserved=0> .

“It brings me closer to my dream, and the dream of many others like me,” Traoré told our reporter, José Bautista.

The government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, a Socialist, described the measure as critical to Spain’s economic future. Migrant labor plays a large part in the country’s economy. Spain’s minister for migration said it would have an impact “on our social cohesion, well-being, and also on the economy.”

Spain’s opposition leaders largely disagreed. Vox, a far-right party, said it would take the government to court over the decision. Its leader said Sánchez was “accelerating an invasion.”


An outlier


Spain’s decision is at odds with the posture toward immigration taken by many Western governments, with widespread public support. Britain recently tightened its rules surrounding refugees. Italy declared that it wanted to detain asylum seekers in Albania while it reviewed their claims. Greece jails those who remain in the country after it rejects their claims.

And in the United States, Trump has vowed to arrest and deport millions of illegal immigrants, ordering a crackdown in order to do so. Illegal crossings at the border have almost stopped, but enforcement elsewhere has led to fatal violence, strife and protests in those places, most notably Minneapolis.

“In the current international context, marked by the rise of anti-migration discourse, Spain’s decision represents a counterweight,” a migration researcher at Pontifical University of Comillas in Madrid told The Times.


How it happened


Spain has legalized waves of undocumented people before, and tried to present itself as a beacon for immigrants. There have been eight campaigns to do so in the country since the mid-1980s, and they’ve rolled out under both progressive and conservative governments. They helped keep Spain’s population from shrinking — the way other European countries have. At least a million migrants benefited, too.

Then came the coronavirus pandemic, when lockdowns in Spain laid bare the importance of migrant labor. A 2021 petition to revive the immigration debate, signed by more than 700,000 Spaniards, went nowhere.

Until Monday, when Sánchez’s government brokered a deal with Unidas Podemos, a smaller left-wing party, in exchange for the support of the Socialists in Parliament.

Traoré, the worker in the citrus grove, told José what that meant for him. The measure provides a chance, he said, “to live in peace and work with dignity to support our families.”

What is the meaning of this image? Evan Gorelick, one of our writers here on The Morning, can tell you:

Last week, I called the Department of Homeland Security to ask about an ICE recruitment ad that said, “WE’LL HAVE OUR HOME AGAIN.” That’s also the name of a song embraced by some white supremacists. I was reporting a story about government accounts that have pointed to neo-Nazi literature, ethnic cleansing and QAnon conspiracies.

A spokeswoman, Tricia McLaughlin, told me that it would be “morally repugnant” if the Homeland Security post were quoting the white-supremacist anthem. But, she said, it was unrelated: “There are plenty of references to those words in books and poems.”

Yet when I opened the post on Instagram, it played audio from the song’s chorus. When I pointed this out, McLaughlin said I was participating in a left-wing conspiracy theory and “mainstreaming racism” by drawing a false connection.

Less than 40 minutes later, the post had been erased.

To some people, these messages sound patriotic. But those well-versed in the language of right-wing extremism hear klaxons. “Morning, boys. How’s the water?”

 

David Foster Wallace told the story <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9hcnRpY2xlcy9TQjEyMjE3ODIxMTk2NjQ1NDYwNz9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB5c80930c&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889107192%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=5AavL25RF%2BhMWjc3RnocRbL0IyBiGZMMQbTfZDeymcY%3D&reserved=0>  of an old fish asking two young ones that question as they swam by. Later on, one of them asks the other: “What the hell is water?”

 

The late author’s message held lessons about life, but we’ll hijack it for one about financial markets. Americans live their lives surrounded by something they never have to think about—the world’s reserve currency. 

 

Homeowners can take out mortgages that foreigners envy, U.S. companies raise money easily and the federal government can run massive deficits <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9lY29ub215L2ZlZGVyYWwtYnVkZ2V0LWZpc2NhbC0yMDI1LWU4ZDIxNTk1P21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB22d18367&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889123208%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=ii3o91jsjhn5Ky4eOiyfUqvnfXu%2FYto3R%2Bg%2FFPx5OS8%3D&reserved=0>  year after year.  Almost 60 years ago a miffed French politician dubbed the dollar system an “exorbitant privilege.”

 

Is America pushing its luck? 

 

Attacks on Federal Reserve independence, yo-yo tariffs and unpredictable foreign policy had already pushed the greenback close to a multiyear low. It tumbled further Tuesday after President Trump, asked if the dollar had fallen too much recently, said, “No, I think it’s great. <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL2N1cnJlbmNpZXMvZG9sbGFyLWV4dGVuZHMtc2xpZGUtYWZ0ZXItdHJ1bXAtc2F5cy1oZXMtbm90LXdvcnJpZWQtYWJvdXQtZGVjbGluZXMtYzk4NDkzYmI_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBd7436f55&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889149946%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=VPbYZ7lsOG%2Bj3SPIWqxkiFOhiLbn53GMAX4L%2BcXm%2FSs%3D&reserved=0> ”

When a Danish pension fund said last week it would dump <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2Uvc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LXRvZGF5LWRvdy1zcC01MDAtbmFzZGFxLW5ldGZsaXgtMDEtMjAtMjAyNi9jYXJkL2RhbmlzaC1wZW5zaW9uLWZ1bmQtYmFpbHMtb24tdS1zLXRyZWFzdXJ5cy11TlV4dUdyVm1zTVRZN2ZDT0tqMj9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBe75fae75&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889179749%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=chp8Gto%2BlJaoJ9sXPHCPoF%2Fmk7PAyoRG5X8BEvEi620%3D&reserved=0>  its U.S. bond holdings over “poor government finances,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the move “irrelevant.” Denmark is irrelevant too <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2UvZ3JlZW5sYW5kLXRydW1wLXRhcmlmZnMtdHJhZGUtZXUvY2FyZC9kZW5tYXJrLWlzLWlycmVsZXZhbnQtc2F5cy1iZXNzZW50LW1GVG1NNVlyM0EwWXJwQWdOdUEyP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBd8d5d319&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889199981%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2BZMPC9D2Rn53jrIiaieSxvUNXZRiwgmsJ391L3PdaiM%3D&reserved=0> , he added.

 

Clearly the Danes were miffed over the Greenland mini-crisis. Yet they aren’t the only investors getting worried: Both bonds and the dollar sold off in an echo of last year’s “Liberation Day” episode.

 

Along with stocks, they rebounded last week after President Trump pivoted <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9wb2xpdGljcy9uYXRpb25hbC1zZWN1cml0eS9hLXBpZWNlLW9mLWljZS1mb3Itd29ybGQtcHJvdGVjdGlvbi10cnVtcC1kZW1hbmRzLWV1cm9wZS1jdXQtZGVhbC1vbi1ncmVlbmxhbmQtY2MxMDE0ZjY_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB92cc26a3&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889222017%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=FOi3XOWeRSjtOqlX7ebofDwD9lXaRU7W%2F4sfr%2FSXq4M%3D&reserved=0> , similarly to last year’s “Liberation Day” reversal. Foreigners are probably a lot less relaxed about that than Americans, though. T.S. Lombard strategist Dario Perkins points out that a haven currency and bond market by definition shouldn’t have behaved that way during a crisis. 

 

A U.S. investor or consumer could be forgiven for barely feeling ripples on the surface of the global financial order recently. Inflation is a bit high and foreign trips a tad pricier, but stocks seem pretty relaxed. Bond yields are even a touch lower than this time last year.

 

Yet foreigners who park so much of their savings and official reserves in American assets have earned less on U.S. stocks translated into their own currencies and have lost money on Treasury debt. 

 

More significantly, doubt is creeping in about how long America’s markets will remain exceptional <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43780880.461420%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL2ludmVzdGluZy91cy1zdG9ja3MtZmluYW5jaWFsLW1hcmtldC1nbG9iYWwtaW1wYWN0LTZlZDY0NmI5P21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB96392680&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbe08f64bcabe493e22c608de5e62a239%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051974889244081%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=VvegUtsYGn07rStgQ51J4e4GJsFbmNVDwDlgHmnlH7U%3D&reserved=0> —stocks that trade at a premium and bonds that stay buoyant despite no end in sight to government red ink. 

 

Currencies like the yen, euro or yuan aren’t ready for prime time. But the dollar’s privilege will inevitably erode, exposing Americans’ portfolios and household budgets to global economic tides.

 

That era is starting to feel a bit closer.

A Sirius Oversight

 

Berkshire Hathaway’s third-largest U.S. public stock holding by percentage of shares owned is Kraft Heinz. A Markets A.M. Newsletter last week said it was the conglomerate’s second-largest by that measure. It’s actually Sirius XM.

Q: What happens when you stop taking Ozempic or Wegovy? 


Popular weight-loss drugs are meant to be lifelong treatments for chronic diseases, not lifestyle fixes. Health columnist Sumathi Reddy breaks down the benefits and risks <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-giutig-hrkusddg-e%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C1f43d192d6124e765e3408de5e61def8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051971642068664%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=K9Mf5nShUPRq6oF8BqL4%2B6iJi4ftsJKEVacV5xKg2ow%3D&reserved=0>  of taking a GLP-1 short term.

A: While nearly 18% of U.S. adults have taken a GLP-1 for weight loss or to treat a chronic condition, about half of people will stop taking it within a year. Often, they don’t understand what is likely to come next.

Studies show that after stopping the drugs, people typically regain lost weight within about 1.5 years. Any improvements in blood sugar, blood pressure or cholesterol are reversed.

People who take GLP-1s regain weight four times faster than those who lose weight through lifestyle interventions, according to an analysis published in the British Medical Journal.

Doctors largely say the drugs are worth starting even if you can’t stay on them long term, but caution the need for proper counseling and lifestyle changes.

The greatest success stories come from combining lifestyle changes with obesity medications, says Dr. Gitanjali Srivastava, medical director of obesity medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

Dr. Robert Kushner, an obesity-medicine specialist, recommends GLP-1 users consider a long-term strategy that could involve transitioning to a less-expensive, older-generation weight-loss medication or starting a more intensive lifestyle intervention.

Four 20-somethings debuted Boy Throb <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-giutig-hrkusddg-yk%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C1f43d192d6124e765e3408de5e61def8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051971642313776%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=ZVGLkeKjxbqdYGLg3u95i1AXLQYBEDcYwNZz4gqjqo8%3D&reserved=0>  on TikTok in November. “We’re the world’s next biggest boy band,” they proclaimed in one video. There’s one problem: Member Darshan Magdum lives in India. For the band to be complete, he needs a visa. To get it, Boy Throb must convince the government that their act is, in fact, extraordinary.

Machine learning tools are a popular way to increase efficiency and streamline workloads by analyzing data and applying that analysis to achieve a specific goal.

 

Whether that goal is a chatbot capable of interacting seamlessly with users, the ability to accurately forecast sales and revenue, or simply spam and phishing detection in your inbox, machine learning can be applied to an infinite number of use cases.

 

 Curious? Get your feet wet and try out a few of these tools:

*	How to Create an Intelligent Chatbot <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGforPCeWOwHIjrXhX0MTo438qUyG1DxJSysTc7i1QZGD-LQBncfFm0jrzogQe6LFe6jd-z9eo%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C17190c54683a48aaa81408de5e47b37d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051859244709891%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=um%2FNYjpcFEgZok29G%2FZxfH2%2F9IOdvoJiYjKiue5for0%3D&reserved=0> 
	In this tutorial, you will create a chatbot that uses the OpenWeather API to tell the user the current weather in any city, and which is intelligent enough to communicate with the user in natural language.
	
	
*	An Introduction to Computer Vision <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGforPCeZ1-W2rD62SlL0Qrb1NFIO3GLqmTveMBO-wa72xJ-ZLhE6ZtrzCcHNWTl9DXBluQf-0%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C17190c54683a48aaa81408de5e47b37d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051859244747686%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=ec6azPDOWAfWfDVFDb%2FOgdtog5Oilvg60kgmgS3PypI%3D&reserved=0> 
	OpenCV, or Open Source Computer Vision Library, is a powerful library used for image processing and image recognition. In this project, you will create a web app that will allow users to detect circles in an uploaded image.
	
	
*	Introduction to PyTorch: Build a Neural Network to Recognize Handwritten Digits <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGforPCefUwITvPQu_hMEv_cHLvEtyyuuvEPENO2AF_2hoySP5EW7XsKfdQGP0e_Y-vYB132Wg%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C17190c54683a48aaa81408de5e47b37d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051859244767303%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=YP8PAjNzHWBpN6Davmdq%2FYQNNzPa8%2FeicCCr5foGbKQ%3D&reserved=0> 
	In this tutorial, you will build, train, and evaluate deep neural networks in PyTorch, a framework developed by Facebook AI Research for deep learning.
	
	
*	How To Build a Neural Network to Translate Sign Language into English <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGforPCeQmDMwffuOrFiC4tEuprqUYTnOQN-uh1Kr9t1D_0n2R28LIdtOA9wQc3lKDSpvWH9rM%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C17190c54683a48aaa81408de5e47b37d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051859244786643%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Owg83v3CvDq0yWKlUak%2BCUIUWPuEtVg4zfDL7vWBm70%3D&reserved=0> 
	Computer vision is a subfield of computer science that aims to extract a higher-order understanding from images and videos. Hi everyone,




At this point in the cycle, most candidates have done the “right things”: networking, technical prep, and interview practice.




What’s separating outcomes now isn’t effort, but whether people are allocating that effort correctly and covering the full opportunity set in front of them. Here are a few pieces of advice we have:




P.S. 📈 🤝 Since the recruitment cycle started, we’ve processed 500,000+ chat requests! We really appreciate your support.

­	 

1. Don't Miss Any MM or Boutique Apps


Every year, more and more people fall through the cracks and don't get an offer. 

This is not because they didn't network or weren't technically prepared. 

But because they didn't cast a wide net and missed MM and Boutique apps. 




Those roles open quietly, close fast, and rarely get blasted across LinkedIn or club GroupMes. By the time most people hear about them, they’re already gone.




AskStanley’s Application Tracker <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgxhch.r.a.d.sendibm1.com%2Fmk%2Fcl%2Ff%2Fsh%2FSMK1E8tHeG13G9XaenS905x30OiX%2F-GOCxgiUzwyI&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce1ebfee4c6d3447190e908de5e068533%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051579282342163%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=f2fAohgQaIj7nvNuYdcPCbA%2F%2FJP4ma1ZQZaSvbY2P%2FE%3D&reserved=0>  updates every morning with:
 ✔️ Middle Market banks
 ✔️ Elite + regional boutiques
 ✔️ Bulge Brackets and niche groups

One dashboard. Every firm. No scrambling.

 <https://gxhch.img.a.d.sendibm1.com/im/sh/gdtaIIxUKbqW.jpeg?u=7xwQLFBtniwQn1MANwiooZhKcuWSuBF> 	
­	 

2. Recruiting right now: what actually matters


As we move deeper into the cycle, the biggest differentiator isn’t grinding more coffee chats. It's spending time efficiently and prepping the right things.




A few reminders we’ve been telling students:

*	Have 6 - 8 strong stories you can mold to fit any behavioral question
*	Have 2 deals prepared for each interview: one that the bank worked on and one in an industry you are interested in
*	Reach out to your strong connections / best coffee chats if you haven't received an interview from the firm
*	Prepare one market view you can articulate clearly (rates, M&A slowdown/rebound, sponsor activity)

 <https://gxhch.img.a.d.sendibm1.com/im/sh/ulCgUGvNGYay.jpeg?u=7xwQLFBtniwQn8DcWlfzyjBQSDGRClV> 	
­	 

3. How Students Are Using AskStanley Right Now


Usage on AskStanley is at an all-time high as recruiting accelerates!




Since summer, we’ve processed over 500,000 chat requests. We’re incredibly grateful for your support and excited to keep building alongside you. If you've made it this far, please let us know if you have any features or requests! Feel free to reply directly to this email. 

These students are using Stanley for: 

*	Track MM, boutique, and BB applications so nothing opens or closes without them seeing it
*	Prep targeted technicals and behaviorals based on what they’re actually being asked in interviews
*	Stay organized across recruiting: applications, networking, interviews, and deadlines in one place

­	 

Hope you are all enjoying using AskStanley. Reply to this email with any questions, and as always, good luck!!

Another photograph, by Kenny Holston, captured the attention of Joe Kahn, our executive editor, who won a Pulitzer Prize for his reporting on China. I asked Joe to tell us what he saw in the image:

A day of stagecraft and ceremony. Xi receives Trump with his feet firmly planted on the red carpet, arm raised high in preparation for a handshake. Trump approaches with his arm held low and his palm open.

ASK THE MORNING


Can you give some tips for distinguishing between real and fake content (A.I., conspiracy theories, misquotes, etc.)? This used to be relatively simple but seems to get harder by the day. How can we stay informed and accurate? | Sophie O’Driscoll | Copenhagen, Denmark

Steven Lee Myers, who covers the spread of information, replies:

You’re right. It’s getting harder. The social media giants have largely abandoned the fight against fake content, even as technology has made it easier to create and spread it. Some companies offer tools to detect videos made with A.I., but they’re not always definitive — and they’re not convenient to use as you scroll through your feed. Organizations like FactCheck.org and PolitiFact do a great job calling out politicians’ lies or conspiracy theories. In Europe, the European Union maintains a database of Russian disinformation. Unfortunately, there’s no silver bullet. The best advice still is to consider the source. Chances are “some random guy on the internet” is less reliable than a government agency or a news organization.

The Young and the Reckless

 

What’s more intimidating, an 800-pound gorilla or a horde of small ones?

 

Big brokers and hedge funds used to move markets, and they still can, but there’s a new boss in town. Self-styled “apes <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45732480.453174%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL3N0b2Nrcy9pbnNpZGUtYW1jcy1jcmF6eS1ib25rZXJzLXVwc2lkZS1kb3duLXllYXItb2YtYXBlcy1tZW1lcy1hbmQtc2hvcnRzLTExNjM5ODAzNjU1P21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB4e75fd5a&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cc692c3b1670545a803d908deb26ee62d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639144386559822738%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=63brTtKNXGRDatsdFqd3GWOkjTDVPnmFpc0QINXcpQo%3D&reserved=0> ” shocked Wall Street during 2021’s meme stock mania <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45732480.453174%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL3N0b2Nrcy93aG8tcmVhbGx5LWdvdC1yaWNoLWZyb20tdGhlLWdhbWVzdG9wLXJldm9sdXRpb24tMTE2NDM0MzI0MTg_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB2bb799b1&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cc692c3b1670545a803d908deb26ee62d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639144386559837694%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=z9XO4mWT4gTgBzJLOsKfOE7AuJZ%2BiQ0dqWE9N6qYZzs%3D&reserved=0> . Now they’re even more influential.

 

Very active traders, mostly young people who get cues from social media, make up a subset of the millions of Americans who hold about $12 trillion in retail brokerage accounts. They punch well above their weight by moving in crowds and magnifying their impact with leverage. That especially shows up when markets are volatile.

 

Goldman Sachs estimated this week that retail trading volumes were up by 28% since mid-April and that a basket of retail favorite stocks had risen by 29% over that stretch. The same thing was seen around the Covid panic, Liberation Day and other selloffs. It has changed how markets react to scary news and also the enthusiasm with which they greet hot new tech such as quantum computing.

 

“There’s just a lot of short attention span money in the market,” says Liz Ann Sonders, chief investment strategist at retail broker Charles Schwab. “We’ve definitely crossed into a new era.”

Older generations always think younger ones are reckless, whether it’s physical risks like riding a motorcycle or financial ones like day trading leveraged ETFs.

✏️ Good morning. While Washington slept, President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping shared a final cup of tea to wrap their high-stakes summit. So, where do the two superpower leaders stand? Both sides hailed a reset in relations—though each has a starkly different idea of what that means. For Trump, it is about opening China’s market to American business and reciprocal trade. Xi, meanwhile, wants “strategic stability,” a predictable relationship in which Washington doesn’t impede Beijing’s economic and geopolitical rise. Under the surface, however, there remains an intense rivalry <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-guiituk-hrkusddg-i%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cdc99fe22951c4c8d7cf408deb26e8ce1%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639144385051846622%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Y3SCUQsIR2X%2FeE7JGwoR2qb89A5n8XtPLjeyNYhIhXg%3D&reserved=0>  that holds the potential to disrupt the world stage.

Q: Are you eligible for a Covid-era loophole tax refund? Here’s what to know. 


Taxpayers could get money back from the IRS if they paid interest or penalties during the pandemic, explains Laura Saunders.

A: Millions of Americans could be owed billions of dollars in tax refunds of Covid-era interest and penalties due to a federal court decision.

A few months ago, a judge ruled in a case involving an individual that taxpayers didn’t owe certain interest and penalties between early 2020 and mid-2023, even if the IRS imposed them. In effect, the decision turned off the consequences of failing to meet many tax deadlines during the pandemic.

As a result, filers can request refunds of certain payments and seek abatements of penalties and interest assessed but not yet paid.

Note: The IRS is expected to appeal the federal court decision. If the agency wins, these favorable treatments may not apply.

The decision applies to tax underpayments such as estimated taxes; interest on deficiencies determined on audit; and possibly interest that accrued regardless of when the liability occurred. It also applies to penalties for failure to file or pay taxes by certain deadlines (like April 15), and penalties for late filings of international information forms.

To be eligible for refunds and other favorable treatment, however, filers need to send paperwork to the IRS by July 10.

💡 Tasking tips: what makes an AI agent different from a chatbot


Most AI tools are reactive: you type something, the model responds, and the interaction is over. An agent is different. It runs inside a piece of software called a scaffold, which gives the model memory, tools, and the ability to take actions on its own — without you directing it at every step. That setup is at the center of what agent coding tasks are asking you to evaluate.

Proactivity is what separates agents from assistants. A regular AI model waits for you. An agent checks your inbox every morning, responds to an alert before you've seen it, or monitors a website on a schedule. When you're evaluating agent outputs, the core question is: is the agent acting on its own initiative, and does that initiative make sense given what it was asked to do?

Memory changes how an agent behaves over time. Good scaffolds build up context — your preferences, past interactions, what's worked before. Two agents running the same underlying AI model can behave very differently because of what's in their memory. When evaluating responses, it's worth asking whether the agent is drawing on what it should know, or acting like every conversation is the first.

Subject: IFSA | Pre-Arrival Webinar July 7th 6PM EST
Body:
Dear IFSA Students and Families, 

 

I am writing to invite you to your IFSA Prearrival Orientation webinar on July 7th at 6 PM EST. 

 

This is a great opportunity to meet our Australia team and learn about travel, orientation, housing, insurance, and more! Please join us for this session by registering here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fevents.teams.microsoft.com%2Fevent%2Fad4aed77-74f7-45a5-a33f-82d8ac57e458%40538059de-6a35-4b9e-9a75-2978f2e06a16%2Fregistration&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8e9de6cb998f4f60ee1b08deb1fa2b44%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143885214384487%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=E84Tkzf2Li%2B5FFbUlTkAvHu8U6AsCJU9yAiLqO6MojU%3D&reserved=0> .

We can’t wait to see you!

Dear Undergraduate Students,

On May 1, an invitation to apply for three opportunities for university service during the 2026-2027 academic year was sent to students. This serves as a reminder that applications are due no later than 11:59 p.m. ET Sunday, May 17. Please see details below: 

Board of Trustees Standing Committees:  Duke University has a tradition of student engagement in the work of the Board of Trustees. For many years, there have been students serving on most of the board’s standing committees. In this capacity, students serve as fiduciaries of the university rather than representatives of the student body, aiming to think broadly about what is best for the whole university rather than any one constituency.

In the coming year, there are opportunities for undergraduate students to serve on board committees. One undergraduate student will be selected to serve on each of the following committees:  External Engagement, Finance, and Undergraduate Education. Undergraduates are full voting members of standing committees. A summary of the purposes of the various standing committees is available here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fd58mqh%2F1ry0blmb%2Fxkmfop&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7039122aa02645bde11108deb1e63c43%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143799582924089%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=s0DngDWRqiFwbnDpdJhBdCCpAkza73TmiYoQ4xPjTNo%3D&reserved=0> .

Students selected for these positions will be forwarded to President Price with the recommendation that he bring the nominations to the Board of Trustees for confirmation.

The standing committee meetings will take place during three of the four board weekends:

*	Friday, September 25, 2026
*	Friday, December 4, 2026
*	Friday, May 7, 2027

The standing committees will meet from 1:15 – 3:15 p.m. ET. The three meetings listed above will be held in person, on campus. (Please note, you must be able to attend in person. We do not reimburse for travel.) There will also be one meeting of each committee in February via Zoom, and we will poll for best availability. 

Climate Commitment Advisory Council (CCAC) Subcommittees:  CCAC serves as an advisory body to the Executive Leadership of the University (President, Provost, Executive Vice President, Executive Vice President for Health Affairs, and DUHS Chief Executive Officer) and is guided by multiple subcommittees for the purpose of operationalizing and coordinating the key concepts of the Duke Climate Commitment. This will be an opportunity for faculty, staff, and students to engage in the goal of infusing climate and sustainability into all aspects of the University mission and to imagine, design and implement a sustainable future for all.

Subcommittees typically meet twice a semester throughout the academic year. There are opportunities for student service on the following subcommittees:

*	Research Innovation
*	Education Integration
*	Sustainable Operations
*	External Engagement for Impact

Each subcommittee will invite two undergraduate students to serve in 2026-2027.

For more information on the work of each subcommittee, please visit - https://climate.duke.edu/leadership/climate-advisory-council/climate-advisory-council-subcommittee-updates/ <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fd58mqh%2F1ry0blmb%2Fddnfop&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7039122aa02645bde11108deb1e63c43%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143799582937390%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=UefEK5MAR40B4IWjihKo9eXDGgHH6NEcMSP1ovKoVRg%3D&reserved=0>  and review the Duke Climate Commitment 2030 Strategy <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fd58mqh%2F1ry0blmb%2Ft5nfop&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7039122aa02645bde11108deb1e63c43%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143799582950438%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=tejlK7VO9WlhfzPWi9d9c%2F3%2Fp5ZDgRw2ki5%2B7DJb%2BQI%3D&reserved=0> .

Campus Experience and Culture Advisory Council (CECAC) Subcommittees. The CECAC comprises leaders from across Duke who represent a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. The council facilitates efforts to strengthen Duke’s campus culture. CECAC’s mission is to ensure that Duke’s campus culture strategy reflects and represents the experiences and perspectives of all members of the community.
To support this work, the council operates through four subcommittees that coordinate and inform centralized initiatives aimed at improving the culture of the Duke community and the overall experience of everyone within it. There are opportunities for student service on the following subcommittees:
Campus Experience Survey
This subcommittee gathers and analyzes survey data to support evidence-based decisions that improve the Duke campus experience. It develops and administers the Campus Experience Survey every three years, with the next iteration scheduled for 2027. The group collaborates with campus leaders to share and interpret results and supports units in using the data to set priorities and implement initiatives aligned with Duke’s Inclusive Excellence principles.
  
Communications Subcommittee
This subcommittee communicates the results of the Campus Experience Survey and related initiatives to the Duke community. It promotes the importance of the survey and supports marketing and awareness efforts prior to its launch, translates survey data into clear and accessible messaging, and provides communication support to campus leaders and units to highlight how evidence-based insights are used to improve the experiences of students, faculty, and staff.
  
Infrastructure and Implementation Subcommittee
This subcommittee reviews and advances policies, protocols, and practices that improve the campus experience for the Duke community. It develops strategies to help units use Campus Experience Survey results to guide improvements and recommends policies that address gaps identified in the data, consistent with Duke’s Inclusive Excellence principles. The group also supports institutional planning to help units measure progress on survey outcomes and collaborates with Human Resources to strengthen staff professional development and related initiatives.
  
One undergraduate student will be invited to serve on each of the above subcommittees. There will be two meetings of each subcommittee per semester.

Please note if selected for one of the CECAC subcommittee positions, we will ask for a two-year commitment or until graduation, whichever comes first.
  
If you are interested in these opportunities, I invite you to submit an application (LINK HERE <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fd58mqh%2F1ry0blmb%2F9xofop&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7039122aa02645bde11108deb1e63c43%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143799582962563%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=3I7qLzNi18x%2BWy3Ni9YavobsFA%2BV%2FBWSgKt1RMCdoeA%3D&reserved=0> ) no later than 11:59 p.m. ET on Sunday, May 17.

Please note:  You may apply for all three opportunities. You will need to submit a separate application for each engagement in which you are interested. You may apply for only one Board of Trustees standing committee.

Notes:  For these opportunities, in order to be eligible to apply, you must be enrolled as an undergraduate student in the 2026-2027 academic year. Students selected for these positions will be notified by mid-June. Please keep an eye on your Duke email for information concerning your application.

Best,

About the Fulbright Applicant Mastermind

 

The Fulbright Awards are some of the most well-known, and thus, some of the most competitive in the world. Fulbright applications require a Personal Statement and Statement of Grant Purpose (a research, study or teaching proposal). Also, most applicants need to identify a host institution abroad and gather recommendation letters, among other elements. It's an intense application process that offers an incredible international exchange opportunity to those who approach the application with purpose. 

 

In this 3 hour workshop, you will learn:

 

*	The Fulbright applicant’s formula for success: What to know before you begin

*	Your Fulbright application plan: Choosing a country and award, planning your application activities & accelerating your productivity

*	How to do investigative background research on your Fulbright award (and why you shouldn’t miss this step)

*	Statement of Grant Purpose brainstorming session: How to make your proposal feasible, memorable, and urgent

*	How to secure not a good – but a *great* – affiliation abroad and how your affiliation impacts your application

*	The 3 things you must address in your Fulbright Personal Statement and exercises to get you started on your story

*	How to receive glowing & detailed recommendation letters (even from people who have not seen you in years)

*	3 secrets to taking your Fulbright application above and beyond

 

I can’t wait to share our winning Fulbright application strategies with you!

In the end, I applied to the Fulbright Specialist program. Guess what? My application was approved!!!!! What I most want you to know is that I am grateful for the services that you provide.” - Mi’Jan Celie Tho-Biaz, Fulbright Specialist grantee

A ProFellow newsletter

Dear ProFellow readers,
 

This is Dr. Vicki Johnson, the Founder and Director of ProFellow. Thank you for joining ProFellow.com <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FTrOBfSpMC9lF%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce71d6e5a123d49a2728b08deb1d06c91%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143705938944746%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=TMxk4%2B9rUUkKfdHd1%2Beay%2FgvFRgqM6mGIkWYiGpfOnk%3D&reserved=0> , the leading resource to help you do something exceptional at any stage in your career. ProFellow offers a HUGE free database of competitive fellowships, graduate schools, international exchange, research awards, leadership programs, and business accelerators.
 

But I don't want you to just find these unique opportunities, I want you to win them! That's what this weekly newsletter — and my new book, Pitch Your Potential: The Formula for Winning Dream Jobs, Awards, and Elite Opportunities <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FhOrU0iuNsCdT%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce71d6e5a123d49a2728b08deb1d06c91%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143705938994765%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=bxaXUcFKXqfGxdxekkP%2F6aQ67eQsseu1eYip5xPh4%2FQ%3D&reserved=0>  — are all about! 

 

In this weekly newsletter, sent every Sunday, I will be sharing tested application strategies to fuel your success. 
 

People often ask me why I started ProFellow and care about leveling the playing field for opportunities in higher education and leadership.

 

It's because many of you have the potential to win these extraordinary opportunities, but lack access to insider knowledge and networks that share them. 

 

When I was growing up, I loved school and wanted to travel the world and become a leader in public service. I just didn't know how — there was a lot of information and guidance that I was missing. 

 

But I was raised by inspiring parents who taught me how to leverage two key skills: storytelling and attention to detail.
 

By honing these skills and mastering the story of my future potential, I overcame the perception of being an "average" student to get into top universities, fellowships, dream jobs, and a top business accelerator, which took me all over the world on a career adventure. 

 

I now love teaching the winner's mindset and how to pitch your potential to others! I created the MATCH ME Formula®, the 7 elements of a winning application, to help you master the tactics of multi-award winners.

 

From 2019, more than 300 members in my Fully Funded Course and Mentorship Program <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2F0vSck4dG5BCp%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce71d6e5a123d49a2728b08deb1d06c91%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143705939018749%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=AHMRvXH1UJanQyFT95Xy4LvKMUooBwAraOUtURt1PqM%3D&reserved=0>  learned the MATCH ME Formula® and were selected for top PhD and Master's programs. Collectively, they achieved 547+ Master's acceptances, 151+ PhD acceptances, and 51 nationally competitive fellowships! This amounted to $36 million in funding awards.

 

This is just the beginning!

 

The first lesson I want to share with you is:
 

	The story of your future is more important to selectors than the story of your past.

 

Your ability to tell a compelling story of your future potential is THE thing that helps you win highly competitive opportunities and beat out people with more experience and credentials. 

 

Each Sunday I'll provide insights and tips on how to tell the story of your highest potential. Stay tuned! 
​

Warm regards,

 

Vicki
 

Dr. Vicki Johnson

Founder, ProFellow
​Author of Pitch Your Potential: The Formula for Winning Dream Jobs, Awards, and Elite Opportunities <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprofellow.krtra.com%2Fc%2FPBgWuxezE1Xc%2FMGoG9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce71d6e5a123d49a2728b08deb1d06c91%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143705939054102%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=u4cW9nqObv61Jz5Dq%2FVN%2BcRTvjuyMVDU1GRLXKEyxao%3D&reserved=0> 
 

“There is no such thing as unrewarded effort when you apply your greatest effort.”

Real stories from students who used the Adventis FMC® Program to build technical skills, land competitive internships, and break into investment banking.

After completing the Financial Modeling Certification® (FMC®) Program during his junior year, Tim (UGA Class of 2019) gained the technical skills, confidence, and clarity to pursue a career in investment banking. The certification on his resume caught interviewers’ attention, and his ability to walk through complex financial scenarios set him apart from other candidates. Tim began his career at Truist Securities and now works in private equity at Nolan Capital. Looking back, he credits his career path in part to Adventis’s early, hands-on training.

‘People Are Desperate for Indicators’

 

How bad was it?

 

The obvious way to measure a market selloff is by the amount that stocks went down, but that doesn’t tell you investors’ emotional state. A recession is unpleasant. A terrorist attack, bank collapse or pandemic can be downright terrifying, even if prices don’t fall by quite as much.

 

That’s where the market’s “fear gauge” comes in. The Cboe Volatility Index <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45710816.455177%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9tYXJrZXQtZGF0YS9xdW90ZXMvaW5kZXgvVklYP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB27803861&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7c1a687db62f4ccf5a8708deb1a63fef%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143524824035352%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=A82HJc0uBsZPhjhLESMubjIeXhr8LwBUovhbk056n2Y%3D&reserved=0> , or VIX, has become a quick-and-dirty way to quantify caution. Well, it used to be.

 

“People are desperate for indicators so they look at VIX and they misunderstand it,” says Scott Nations, president of volatility index developer Nations Indexes.

 

The VIX holds steady all the inputs in the formula for pricing S&P 500 call or put options contracts over the next 30 days, except for how much choppiness they assume—the market’s implied volatility. (Calls confer the right to buy, puts the right to sell, at given prices).

 

Those options are a bit like insurance. Premiums surge when a storm is upon us and gradually get back to normal.

 

Lately, though, options prices have been tamed by an influx of supply from deep-pocketed insurance agents. Popular funds like the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF sell calls to boost their payouts <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45710816.455177%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL2ludmVzdGluZy9ob3ctdGhlc2UtbmV3LWZ1bmRzLXNxdWVlemUtMTQteWllbGRzLW91dC1vZi1zdG9ja3MtY2VhNDhjNmI_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBa2ccf613&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7c1a687db62f4ccf5a8708deb1a63fef%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143524824052652%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=GlJpDbfKSzArxgzXnwbMx54Y9SQCBZdrRwIJHdxaikY%3D&reserved=0> .

 

“There’s a giant complex of derivatives that help keep volatility suppressed,” says Brent Kochuba, founder of options research firm SpotGamma.

 

So the VIX’s signal as an indicator of investor angst is being muted, and when it does spike it doesn’t stay high for as long.

 

For example, it breached 60 during last April’s Liberation Day swoon. That was its highest level since the Covid panic five years earlier (the number represents annual implied volatility in percentage points). But the VIX fell below 30 in a couple of weeks with tariffs only delayed. It was back to a humdrum 20 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45710816.455177%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2Uvc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LWpvYnMtcmVwb3J0LWRvdy1zcDUwMC1uYXNkYXEtMDYtMDYtMjAyNS9jYXJkL3ZpeC1mYWxscy10by1sb3dlc3QtbGV2ZWwtc2luY2UtYmVmb3JlLXRydW1wLXMtbGliZXJhdGlvbi1kYXktLXVCTkd2Q1g2OW80aGdTSm13SVBiP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB90ab49a9&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C7c1a687db62f4ccf5a8708deb1a63fef%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143524824109359%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=V%2BdTcXn%2F1Pa9eLkywV9zqDrx5Bvq9iIhUtLvt6ITEs8%3D&reserved=0>  in a month.

 

Because it has been so profitable to “sell” volatility—a bet that it will decline quickly—investors have jumped on VIX spikes using exchange traded products or options.

 

“If it works, people do it more,” says Nations.

 

The Iran conflict has seen some unusual complacency. Kochuba says that in turn reinforces the boldness of day traders and systematic, trend-following hedge funds who buy dips in stocks. Recently, the VIX had the sort of drop on vague Iran peace headlines only seen once before following a surprise Fed rate cut.

 

With the price of insurance low and volatility following a predictable, profitable pattern, Nations sees a risk that investors will take on more risk than they realize and get blindsided.

 

“I think it’s only a matter of time until people see it spike and then rush in and then it spikes again and they get carried out.”

 

We have nothing to fear but the lack of fear itself.

A crowded field


The next presidential election is more than two years away. But watch in the coming weeks and months when politicians from out of state start showing up in Iowa to give speeches and shake hands. Online and in the circles I travel in, it’ll lead to a knowing smirk: He’s runnin’. Or she is. Folks in the political class are beginning to think about the future, and about how brightly it could shine on them.

Reid Epstein, who has covered every presidential campaign since 2008, has kept an eye on the shadow campaigns. He maintains a spreadsheet of every potential candidate for the nation’s top job. The vice presidents

The New York Times	

Vice President JD Vance isn’t saying much about 2028 right now. His boss is still running the show, and it wouldn’t look good. But he’s styled himself as Trump’s heir for years, and was in Iowa at the start of the month.

Then there’s former Vice President Kamala Harris, who probably has the biggest name in the field. That cuts both ways. Many Democrats may hunger for a candidate less tied to President Joe Biden after their disaster with him in 2024.

	

The Trump administration officials

 <https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/05/14/multimedia/14themorning-nl-admin/14themorning-nl-admin-jumbo.png> 	
The New York Times	

Secretary of State Marco Rubio is also in the mix, Vance’s top primary competitor should they both run (or top ally should they run together). He ran for president in 2016.

Other cabinet members have already taken runs at the White House, including Doug Burgum, the interior secretary; Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the health and human services secretary (he ran as both a Democrat and an independent in 2024); and Tulsi Gabbard, the director of national intelligence. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has not made a bid for the presidency before, but now that a lot of people know his name, he might want to try.

The governors

The New York Times	

A lot of state leaders, of both parties, would like to make the jump to the national stage.

Among the Democrats, there’s Gavin Newsom of California, one of the loudest anti-Trump voices. Also the billionaire JB Pritzker of Illinois and Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania. And Wes Moore of Maryland has been steadily building a national profile. For the Republicans, it’s possible that Ron DeSantis of Florida could enter the race again. And Greg Abbott of Texas might try for the first time, hopeful that his anti-immigration policies echo nationally. You could see Brian Kemp of Georgia on the hustings, too, along with Sarah Huckabee Sanders of Arkansas and Glenn Youngkin, the former governor of Virginia.

For the Republicans, look to Ted Cruz of Texas and Rand Paul of Kentucky. They both ran in 2016. And to Tim Scott of South Carolina, who ran in 2024.

The reign of ‘El Chapo’ is over but the bodies keep piling up. 


As the U.S. targets corrupt Mexican officials who aided the imprisoned drug lord’s clan, a bloody civil war <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-guilkyk-hrkusddg-c%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce298adf51ee44888349308deb1a2813d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143508684871135%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=oNgklSheeWoZ%2B9tGogAmkHriVOsme48HE7l1nXBCENc%3D&reserved=0>  is raging for control of the Sinaloa cartel. It’s a war that the Chapitos, the heirs of Mexican drug boss Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, appear to be losing, casting doubt on the future of a dynasty that once ruled vast swaths of the criminal underworld on its way to becoming the world’s top producer and smuggler of fentanyl. The fight among criminal pretenders to Guzmán’s throne has unfolded like a Shakespearean drama, sparked by betrayal, ambition, greed—and rivers of blood, report José de Córdoba and Santiago Pérez.

Q: How is the U.S. government responding to hantavirus? 


The Trump administration’s health officials are walking a tightrope on hantavirus: trying to avoid public panic and a repeat of what they view as pandemic-era missteps, while escalating the federal response <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-guilkyk-hrkusddg-g%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce298adf51ee44888349308deb1a2813d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639143508684978903%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=2txaSYqSnUTUpp8m6O3c1DNccS%2FAfflYYcC1X06FDiU%3D&reserved=0>  to the threat, explain Sabrina Siddiqui and Jennifer Calfas.

A: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has increased the number of staff assigned to the effort from three late last week to around 100, according to internal CDC data viewed by the Journal.

The group working on hantavirus includes staffers from the agency’s National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases, according to CDC employees.

The increase in personnel reflects mounting urgency inside the administration to contain a rare hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius before it spreads further.

But lingering skepticism among some top health officials about strict Covid-19 pandemic measures has made the administration cautious about imposing quarantines or other restrictions for a virus known to be less transmissible, but more deadly, than Covid, according to people familiar with the matter.

On Monday, 18 passengers returned to the U.S. and 15 of them were taken to a specialized quarantine facility at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in Omaha.

Dear Graham,

As part of your Blackstone campus program application, we would like to invite you to complete our pymetrics online games. The games are one of the components of our overall application process and help us identify your strengths in an objective manner and learn a little about you in a fun and interactive way. After playing these games, you will be considered for the next phase of our process.

Best practices:

- Work through the games steadily and complete in one-sitting; estimated completion timing is 25-30 minutes for all the games

Dear Graham,

 

The digital world is entering a phase where connectivity is no longer simply an enabler. It is becoming the system itself. Infrastructure, communication, and security technologies are converging into integrated environments designed for continuous, real-time operation. Developments in April 2026 reflect a clear shift toward building a connected world where systems are expected to operate seamlessly across physical and digital boundaries.

 

This shift is being shaped by several significant developments. Amazon.com, Inc. announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire Globalstar, Inc., enabling Amazon Leo to incorporate direct-to-device services into its low-earth-orbit satellite network. This allows smartphones to connect directly to satellites, extending cellular coverage beyond terrestrial limitations.

 

By integrating Globalstar’s spectrum and proven mobile satellite services capabilities with the scale and reach of Amazon Leo, the company is positioning itself to deliver continuous connectivity across consumer, enterprise, and government use cases worldwide. At the same time, Stellantis entered a five-year strategic partnership with Microsoft to accelerate its digital transformation. The collaboration focuses on building an AI-powered ecosystem that enhances engineering capabilities while embedding cybersecurity directly into vehicle architecture.

 

Data across mobile applications, in vehicle systems, and cloud environments is secured as part of the system itself. In parallel, Zyxel Networks introduced the WBE665S, a BE22000 12 stream WiFi 7 Triple Radio NebulaFlex Pro ruggedized access point. Designed for professional installers operating in harsh environments such as manufacturing plants, cold storage facilities, and warehouses, the system combines high-capacity performance with an IP67 rated weatherproof design and intelligent cloud management.

 

Together, these developments point to a broader shift toward communication-centric infrastructure and a more connected world. Connectivity is no longer defined by speed alone. It is becoming foundational to how systems operate, scale, and interact. At the same time, cybersecurity is evolving into both a product feature and a regulatory necessity, particularly in the automotive industry. Standards such as UNECE WP.29 now require manufacturers to implement risk management and software update governance systems, embedding security directly into system design.

 

Demand signals reinforce this transition. According to the Cisco State of Wireless Report, WiFi has developed into a multiplier effect producing strategic growth engine. Nearly three out of five businesses are planning to implement WiFi 7 in the coming years, driven by the expansion of AI workloads, the Internet of Things, and high-bandwidth applications such as augmented reality, virtual reality, and 4K and 8K streaming. As a result, wireless modernization is becoming central to digital infrastructure strategies.

 

Several trends are accelerating this shift. AI-powered cybersecurity platforms are becoming essential as systems expand and threats increase in sophistication. Multi-band satellite architecture is improving reliability and performance by combining frequency bands such as C, L, Ka, Ku, and V. Direct-to-device connectivity is reducing reliance on terrestrial networks and expanding access to remote regions. At the same time, advancements in WiFi 7 are enabling low latency and ultra-fast connectivity, supporting remote work, streaming, and smart home ecosystems.

 

From a market perspective, the impact is already visible. Cybersecurity is becoming a mandatory layer in modern vehicle architecture, while also enabling new revenue streams. Growth in the connectivity market is being fueled by industrial IoT, immersive media, and high-bandwidth applications. At the same time, the industry is shifting from hardware-based models toward software-driven platforms, supported by regulation-driven expansion and the need for integrated solutions.

 

However, scaling this infrastructure introduces several challenges. Cybersecurity risks remain a major concern, with increasing remote attacks that require no physical proximity to systems. The transition to WiFi 7 requires significant investment in new switches, cabling, and compatible devices, creating capital expenditure challenges for small and medium-sized businesses.

 

Satellite connectivity also depends on supporting infrastructure such as gateways and integration with terrestrial networks, which can slow adoption. In addition, orbital crowding is emerging as a real risk. In April 2026, a Starlink satellite broke up in orbit, prompting SpaceX to reposition approximately 4,500 satellites to alleviate congestion, highlighting the complexity of managing large-scale satellite networks.

 

Looking ahead, the next phase will be defined by deployment at scale. AI-driven cybersecurity platforms are expected to move from pilot to implementation, including the expansion of vehicle Security Operations Centers and AI-based anomaly detection across fleets. Stellantis and Microsoft are strengthening global cyber defense capabilities through AI-driven analytics to protect vehicles, customers, and operations worldwide. At the same time, WiFi is entering a new growth phase. WiFi 7 is expanding rapidly and laying the foundation for WiFi 8 and mmWave technologies, enabling deployments that improve user experience, generate income, and lower operational costs. As WiFi converges with 5G and eventually 6G, organizations will be able to build smarter factories, smarter cities, and new ways to involve customers.

 

Another critical development is the expansion of direct-to-device connectivity. Companies are working to bring satellite-based broadband directly to smartphones. In April 2026, AST SpaceMobile received a commercial license from the Federal Communications Commission to use spectrum from partner mobile network operators such as Verizon, AT&T, and FirstNet. Operating in low-band frequencies between 700 MHz and 800 MHz, this enables seamless space-based cellular broadband for everyday users, helping people stay connected regardless of location.

 

What is emerging is a digital ecosystem where connectivity, cybersecurity, and infrastructure are tightly integrated to support continuous, real-time operations. The ability to scale will depend on how effectively these elements are combined into systems that are both resilient and adaptable.

 

This is the moment when automotive cybersecurity, WiFi 7, and satellite internet collectively indicate the rise of next-generation connectivity infrastructure designed for autonomy, scalability, and resilience.

Good morning. I am really looking forward to introducing you to the last full-time museum taxidermist in the United States. But first, a few things.

	
	
	
 <https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/05/13/multimedia/13themorning-xi-fgmw/13themorning-xi-fgmw-jumbo.jpg> 	
President Trump and Xi Jinping in Busan, South Korea, last year.  Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times	

At the summit


“This is not how President Trump wanted to arrive in China,” my colleague David Sanger writes <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2F_uHRI04qh9BJLmevQoajAg~~%2FAAAAARA~%2F-7CluAovpAwHyRZaMn78gDzg7I-QQifcTMFnfXENaT0coZUAOw1jk0-c1zsbywl9EZBkMcVx2G73tTnuzaEprRc6aHnNvkycV4HrQbQNCcOeXHg7CfC8OHNmJSHOJkgo0Xu5f4Nuax8MmiUNDb7KTJQ4Of8R7QjqI4G8oKsN5uPOHa09eYGk8EK5xo5GxwnqUkJm4EvXRtYb9XNiirz-b0kRplD1x88IRi2oGRZR7VpHZgyQ3D0m4fApR8FN7a6mXSKHFXurtW-QSOjcvSFffJljDuntulb7x4o0vWtViDXbUCHfbSeuOImqyqeiS_7rMyT9NzDV7PTy9VnZGAM3wxCPPvxyP2RAiE8YTH0CHqM~&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ccc73b7804f84428e6bca08deb0dbc817%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639142655187736587%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=XsKmdMz8io57OdnifhmFRJuNWUjKXdHQQ9mfLMvZazA%3D&reserved=0> .

Six weeks ago, Trump pushed off his summit meeting with China’s leader, Xi Jinping, because of the war in Iran. He’d thought the conflict would be over by now, showing Beijing that reports of America’s demise as a superpower were premature. Instead, David writes, Trump starts the meeting today “bogged down by a far lesser power in a war he started.”

But Xi’s in a tough spot, too. China gets more than 30 percent of its oil from the Persian Gulf, which is now cut off. Economic growth there is falling as energy prices rise. “The result is that this is a summit like few others,” David writes. It features the world’s two dominant superpowers looking hobbled. Experts aren’t optimistic the sides will announce a major economic deal or resolve their differences.

China correspondent David Pierson replies:

Despite being the largest importer of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz, China has weathered the crisis relatively well. It has been stockpiling oil since last year. The numbers are startling. Reading scores were down last year in 83 percent of school districts for which we have data. Math scores were down in 70 percent.

The drops happened in rich districts as well as poor ones — in urban, suburban and rural ones. They crossed racial divides. And the biggest losses of all were among the lowest-achieving kids. In one in three school districts in the U.S., my colleagues report, students are reading a full grade level lower than they were in 2015.

Education experts told The Times that there’s no single reason for this learning recession. But federal school accountability has relaxed since the No Child Left Behind Act was replaced in 2015. There was also the rise of iPhones, social media and school-issued laptops. And of course the pandemic didn’t help. Student absenteeism spiked and remains high in its wake.
