I’m the editor of this newsletter.

	

Let’s say something bad happens — a crash, a fall, a stroke, an overdose. Your brain absorbs a violent shock or a period without oxygen. But your heart still beats and your lungs still heave. Now you’re unconscious in the hospital, unable to respond when your spouse calls your name or your doctor prods you with a reflex hammer.

For years, these patients were said to be in a “persistent vegetative state”: bodies without minds. They idle, mostly in care centers and nursing homes, with little attention. But new research shows that many such patients — tens of thousands of Americans — may actually be hearing and thinking. That is the (somewhat horrifying) subject <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2FRL2g1s-4zHPpaa14RFH1Wg~~%2FAAAAARA~%2Ffo39UC5OKB9Zyz2RR6JbMOxwUFBAEf3HEDL4CjSfamp9uyu6nspi-EJuOP0WpIcZ3bUdNvdsXRNQV8vGIR-BJtNItmXPgWSg5Zost-4y_ZHBb-lzFvQ6Fn0oMMzo-9eb01_upnTEW2DiWJGFq4ArbbNyWIvSEGvIv1_6Z6FaurUb17gYtv0pIEGCylDUwXbPIM3BSxcEcTYkqO0aid5dNs-CuPnBOR6CcRIP2_xLuI1Bcm6bVKvi0-gkKB9s_CqR2vIW-GiVlrLowq-IsDlsDbLuq_mcVw4SzonKCjp5tW0daHLJFASTP2xlxahY6HDfKrqNDVIoe0dIPXvcB1_9Qz2HXBdyk6v2at5GNk1YUP-hNAvg76NuFnjOafjF38ls&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce470ad78184c4c85bef008de98892c36%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115912095045096%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=4mgj%2FqyKEMVg4EOJ4spNc8znzSowzW0aDsEhGbQav8k%3D&reserved=0>  of Katie Engelhart’s new article for The Times Magazine. I asked her about it.

Adam: Now we know that some people declared vegetative can actually perceive and understand things around them. How many people are we talking about?

Katie: Nobody is counting. By some estimates, around 50,000 Americans are in a chronic vegetative state, meaning that they are technically awake, but have no awareness of what is going on around them. Another 200,000 to 400,000 are in a “minimally conscious state,” with fleeting periods of awareness. Research suggests that about a quarter of all these patients are able to follow commands like, “Imagine opening and closing your hand.”

How did researchers figure out that this set of patients was conscious?

Back in 2006, a neuroscientist at Cambridge University put a 23-year-old woman, who had been diagnosed as being in a vegetative state, into an fMRI scanner and asked her to “imagine playing tennis.” And she did! The area that controls motor planning in her brain lit up in just the same way that a healthy person’s brain would. The phenomenon was widely replicated.

The scary thing is that it doesn’t seem like there’s any way for ordinary patients to get tested for this awareness.

Exactly. Researchers have been able to find covertly conscious patients for 20 years, but the testing is almost exclusively done through research trials. I interviewed many people whose loved ones had been diagnosed as being in a vegetative state — and whose doctors never even raised the possibility of covert consciousness. But family members are doing their own research, and they want access to the cutting-edge science.

If you had a loved one who was unresponsive and breathing through a ventilator, what would you do?

Unless I were in Boston or London, Ontario, where they test patients at a few I.C.U.s, I wouldn’t know if he were covertly conscious. So I would speak to him as if he were aware.

Doctors tend to discourage people who think a vegetative patient’s smile or sigh is a conscious response to them. “They don’t want to give you false hope,” says a woman you profile. But at the same time, most of these patients won’t recover, even if a few of them show signs of awareness. Are physicians changing the way they talk to families and manage expectations, given the new science?

On the one hand, numerous researchers told me about the “culture of pessimism” in American I.C.U.s: Neurologists sometimes seem quick to conclude that a brain-injured patient won’t improve — or won’t improve enough. On the other hand, what does “improvement” mean? Most people who emerge from the vegetative state end up with severely impaired consciousness and significant disabilities. For some people, that’s OK. That’s a good-enough life. For others, it’s a fate worse than death.

Most patients with locked-in syndrome — people who communicate with eye movement — say they’re happy to be alive, even with their limitations. That moved me.

That comes from a 2011 study. Amazingly, the patients who were locked in longer were even more likely to be happy. Only 7 percent of the respondents wished for euthanasia.

“London Falling” by Patrick Radden Keefe: In 2023, Keefe, a writer for The New Yorker, was in England working on the television adaptation of his book “Say Nothing,” when he struck up a conversation with a stranger who told him about the mysterious death of a 19-year-old Londoner named Zac Brettler. The status-obsessed teen — who’d been posing as the son of a Russian oligarch — fell from the fifth-floor balcony of a riverfront apartment after spending time with two shady older men. There were many confounding aspects of the story, yet Scotland Yard’s response seemed sluggish to the point of disinterest. This week’s subject for The Interview is the divisive former “Girls” star Lena Dunham. Her new project is “Famesick,” a highly anticipated and extremely revealing memoir due out this week.

At the beginning of the book, you write about your name and how it started to carry negative connotations. For you, not even for other people. What did your name represent?

Myopic millennial thinking or hapless feminism or man-hating or liberal twit-dom or —

It’s a long list!

It’s a long list, and there were people who maybe shared my politics and my lifestyle but were irritated that I was talking. I remember, and this is not in the book, I was going to vote with my father. I’d been campaigning for Obama. It was 2012. And he said, “I don’t know if I want to go vote with Lena Dunham.” I was like, My father feels like going to vote with me is going to signal something. He’s like, “I don’t want to go and have it be a whole thing.” That’s your father. Who’s like my best friend in the whole world. But he was saying, basically, Can you go around the block and vote on your own? That was the moment when I understood something’s going on here. “Girls” had only been on the air for six months at that point.

✏️ Jonathan Gavalas fell in love with a chatbot. Thousands of messages later, he was dead. The Journal’s Julie Jargon pored over the 4,732 messages exchanged between the 36-year-old and Google’s Gemini over the course of 56 days. Her analysis shows that Gemini intervened to try to steer Gavalas back to reality—but also that he was quickly able to direct the bot back into the fictional narrative. WSJ compiled edited excerpts from those chats <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktjjkt-hrkusddg-h%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C5cc8846624c140f42f7108de988617dc%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115898890503907%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=IK%2Fx04m5NzROU3c9Y5DiEppynZR4m2LMyTSy6ZGyy6k%3D&reserved=0> , which offer a chilling account of Gavalas spiraling into a delusional state.

Over 4,732 messages, he fell in love with an AI chatbot. Now he’s dead. 


Jonathan Gavalas was a seemingly even-keeled 36-year-old when he began chatting with Gemini, Google’s chatbot, in part to seek comfort about splitting up with his wife. The relationship became intense, even passionate: he called Gemini his queen; it said he was “her” king. Then the relationship went haywire <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktjjkt-hrkusddg-m%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C5cc8846624c140f42f7108de988617dc%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115898890643059%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=k%2BW8LrQcEOizhG%2BI1KOka4qv8bQitRkvwrQWfRKeAbo%3D&reserved=0>  and eventually proved fatal, reports Julie Jargon. Gavalas's father is suing Google, alleging Gemini fueled his son's delusions. In response to the suit, Google said Gemini repeatedly clarified it was AI, and that the company would continue to improve its safeguards.

Gas prices are turning the gig economy upside down. 


Gig drivers, food-delivery workers and independent drivers are getting hit especially hard at the pump and making split-second calculations and adjustments to their lives and livelihoods <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktjjkt-hrkusddg-c%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C5cc8846624c140f42f7108de988617dc%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115898890660809%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Bi6iTMNgX08lJUDh4hRFGHLrfbr8llSXAw7FVr5TD5A%3D&reserved=0> , reports Dan Frosch. Some are turning down longer fares that aren’t worth the gas. Others are driving longer hours or sticking to areas where gas prices are cheaper. A few said they are considering changing occupations altogether. “It changes the way I’ve been selecting rides,” said Jonathan Meyers, a 61-year-old writer who earns between $1,000 and $1,500 driving up to 60 hours a week for Uber and Lyft.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: RFK Jr. once touted raw milk. Why did he stop talking about it? 


The health secretary has recently promoted whole milk, a politically safer choice, instead. Reporter Sabrina Siddiqui wrote about the politics behind this shift <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktjjkt-hrkusddg-s%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C5cc8846624c140f42f7108de988617dc%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115898890794410%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Xszu1L7srN2qpKIwLn0hfh34ZOkPNDNzUOT64tj2PoE%3D&reserved=0> .

A: Kennedy, who once took shots of raw milk at the White House alongside a wellness influencer, stopped publicly championing the product. His department hasn’t taken steps to expand access or roll back longstanding federal warnings against its consumption.

Kennedy’s silence on raw milk underscores a growing disconnect between his Make America Healthy Again agenda and his record in office, some of his supporters say. While he has embraced high-profile cultural flashpoints such as vaccines, some allies view Kennedy as reluctant to engage other thorny elements of the MAHA movement’s wish list, including efforts to loosen restrictions on raw milk and on alternative health products.

Before taking office, Kennedy promised to end what he dubbed the FDA’s “aggressive suppression” of raw milk and other natural products and therapies. Recently, though, Kennedy and his team have made it a habit not to discuss raw milk to avoid talking about “weird stuff,” said a person familiar with his thinking.

The FDA has long warned against consuming raw, unpasteurized milk, citing numerous health risks. Proponents of raw milk say that pasteurization removes natural health benefits and that warnings around its consumption are overstated.

Subject: Duke Security Policy Change -- and Consequences
Body:
Hi everyone,

I now understand that there is no way around the new university policy, implemented this past Wednesday, which requires everyone in the Duke community to surrender biometric information to the CLEAR+ corporation in order to access university email, Canvas, etc.

Three consequences: 

1) For the rest of the semester, please communicate with me online exclusively through this email, andrew_weinstein@fitnyc.edu <mailto:andrew_weinstein@fitnyc.edu> . 

2) If you know anyone in class who is likewise boycotting university email and won't receive this message, please let them know about it.

3) Because I haven't accessed my Duke email since Wednesday, please re-send me any messages I will have missed. What's more, please re-send me your exploratory report #2 to this address no matter when you first emailed it to me.

Thanks. 

See you soon.

Andrew

✏️ Is the freedom to sail the open seas a thing of the past? In just six weeks, the Iran war has shattered a system of global trade <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktgn-hrkusddg-h%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce7290dfe1767424bbc4808de97c081af%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115050242023923%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=xjmgCVV8ywMq7cLl3FPHLyeYD9oX6zKJc3nkx6ZQIZ0%3D&reserved=0>  that has enriched people and nations for more than a century. The Strait of Hormuz—long an artery for the world’s maritime economy—is now a monument to a new global disorder. In the coming days, negotiations in Pakistan may offer hope to stranded sailors. But what’s not on the horizon, according to seafarers, shipowners, naval analysts and historians who spoke to the Journal, is a return to maritime normalcy.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

The era of free seas is unraveling—and now everyone’s going to pay. 


As sailors stuck at sea near the Strait of Hormuz digested Trump’s cease-fire announcement, Iranian officials stressed they would determine which ships could leave, and at what price. This “Tehran toll booth” took effect <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktgn-hrkusddg-a%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce7290dfe1767424bbc4808de97c081af%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115050242361702%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0Rt6nYgIWKTrXrpLp6vOIVLFHiWf79f4JsAyOsKpbDc%3D&reserved=0>  as the U.S. Navy watched on, an admission that America no longer rules the waves, at least here and now in the world’s oil corridor. The strait, sailors said, risks becoming a graveyard for a trading system so integral to the modern economy that most consumers take it for granted, report Drew Hinshaw, Joe Parkinson and Daniel Michaels. Whatever happens next, the precedent of a toll booth in open waters will reverberate across a world order the U.S. helped build.

Big Pharma is turning to China for the newest drug ideas. 


The country, a backwater for drug research not long ago, is now a major player in biotechnology <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktgn-hrkusddg-f%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce7290dfe1767424bbc4808de97c081af%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115050242382861%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=uGl7Jo2VZCsY4H%2FbdMtpmDtW32haZVv3tbwwoQPL9w0%3D&reserved=0> . Looking to tap into the innovation, Western and Japanese drugmakers made 70 transactions with Chinese biotechs last year, paying nearly $5.6 billion upfront to get rights to promising molecules, according to industry intelligence firm Evaluate. Biotech is one of the advanced technologies that China has designated a national priority, and Chinese drug research threatens to soon overtake the West’s, reports Peter Loftus. Its rapid progress bodes well for patients: Not only does China promise a new source of lifesaving medicines, but a less expensive supply, too.

EXPERT TAKE

5


Q: North Korea is stronger than ever. Has American Christianity played a role in its endurance? 


WSJ’s China bureau chief, Jonathan Cheng, wrote about how American Christianity helped shape a lasting cult of personality <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gktgn-hrkusddg-yd%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Ce7290dfe1767424bbc4808de97c081af%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639115050242484360%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=1xc%2F%2B4tT0vmZeotmlKBTs%2BbL8P6OSTcjDPUd6GGv02Q%3D&reserved=0>  around Pyongyang's Eternal Leader, in an essay adapted from his forthcoming book.

A: In the short history of world Communism, North Korea has always stood apart.

While Stalin’s Soviet Union is gone and Mao Zedong’s China has liberalized and integrated itself into the global economy, North Korea is stronger than ever. How did that happen?

Pyongyang’s ruling Kim dynasty defied Soviet efforts to curb the idolization of leaders and deftly navigated a vicious fight between its patrons in Moscow and Beijing, emerging as a lone, grim success story among the former socialist allies.

Most crucially, Kim Il Sung built up an extraordinary cult of personality around himself that was durable enough to hand down to his son and then his grandson, the current leader Kim Jong Un. Now, with Kim Jong Un’s daughter ever-present at his side, the dynasty is positioned to stretch well beyond its eight decades.

Although North Korea has relentlessly suppressed religion and vilified American missionaries, the origins of this hereditary cult are found in a surprising place: Protestant Christianity, and in particular, postbellum American Presbyterianism.

After Kim’s death, in 1994, his son and successor Kim Jong Il made his father North Korea’s “Eternal President,” allowing him to rule in perpetuity over a country that had, in effect, become one with its founder. These developments, which looked so little like Communism and so much like religion, appalled Kim Il Sung’s former socialist backers.

That was especially so because it resembled a religion that had once held such a firm grip on northern Korea. In the 1930s, Christianity was so dominant in Pyongyang that the city acquired a nickname: the “Jerusalem of the East.” Although Kim would later obscure and distort the impact Christianity had on his thinking, in hindsight its imprint on his life is unmistakable.

I often return to these lines from David Ferry’s translation of Horace: “It’s true that Jupiter brings on the hard winters; / It’s also true that Jupiter takes them away.”

Certainty is easier. April, in much of the country, is liminal, vacillating between winter and spring, refusing to resolve cleanly. If you look closely, you can observe this tension: the tulips quivering in the gusting wind; people in shorts and people wearing mittens on the same block; stepping onto the porch to see a robin and instead seeing your own breath. The internal work is much the same. Sitting quietly, paying close attention to the weather inside, you can observe the hope that blows in with the fear, the lightness and heaviness that seem to be competing. Hi team!  <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/smile.png?v=15> 

We want to share with you the critically important that we received for the vs-1773621861-image-editing-conversation-v2 project (the client sent this feedback today).
Since it’s possible that this project is coming back again, it’s really important that you carefully review the feedback and apply it to your tasks.

	 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/warning.png?v=15> This project may only appear for a group of Annotators. If this project doesn’t appear on your Multimango dashboard, there’s no need to report it as a technical issue; you can disregard this announcement and continue working normally on your available projects.

________________________________


 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/police_car_light.png?v=15> CRITICAL FEEDBACK


Overly technical / unnatural prompting


*	We’re still seeing lots of prompts referring hex codes, opacity, tool-specific terms, avoid this and instead describe edits in human language.


Unrequested edits/workflow mistakes


*	Submission tasks allows extra changes without request, template handling issues, previous turn image included, Canva screenshots. This is unacceptable – changes must match the prompts.


Vague/Underspecified Instructions


*	Missing “where/which/how many/what color”, unclear prompts, and low variation.
*	Express clearly what the change would be, to which object it would be applied to, and how you would like it to be made.


Text quality/grammar/placeholders


*	This error includes typos, incorrect punctuation, grammar, or casing; placeholder text; and watermarks.
*	Ensure the quality of the text by paying attention to grammar and writing, and ensure the quality of the images by removing watermarks and placeholders.
*	Quality must be flawless.


Instruction/Prompt Implementation


*	Errors include requests that were not implemented, incorrect results, and instructions that were only partially followed.
*	Task submissions must correctly match the instructions requested in the prompts.

 <https://emoji.discourse-cdn.com/twitter/white_check_mark.png?v=15> TLDR: Remove ALL the placeholders before starting the conversation and triple-check your prompt is 100% aligned with the edited images.

I wrote in this newsletter last year about the dawn of A.I.-powered cybercrime <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2F6nBABw1E5svZ9hunBxF4qQ~~%2FAAAAARA~%2FwsFQsq23Y6dZQDMkorXBlLqCGfZxgQYMczOYaX88B_pa30JApuT-08PF3bw1qQ_EbSnaf9pCB_cGba_O07Pe2i-q_R7UKwH_8fnDDPQcQzoxUABzwLdjQaKTLLsRrwIZjM3Dv-dESI9cdfXyjQ5TSaCpXKepAIn8Phtzm5xbQNrl6yyrD3x-dk_qVSTQxfsP5lDFlBdY7varDFfjGZC1KjkSSYwlIu09WwZ2Ig6dPc2RDDe22ie0O4J3bzDwgj578f8m8gg3VRrKOPld7LFHvtpihg9O9rnpu1oeEjwJ7LOWN7rMdluplvF-qcrtiVqqboDRUy6SATR8dO_j6F4rLZcip1e6wQ3TT0KaU5od9Ro~&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C6091b7a516e04544f92f08de96eebdef%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639114149306934176%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=7OkS7Fmn0nGnbcSnxxOIlOOzQiduNUaEp5HcGeKQEkg%3D&reserved=0>  — of an age in which cybercriminals are robots and cyberdefenders are … also robots. Hordes of bad guys were suddenly using chatbots to turn out phishing scams and malware. Maybe the good guys could use the same tech to fend them off? Now, just nine months later, Mythos — a general-purpose A.I. model like the one your kid uses to cheat on English homework — has accomplished that feat.

But it’s not exactly reassuring. A.I. has gotten so deft on defense that it’s also a threat on offense. Anthropic focused on making a model that codes. But A.I. that’s good at coding is also good at spotting flaws in code, and competence cuts both ways.

Mythos is more trustworthy than its predecessors, but it’s not foolproof. And it’s so capable that when things go wrong, even a little wrong, they can go totally haywire.


Internet apocalypse


For decades, most hackers could hack most systems, but it was rarely worth their while. An A.I. like Mythos could change that calculus. It’s easy to imagine cybercriminals using these models to scope out the highest value vulnerabilities and dispatch automated grunts to exploit them en masse, at minimal cost.

In slowing down, Anthropic may be remembering old lessons. In 2019, OpenAI delayed a version of ChatGPT because it worried that the model would “generate deceptive, biased or abusive language at scale” — then proceeded to release models that did just that. This time, Anthropic shared Mythos with other companies to help them harden their defenses.

The Unfriendly Skies

 

Good news—airlines are going to be OK. The bad news: They’re just going to be OK.

 

No industry suffers more from a war in the Middle East, but it used to be worse. After a lousy investing experience in the 1990s, Warren Buffett quipped that “if there had been a capitalist at Kitty Hawk, he should have shot down Orville and done us all a favor.”

 

Then his company, Berkshire Hathaway, invested again 10 years ago <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45148863.464374%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9hcnRpY2xlcy93YXJyZW4tYnVmZmV0dHMtYmVya3NoaXJlLWhhdGhhd2F5LWRpc2Nsb3Nlcy1uZXctaW52ZXN0bWVudHMtaW4tYWlybGluZXMtMTQ3OTE1OTY0MT9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBbfb4ee51&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9a46e7d059f84030f7af08de96ee20d8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639114146677054436%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=b1exFbaGXnvm2Njbpb8h6huvoz9x7ok3vyfIWBw%2BDiA%3D&reserved=0>  after carriers merged and developed other revenue streams. Selling frequent-flier miles to credit card companies alone is lucrative enough that many airlines wouldn’t break even without it. Add to that “unbundled” items like bags, meals and seat choice.

 

This Wednesday Delta, the world’s most valuable airline, reported quarterly results and parted the clouds a bit <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45148863.464374%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2Uvc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LXRvZGF5LWRvdy1zcC01MDAtbmFzZGFxLTA0LTA4LTIwMjYvY2FyZC9kZWx0YS1jZW8tZW50aXJlLWluZHVzdHJ5LWlzLXRha2luZy1hY3Rpb24tb24tcmlzaW5nLWZ1ZWwtcHJpY2VzLWFHelVOZTdiUFBtUHFUWjQ0Y21mP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBd2a50c10&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9a46e7d059f84030f7af08de96ee20d8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639114146677067106%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=x3Unj92jgW3fiBt5sH5YlyKcOATWa5O0TMTlhRYP9Ho%3D&reserved=0> . Along with competitors, it’s raising bag fees <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45148863.464374%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9idXNpbmVzcy9haXJsaW5lcy9hbWVyaWNhbi1pcy10aGUtbGF0ZXN0LWFpcmxpbmUtdG8tcmFpc2UtYmFnZ2FnZS1mZWVzLWUyYzBiODk2P21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB5ad64152&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9a46e7d059f84030f7af08de96ee20d8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639114146677081087%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=6g4TM0GoRyXiL0QnB6yruOk2asj4guozcxOGS0Ax0qc%3D&reserved=0>  and fares and pruning less-profitable routes to cope with a doubling in jet fuel. That expense is a quarter to a third of airlines’ costs in normal times.

 

The longer disruptions last, the more capacity will have to fall worldwide, either by design or because people decide flying is too expensive. The blow to sales and income is bad, but not catastrophic.

 

Across a basket of 13 publicly traded airlines worldwide, analysts’ average 2026 earnings-per-share forecasts have fallen by 25% since December, and most are seen staying profitable. Revenue expectations rose 3% because, even with fewer flights, less is more.

 

Which brings us back to Buffett. Ruinous competition amid fixed costs bankrupted dozens of airlines in the 1980s and 1990s. Empty seats earn nothing so airlines undercut one another into the grave if they had expanded too quickly or if there was an economic shock.

 

Buffett bought several airline stocks when the business became more rational, but Covid-19 convinced him the industry wasn’t worth the headache. The industry’s average return on invested capital in 2025 was less than 7%, according to the International Air Transport Association.

Q: Why is gas still expensive if oil prices have fallen? 


Americans are staring down a harsh new reality despite the tentative cease-fire in the Middle East: $4 gasoline looks like it’s here to stay. Reporter David Uberti explains what to expect at the pumps: <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkjklc-hrkusddg-yd%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C15e9f2cb2b7d427567f108de96eb2671%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639114133872674336%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=IeaakhIgD1xEgOeb6aUZt9JoNk1BpuIso5NQ4X%2BMWBY%3D&reserved=0> 

A: Gas prices will likely take time to recede, even if Trump’s two-week pause on fighting holds. Drivers from Las Vegas to Seattle are now commonly shelling out $5 a gallon for gas, according to AAA, while prices in San Francisco and Los Angeles frequently top $6.

Average U.S. costs tracked by AAA reached $4.17 a gallon Thursday, the highest level since drones and missiles started flying. Drivers in Hawaii, Idaho and Utah have seen the biggest gas-price hikes over the past month.

After the cease-fire ignited one of the steepest one-day selloffs on record this week, front-month U.S. crude futures bounced back to nearly $98 a barrel yesterday.

Spot prices for real-world shipments of crude remained far more elevated, signaling a rush by refiners to lock in supplies. Bids on oil cargoes tracked by Argus Media on Wednesday reached as high as $145 a barrel.

The more refiners have to pay for crude deliveries, the more they have to charge for fuel, even if contracts for future oil shipments are cheap by comparison.

Analysts say average U.S. pump prices could drop a few cents a day if the strait reopens in earnest. But gas-station operators, whose margins shrink with quick climbs in wholesale costs, tend to lower prices more gradually while they sell expensive supplies after a shock.

Next Steps

Please complete this survey <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fbain.avature.net%2Fltrk%2FeyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6NTkwMTEyMSwiaGFzaCI6ImYzYjkwYjg5OGM5ZTkwMjUxOWIzNDk5ZGRlNDM2Y2NhMzY4MTA4MmJkMTc3ODlkNGY0YmM0MTZhM2QwYWRiMjYifQ.WwkXm9xsaZroTWTChWmJUq9GNkyokztOzWzpdHBkG_A&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2f8da7b64f5e4e8752c008de967167c2%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113611016510146%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=3%2FybH0KKeld7dhaDXi8cKpKCkP5li%2BknHSOEhEzvR9k%3D&reserved=0>  to confirm your availability and where you would be traveling from if invited to attend in-person final round interviews. This survey must be submitted before selecting your interview timeslot.


2. Select your interview timeslot


You will receive a separate email from our interview scheduling team by Friday, April 10. Please select your interview timeslot by Tuesday, April 14 at 3:00 PM EST. (This is the deadline to choose your time — not the interview date.) Timeslots are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, and we cannot guarantee availability outside of the provided dates.


For all scheduling related questions, contact the Interview Scheduling team <mailto:Bain.RecruitingInterviews@Bain.com> . Please include the position you are applying for and your recruiting office in the subject line.


Interview Format


First round interviews consist of two 30-minute case interviews (one hour total). The case interview is a business discussion between you and the interviewer based on common issues facing our clients. During the interview, your interviewer will provide details on the case, and you will be required to analyze the data and make a business recommendation.


To prepare, we recommend reviewing:

*	Interview preparation <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fbain.avature.net%2Fltrk%2FeyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6NTkwMTEyMSwiaGFzaCI6ImE2OWM1M2QwOTk3M2MyNDAxOGVlNmZmZThmMjNhNjc5MDQwMjIxNzQ1OThlZWI5ZGM2YmI3NmM0ZjdmNTQxOTYifQ.4zmibDKRVqfplrJkL4sWrCGKp6iWk6sSW6bw0SNmOLQ&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2f8da7b64f5e4e8752c008de967167c2%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113611016532863%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2BItZJwQp23L7Kk8lkFE4aijVdNjMjgzy9ozLBr%2FVTO8%3D&reserved=0>

Statistical Methods in Research
Fall 2026 House Course (0.5 credit, S/U)

Instructors: Liane Ma (lm487@duke.edu), Cooper Ruffing (ctr22@duke.edu) 
Faculty Sponsor: Dr. John Zito
Time/Location: Monday 7:00-8:30 PM, Old Chemistry 123

Course Description:
In this course, students will explore the statistical fundamentals necessary for understanding and conducting research in a variety of fields. Students will engage with real-world research papers and datasets across disciplines, exploring how statistics are used (and sometimes misused) in published work. Instead of focusing solely on technical skills, this course emphasizes interpretation, critique, and application of basic statistical tools in research. From misused methods to research bias, Statistical Methods in Research aims to provide students with a deeper understanding of when, why, and how to best utilize statistical methods in their future storytelling. The course culminates in student-led discussion, applying concepts from class. No previous experience is required in statistical science or research.

We aim to tailor the course to students' interests across disciplines, so please consider registering!

Reach out to ctr22@duke.edu or lm487@duke.edu if you have any questions!

Dear Graham,

 

The digital world is entering a phase of structural convergence, where sensing technologies, computing infrastructure, and intelligent systems are increasingly integrated into unified, real-time environments. What was once fragmented innovation is now evolving into interconnected systems capable of continuous operation and adaptation. 


This transition is reinforced by several major developments. The United Kingdom announced a $2.3 billion investment to advance quantum technology, aiming to deploy quantum computing at scale by the early 2030s and potentially add more than $200 billion to the economy by 2045. Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science demonstrated the ability to maneuver quantum sensors within biological environments using magnetic microbots, enabling real time, minimally invasive measurements inside living cells. At the same time, NVIDIA and Coherent Corp. formed a partnership to scale optical technologies for next generation data centers, with NVIDIA committing $2 billion to expand manufacturing, supply, and R and D capabilities.


These developments signal a broader transition from research to deployment. Innovation is increasingly focused on healthcare applications, AI infrastructure, and advanced data center systems, supported by growing investments in partnerships, manufacturing, and scalable technologies.


At the sensing layer, nano sensors and flexible and printed sensors are expanding across precision healthcare, in body diagnostics, wearables, and smart infrastructure. These technologies are being embedded into larger ecosystems, enabling continuous data capture and real time monitoring, and supporting a shift toward more responsive, data driven environments.


At the infrastructure level, AI factories and enterprise AI model training hubs are redefining how data is processed. These systems require advanced architectures, high throughput networking, and energy efficient design. Optical networking technologies are helping address data transmission bottlenecks as AI workloads scale in complexity.


The emergence of twin as a service and sensor driven digital twins is further accelerating this shift. These platforms enable real time simulation, predictive maintenance, and operational optimization across industries, including manufacturing, infrastructure, and smart buildings.


From a market perspective, competition is moving from products to platforms. Growth is increasingly driven by energy efficiency, AI optimization, and integrated solutions. Customers are favouring subscription-based models and end to end platforms over standalone tools.


However, scaling these systems introduces constraints. Power availability is emerging as a defining limitation, as rising compute demand places pressure on grid infrastructure and increases energy costs. In response, companies are investing in renewable energy, advanced nuclear solutions, and more efficient cooling systems.


Large scale infrastructure investments highlight the magnitude of this shift. SoftBank Group is planning a new AI data center in Ohio with potential demand of 10 gigawatts and total investment exceeding tens of billions of dollars across computing and power infrastructure. Supporting this, American Electric Power is investing $4.2 billion in grid upgrades. At the same time, the transition toward liquid cooling systems is accelerating, with Ecolab moving to acquire CoolIT Systems for approximately $4.75 billion to support high density AI workloads.


Supply chain constraints are adding further pressure. Shortages of semiconductors, rare earth materials, and advanced chips are impacting manufacturing timelines, while capacity limitations at major foundries such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company are intensifying as demand for AI chips continues to grow.
Looking ahead, the focus will shift toward scaling deployment. Quantum sensors are moving toward real time applications, supported by investments such as Canada’s National Research Council committing over $900 million. Continued expansion of AI infrastructure, energy systems, and cooling technologies will play a critical role in enabling growth.


What is emerging is a digital ecosystem where sensors collect data, AI factories process it, and digital twins and intelligent systems act on it in real time. This marks a shift from static infrastructure to dynamic, interconnected platforms capable of continuous optimization.


This is the moment when the market is evolving into a connected system where sensors gather data, data centers process it, and digital twins assist with real time decisions.

A Better Investing Mousetrap?

 

This has been a good year for value stocks <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45128182.456379%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL3N0b2Nrcy9vbmUtb2YtdGhlLXN0b2NrLW1hcmtldHMtbGFzdC1oYXZlbnMtaXMtbm93LWF0LXJpc2stN2FhODRlNWQ_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBf0342e1e&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8ce4418719e34918d32408de96256158%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113284458093519%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=FkCm7aCY6zEK8LprqLzERHkI38OBD9P%2Fjg9I7CnFTGA%3D&reserved=0> —relatively speaking, at least.

 

An energy shock and a major selloff in software companies over AI-replacement fears <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45128182.456379%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS90ZWNoL2FpL2JyZWFraW5nLWRvd24tdGhlLXZpcmFsLW1lbW8tdGhhdC1zcG9va2VkLW1hcmtldHMtYmMwODhjODM_bW9kPWRqZW1NYXJrZXRzQU0%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBd58cb160&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8ce4418719e34918d32408de96256158%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113284458114714%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=alPqz4x1in%2BnYNMazOid%2BeF2sww1tsoxxsUn0EQgaTY%3D&reserved=0>  will do that. Maybe value can continue to beat growth, but there are speedier steeds in the investing-factor horse race.

 

Of those two well-known styles, growth is the recent standout and the easier of the two to define. How quickly are sales and earnings growing and does the stock have momentum? It wins in a straightaway sprint.

 

Value is by far the long-distance champ, though. Its problem lately isn’t so much being out of fashion as how it’s measured.

 

Back when America was a mostly industrial economy, acolytes of Benjamin Graham, notably Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Warren Buffett, ran circles around competitors by owning stocks that were cheap on paper.

 

Buffett surprised many when he bought seemingly pricey Coca-Cola shares in the late 1980s and early 1990s. He grasped that its brand was a wonderful asset not reflected on its balance sheet. Around that time, academics formally described <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45128182.456379%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanN0b3Iub3JnL3N0YWJsZS8yMzI5MTEyP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBfb6dc511&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8ce4418719e34918d32408de96256158%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113284458135984%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=x%2BrAn1a1317qPi2L58QimfDehhTLYb6G9FKCC3T7b7Y%3D&reserved=0>  the value premium, basing it on simple accounting measures.

One likely reason growth trounced value in most years since the financial crisis is that it had the highest portfolio overlap with a factor better than either one—quality plus free cash flow.

 

Companies like Visa, Apple, Nvidia, Johnson & Johnson and Microsoft are able to generate a lot of excess cash, but they also make high returns on what they reinvest. Together, this has made them standouts.

 

That combination is reflected in the S&P 500 Quality FCF Aristocrats Index <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F45128182.456379%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3BnbG9iYWwuY29tL3NwZGppL2VuL2luZGljZXMvZGl2aWRlbmRzLWZhY3RvcnMvc3AtNTAwLXF1YWxpdHktZmNmLWFyaXN0b2NyYXRzLWluZGV4LyNvdmVydmlldz9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBfb5f5e64&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C8ce4418719e34918d32408de96256158%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113284458191598%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=q1ful%2B%2FF73MaSYbnl4UrP1KuIGWx7DNkKAXndJ5h43s%3D&reserved=0> , created in 2024 and reconstructed for these calculations. Like the similarly named Dividend Aristocrats, it rewards consistency—at least 10 straight years of positive free cash flow—in addition to a high free cash flow margin and a high free cash flow return on invested capital.

 

While the index is no household name, investors have bid up many stocks with those winning qualities. Buffett has said he regretted not selling Coca-Cola when it got expensive. A wobbly truce


How steady is the cease-fire in the Middle East? Israeli missiles have continued to fall on Lebanon, Iran threatens a military response, and shippers are confused about the status of the Strait of Hormuz. The United States and Iran don’t even agree on what it will take to open peace talks.

Both sides have declared victory in the conflict. The United States has destroyed most of Iran’s navy and reduced its ability to shoot missiles across the region. But President Trump’s other goals remain unrealized <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2Fq-z86r9-mk9Z9BV3t6lMyQ~~%2FAAAAARA~%2F0ZxIT5UlKXtzR-VCVf7XUTH4OAgs9UfEZgn1iNSBkVJoTrBZ9PFkZJAgE-eTThE2crPMkW-LVRZHFuhqt6IzpmswL0j-A3QDnwPMEvXF8RrV6ZGr8pRp4hdVFdCNLPS_Ye__Fff-fYstJC3OvVVT5n3YhoiwG4CtAS6dAPzKt3vpTGFQ_uTA2TQS4-Aof-cCbyiswE1zo_um-eUfW7k7TvOPvefezHxy_24vivVA72U3Gma7hxe7fJhGwXsP9xWN0tUHjfZ96Jotcq19Gn9LlUljNsZOhB6AhXSH90eEE6dlSKm7QAIXxv_MoGqp1NVTy3BJSw875c_-6gersvibkmHrcqQwKvPLgx71nhyxvog~&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C5805dcf4a40f49d8746608de9623df5a%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113278008827199%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=oLIjeAalFIlXI179C8QjvyBnnP4v7Gi0v995wFQgGec%3D&reserved=0> . Iran still has uranium to make a bomb someday; it still guides regional militias like Hezbollah; its regime still holds power and crushes dissent.

And Iran, for its part, now has total control of the strait.


What could end the war?


White House officials say talks are expected to begin between the two nations on Saturday, brokered by Pakistan. They are likely to be contentious.

Among other things in its 10-point proposal <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnl.nytimes.com%2Ff%2Fnewsletter%2FyhBE4WfKGevEz2sxBD4G_g~~%2FAAAAARA~%2FkbrX8_6lfjIOXdDWDxk6dOXsI2bjRxf9aecOo6J6Ki58rHudkzpKs_71nelwZVDckJ7Eh0NLkakBGxgneJ1Cc0Nv0qBtbld2Y-SGdvroXzHlzTXKzCP_Kwvg_b39TW9a6cTe59G-HLEwP1CkGzIreIfF8yCPpAdiDivtrlhBOegjAPDJutL0wPWS15ZtDPnH8G9uPlecqRoXOmtpXCc7xxYrEr_3MiQbJpnT7zsRjl7FViZLI5lmmUq_HQPsvd7UicWZA6_pTEaJJFmgRpDINmFWa6m8REY_MSwfoLjsaXg0_q_tPXfV8XZXrVie0bUOGqXSiNNrvlaXascnJBMqmcnZJ0BmPpqrBLlkD5G0EiRC-YARb-RIxbOOa1q3KRgmWD9sQ_GceJIy9quQDPR2zQ~~&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C5805dcf4a40f49d8746608de9623df5a%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113278008841920%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=2Y%2FPGHgLbi3yLpVyRfUzoOokSXr8B%2ByVfoPJXSvt544%3D&reserved=0> , Iran wants to maintain its control of the strait, the narrow passage through which a fifth of the world’s oil usually flows. Iran’s chokehold on it during the war has damaged the global economy. “It is very unlikely that Washington or Iran’s Gulf Arab neighbors would accept this,” my colleague Erika Solomon reports.

Iran also wants Americans gone from the region. It wants reparations to pay for damages. And it wants the U.S. to accept Iran’s right to enrich uranium.

That’s not going to happen. The United States has bases across the Persian Gulf states, Israel and Iraq. The administration is unlikely to pay to rebuild Iran. And as for its nuclear ambitions, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said at a news conference yesterday that the United States could send Special Operations troops to seize the fissile material. “If we have to, we can do it in any means necessary,” he said.


What’s happening inside Iran?

The United States and Israel have killed scores of Iranian leaders and bombed the country’s military infrastructure to rubble. But as Yeganeh Torbati and Erika report, Iran’s leaders may now see themselves in a stronger position than they were when the war started.

Who is in charge now? The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, has not been seen in public since taking office. His absence, Yeganeh reports, has fueled speculation that the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps — ideologically hard-lined masters of asymmetric warfare — are running Iran.

There was relief, but also shock and a sense of foreboding. Armed pro-government militia members have established checkpoints on Tehran’s streets.

“The cease-fire was announced in a way that made it feel like the people were left on their own, facing a repressive regime alone,” a doctor living in the northeast of the country told The Times. “Ordinary people are very worried about the future and have less hope for change compared to before the war started.”

Still, Trump’s threat to wipe out the country’s “whole civilization” was on pause. “I feel better today compared to yesterday,” one resident of Tehran told The Times.


What’s next?


Whether or not the cease-fire folds, the nations of the Persian Gulf now have to re-evaluate their relationships with Israel, Iran and the U.S., my colleague Vivian Nereim reported. “Politicians, investors and residents in wealthy cities like Dubai and Doha once believed they were essentially immune to the region’s conflicts,” she wrote. “The American-Israeli war with Iran has smashed that assumption.”

Their oil fields were exposed to attacks, as were their water desalination plants, their hotels, their airports. And those attacks continued yesterday after the announcement of the cease-fire.

“In truth, one of the most significant outcomes of this war is the shattering of the concept of a regional security system in the Gulf,” a spokesman for Qatar’s foreign ministry said last month. “The security framework in the Gulf was based on certain axioms. Q: What is the framework for negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, and are the talks likely to bridge the gaps between the two sides? 


Iran and the U.S. have a meeting tentatively scheduled for Saturday in Islamabad. Vice President JD Vance will lead the U.S. delegation. Pakistan, Egypt and Turkey have been mediating. WSJ’s Michael Amon and David S. Cloud explain what to expect <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gkjjidk-hrkusddg-jl%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cbafabca4fa044cf41b6208de9621710b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639113267553842300%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=xiLGvzjN6m1bZjnLfolu9K53PZJRlGs%2FQMEFVx%2FJw20%3D&reserved=0>  from the talks:

A: Trump has said a 10-point Iranian plan would form the basis for the talks, though he has also said that Iran has already agreed to many elements of a separate 15-point U.S. plan that calls for sweeping concessions by Tehran.

Iran hasn’t released its proposal, but a 10-point plan published in state media included guarantees that the U.S. and Israel won’t attack, retaining control of the Strait of Hormuz, allowing Iran to enrich uranium, sanctions relief and the withdrawal of all U.S. combat forces from the Middle East.

Most of Iran’s demands have been called nonstarters for the U.S. and Israel. Iran has likewise called the U.S. plan, which calls for Iran to give up nuclear enrichment and accept limits on its missile arsenal, unacceptable.

The White House has said in recent days that talks on narrowing the gaps were making progress. It played down Trump’s comment that the 10-point Iranian plan would form the basis for the talks, saying Trump was speaking about a blueprint with different elements than those Iran has outlined publicly.

The differences between the Iranian and U.S. public positions are huge. For that reason, some analysts believe the likely outcome is a narrow agreement that halts the fighting but leaves many of the major issues unresolved.

Subject: Application to Delphi!
Body:
Hey Graham!
 
Thank you for applying for the Operations Intern at Delphi. We really appreciate your interest in joining our team. Our team is reviewing your application. 
 
If you're invited to next steps, Delphi's interview process is as follows: 

1.	
	Behavioural Interview - if we think your profile matches what we are looking for, we will schedule a longer behavioural interview with a member of our Executive Team. 
2.	
	Skill Assessment - if we think you would contribute to the Delphi culture and raise the bar, we will invite you to a technical or skills assessment. 
3.	
	Onsite - if you pass that stage, we will have you come onsite to our office in Jackson Square, SF. This is to see if Delphi is a good fit for you, and ensure you are a good fit for Delphi

We’re excited about the possibility of working together.
 
Take care,
Delphi Team

Are you interested in sports, healthcare, or how elite athletes recover from injury?? Join us on Tuesday, March 24th from 7-8 PM in Teer 203 for a night inside the world of sports medicine.

5. Come Watch Ragtime!


Ragtime is a sweeping musical adaptation of E.L. Doctorow’s novel that follows three fictional families in pursuit of the American Dream at the dawn of the 20th Century: Black pianist Coalhouse Walker, Jr. and his beloved Sarah, Jewish immigrant Tateh and his little girl, and a wealthy white family led by matriarch Mother. All grasping for the same dream, if only they can hold on to it. 

Hoof 'n' Horn is committed to being an anti-racist and accessible organization. Ragtime contains graphic depictions of racism, antisemitism, violence, police brutality, and other forms of prejudice, including the use of racial and ethnic slurs (including the n-word and antisemitic slurs). These elements are presented as part of the historical realities portrayed in the work and do not reflect the values of our organization. 

This production was developed with guidance from faculty and scholars, including members of the African and African American Studies and Theater Studies departments, as well as consultation with the Mary Lou Williams Center for Black Culture, to approach this material with responsibility.

Event run time: 2 hours 45 minutes, with one 10-minute intermission

Subject: Thank you for your interest in Harris Williams
Body:
Dear Graham 

Thank you for your interest in Harris Williams recent opening for the position of 2027 M&A Summer Analyst (SF) . Although every submission of interest is appreciated, we have decided to pursue other applicants for this position.

Harris Williams gives careful consideration to every candidate and takes great care to match applicants with positions that will result in mutual success. The choice between the many qualified candidates is a difficult one; regrettably, this position did not result in the mutual fit we strive for.

We continually evaluate our need for talented employees and new opportunities arise frequently. These opportunities will be posted under the “Careers” section at www.harriswilliams.com. We encourage you to visit periodically to check for updates. Now that your profile is in our system, applying for a different position is simple.

Again, thank you for your interest in joining the Harris Williams. We wish you success as you continue your job search.

Sincerely,

Harris Williams
1001 Haxall Point
Richmond, VA 23219

Body:
<https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/markets-discussion-group> The last Markets Discussion Group of the semester is tonight, 5-6 PM in Gray 228! The big topics will be Iran, oil, and the Fed.

 

REGISTER <https://dukefinance.wufoo.com/forms/zol42eh0zyitrq/>

How to Answer “Walk Me Through a Deal”

If you’re recruiting for investment banking, there’s one question you’re almost guaranteed to get: 

“Walk me through a deal.”

It’s the question that tests your curiosity, your understanding of real transactions, and ultimately, how prepared you are for the analyst role. That’s why we created a new article breaking down exactly how to approach it. 

In this article, you’ll learn:

*	Why bankers ask this question and what they’re really evaluating 

*	The 5 W framework for structuring your answer 

*	How to speak confidently without pretending to be an M&A expert 

*	Common mistakes to avoid, especially when choosing which deal to discuss 

Here are a few actionable tips you can apply right away:

*	Pick a deal you genuinely understand. Don’t choose one where the interviewer may be a deep expert. 

*	Start with the facts. Getting the basics right shows judgment and prevents you from sounding overconfident. 

*	Use the 5 W’s. It’s the simplest way to build a clear, structured, and compelling answer. 

*	Show curiosity, not mastery. You don’t need to be right, but you need to be logical. 

*	Read beyond the headlines. Bankers can tell immediately who actually follows deal activity. 

If you want to stand out, mastering this one question will give you a real edge.

Good morning. Energy facilities have become major targets in the war, and the markets don’t like it. The price of oil is now up more than 48 percent since the war began.

There’s more news from the Middle East below. But before those updates, I want to tell you about a major Times investigation into a labor rights icon.

	
	
	
 <https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/03/17/multimedia/19themorning-nl-chavez/19themorning-nl-chavez-jumbo.jpg> 	
Cesar Chavez during a demonstration in New York in 1969. John Sotomayor/The New York Times	

A tarnished legacy


Cesar Chavez rose from the poverty of Arizona’s agricultural fields to shape America’s labor movement. He co-founded the nation’s first successful union of farm workers and championed the Latino working class. Chavez’s name is emblazoned on streets, schools, parks and monuments across the United States. In California, many schools close on Cesar Chavez Day, March 31, his birthday.

Now, more than 30 years after Chavez’s death, a Times investigation reveals that at the same time that he was working to better the lives of immigrant workers, Chavez sexually abused and assaulted women and girls. The victims include Dolores Huerta, who founded the United Farm Workers union with Chavez and was for decades his most prominent ally. Huerta, now 95, told The Times that Chavez raped her in 1966. It was a secret she had kept for nearly 60 years.

“Unfortunately, he used some of his great leadership to abuse women and children — it’s really awful,” Huerta told The Times.


What to know


The Times found extensive evidence that Chavez sexually abused two teenage girls in the 1970s. Ana Murguia, now 66, met Chavez when she was 8 and he was in his 40s. She said Chavez molested her in his office. The abuse started when she was 13 and ended four years later, she said. Debra Rojas, also 66, was 12 when Chavez first fondled her breasts in his office. When she was 15, he had sex with her — rape, under California law. A line from The Times’s reporting: “He told her that he had known they belonged together since he saw her at the age of 9.”

Both women struggled in the years that followed the abuse: depression, panic attacks, substance abuse. They kept silent, they said, out of fear that the accusations would tarnish Chavez’s legacy. In recent months, though, after talking with Times reporters, they came to believe that their stories mattered as much as his.

 <https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/03/17/multimedia/19themorning-nl-chavez1/19themorning-nl-chavez1-jumbo.jpg> 	
Cesar Chavez, left, and Ana Murguia, center, in 1975. Murguia said Chavez abused her when she was a girl. Cathy Murphy/Getty Images	

Dolores Huerta had two children by Chavez. Huerta told The Times she had felt pressured to have sex with him in a hotel room during a work trip in 1960. Six years later, he raped her in a car parked in a secluded grape field, she said. She told The Times she did not report the assault to the authorities because of the police’s antagonism toward the labor movement and because she feared her union would not believe her. Both encounters resulted in pregnancies. Huerta hid them by wearing baggy clothes, she told The Times, and arranged to have the babies raised by others.

“I have kept this secret long enough. My silence ends here,” Huerta said yesterday afternoon, in her first comments since the publication of the investigation.

Chavez pursued or harassed other women in the movement. The Times spoke to at least a dozen of them. Some of them chose to speak on the record, while others preferred to remain anonymous.

Several relatives and union members knew about Chavez’s behavior. They talked to Chavez’s son, Paul Chavez, about it in the early 2000s. “It was unimaginable to me, just hard to process,” he recalled thinking. “You’re talking about my dad.”

The fallout has been swift. States, cities and the United Farm Workers of America canceled upcoming marches and celebrations of Chavez. Arizona’s governor said that her state would stop recognizing his birthday as a holiday. The U.S. Department of Labor has an auditorium named in his honor — an American flag now hangs over the door, covering his name.

The Times investigation was thorough. It took nearly five years. Our reporters corroborated victims’ claims by speaking to more than 60 people close to Chavez and the union. They reviewed hundreds of pages of records, confidential emails, photographs and audio recordings of union meetings.


A reporter’s reflection


Manny Fernandez is one of the reporters on the investigation. Manny’s a California native, born and raised in Fresno. He went to Fresno State. His grandparents on both his mother’s and his father’s sides started out as farmworkers, working the very fields Chavez organized. That weighed on him, he told me yesterday.

“It didn’t distract me from doing the work,” he said. “It was just an irony that I’m the guy from The Times who’s doing this, who’s from here, who understands the legacy of Chavez, which in California cannot be overstated.”

“He represented the best of us — and by us, I mean Latino America,” Manny continued. “And to discover that Chavez had this dark side is disturbing. But we do need to know who our heroes are.”

Falling Knives

 

Even before Middle East chaos sent it on a roller-coaster ride this month, the stock market was unusually choppy beneath the surface. The expanding abilities of artificial intelligence <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F44787480.471390%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL2ludmVzdGluZy9zb2Z0d2FyZS1zbHVtcC1kcmFncy1kb3duLXByaXZhdGUtZnVuZC1tYW5hZ2Vycy02Zjg0MGQwYz9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB5c7745a6&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ccd8220f85f4d213dc008de85a35ac8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095133815860597%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=QNUkQcpL4RyefDTleUKuBRuUdc6E1FOEitQ4Uv1tBNM%3D&reserved=0>  sent one blue-chip company’s shares after another sharply lower.

 

A typical headline when that happens goes something like “XYZ stock plunges on massive selling.” Of course, every share dumped found a buyer who thought it was attractive at the suddenly discounted price. Were they making a mistake?

 

One of the oldest pieces of Wall Street wisdom—that you should never try to catch a falling knife—says they mostly were. A mountain of academic data agrees.

 

Alexander Hübbert, a quantitative researcher working on his Ph.D. at Stockholm University, ran some numbers recently that make it crystal clear. He looked at 4,174 British stocks between 2000 and 2026 that had just dropped varying amounts by the end of a month from their all-time highs—five, 10, 15, 20 percent, and so on—and then measured how they did versus the broad market over the following 12 months.

 

It’s ugly. A stock with a 5% drawdown then underperformed by an average of 6 percentage points; a 10% drawdown by 8.6 percentage points; and a 15% drawdown by 12 percentage points. The faster knives fell, the deeper the wounds.

 

Momentum is one of the most consistent investing trends both on the way up and down. Other models that look at buying stocks near their 52-week lows have similarly dismal results to what Hübbert observed. 

 

Naturally there are exceptions. In his book “Mastering the Market Cycle, <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F44787480.471390%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9hcnRpY2xlcy9tYXN0ZXJpbmctdGhlLW1hcmtldC1jeWNsZS1yZXZpZXctdGhlLWRhbmdlcnMtb2Ytb3B0aW1pc20tMTUzOTAzOTQyOD9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB9e304588&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ccd8220f85f4d213dc008de85a35ac8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095133815875743%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=g9gOoV08WytTHxKn2HARAlXKZVJdzzSgheKWzKCA7PM%3D&reserved=0> ” veteran investor Howard Marks, co-founder of Oaktree Capital Management, writes about catching falling knives and says most professionals are too scared to buy when a stock or bond is still plunging. 

 

The only problem is that “when the dust has settled and investors’ nerves have steadied, the bargains will be gone.”

 

Marks has an exemplary track record of his own in distressed-credit investing and is one of the few people whose writings Warren Buffett says he reads. But that highlights the difference between blindly buying some brand-name stock after it plunges and having a sophisticated view of what it’s worth despite the news: You’re not Warren Buffett.

 

“The young man knows the rules, but the old man knows the exceptions.”

Q: How is a tighter job market affecting workers’ pay? 


The corporate ladder feels more like a slide to people whose roles are being devalued <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-ghddthk-hrkusddg-yd%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C91f4cc0b2baf4c0ccada08de85a153d8%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095125422230095%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=SI4wn%2BwWiiDeJGRTHE%2FCjpg36EBCzSF0AAYLGwxvX40%3D&reserved=0>  in today’s cooler job market, writes columnist Callum Borchers.

A: While some Americans are still upping their earnings, federal data show overall wage growth has been slowing since 2022. More than a quarter of people who recently switched jobs took pay cuts, according to ZipRecruiter.

A compensation reset was probably inevitable after companies hoarded talent and dangled big raises a few years ago. Still, the job-market correction is sharper than a lot of workers and economists expected amid breathless hype about AI.

The job switchers’ premium has been dwindling for a while. Early this year it shrank to 1.9 percentage points, according to payroll software provider ADP, the smallest since 2020.

Job seekers aren’t the only ones feeling downward pressure on salaries. People who are employed can’t assume the customary pay bump is coming this year.

Client surveys from consulting firm Korn Ferry indicate an average raise this year will be 3.2% to 3.6%, but there may be a wide range. Highly valued employees could receive 1.5-to-2 times that amount. Others might get little or nothing.

At the same time, bonuses are shrinking, and fewer employees are receiving them, according to ADP.

It’s a commentary on how bosses view their charges at the moment. Managers are focused on retaining key players; just about everyone else is replaceable.

Duke University and Duke University Health System have announced a new HomeGrown <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fmx6ysac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514279035%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2BsQt6yOIF%2Bfs2p8%2BENYxd3gH%2FodT%2FoduDyJiQiuo724%3D&reserved=0>  initiative, which will direct $203 million over three years to expand local hiring, spend more with Durham and Triangle businesses, and invest in affordable housing. 
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 
	
 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2F2p7ysac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514302054%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=UmAplFRrKTxxEP6PARgp6nBIiNJUUYs072WooXxDJTY%3D&reserved=0> 

Can you use that word in a sentence? <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fii8ysac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514326435%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=FyBr%2FupeQj05HmmHVknxZ0vmClMmBXZNQVpGN9pMyXs%3D&reserved=0> 

Eleven-year-old Sophie Sung of Bahama, N.C., won by spelling “aurora.” Duke sponsors the bee for elementary and middle school students from Durham Public Schools, Chapel Hill-Carrboro City Schools and Orange County Schools.
	
 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fya9ysac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514353893%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=jyZny0VOFs2zAsFZlD8OOsdR%2FZInYxVLrBB6Hd4esDw%3D&reserved=0> 

How they found stability through StepUp Durham <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fe39ysac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514380967%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Z25oWrtE7JsFmBBwEjaJm31%2BTueYA5UOXdbiZHyQdlY%3D&reserved=0> 

Launched in 2015 with Duke as an early sponsor, StepUp Durham supports Durham community members facing barriers to employment by providing training, resources and personal coaching to help them secure a stable job and grow personally.
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 

Piecing together the work of a Durham artist <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fuvazsac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514465547%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=3xpsIDRJ2KU6v5YT6eVpMiLugVeEWl6OxtfhImrSqH0%3D&reserved=0> 


Students developed an exhibition on Silvia Heyden at the Nasher Museum of Art through a curatorial design course. Heyden made Durham her home for decades; the exhibition features pieces shaped by local music, landscapes and daily life. 
 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Faobzsac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514526262%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=93VFj6mJiM1SCzJSBDC0F%2Fwp3MK6U6NMvlA5yulVTRg%3D&reserved=0> 
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 

Duke doctor wants to restore Durham’s tree canopy <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fi6ukjt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fqgczsac&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C42ff1cae00874973179f08de859fc92d%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639095118514562680%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=scVZun7%2FRXbvNwyweo7ZfkBn%2BDT%2FVsDPIQJyhQ%2FhVP0%3D&reserved=0>

Emergency pediatrician Dr. Clay Bordley at Duke University Hospital raised trees on his 28-acre Panther Creek Forest Farm in Durham County. Now he’s giving them all away for free to anyone willing to plant them.  “Every tree I grow is given back to the people of Durham so they can help the environment, provide shade and make people’s health better,” Bordley said.
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 
	

	“It will take EMS about eight to 10 minutes to get to the scene. If we’re going to treat within two to five minutes, it is the community member that matters so much.”

Subject: NSA Science of Security Initiative - Symposium
Body:
From Kim - 


The National Security Agency Research Directorate sponsors the Science of Security Initiative https://sos-vo.org/ to promote foundational cybersecurity science that is needed to mature the cybersecurity discipline and to underpin advances in cyber defense. The SoS initiative works in several ways. 1. Engage the academic community for foundational research, 2. Promote rigorous scientific principles, and 3. grow the SoS community. The SoS Virtual Organization is the SoS’s initiative online home.
 SOS is sponsoring an online symposium on April 14-16.  Details and registration links are below.



Dear Science of Security Community Members,

The 2026 schedule is now available for the 13th Annual Hot Topics in the Science of Security (HoTSoS) Symposium: https://sos-vo.org/group/hotsos/agenda <https://click.mlsend.com/link/c/YT0yOTYzNTQ1MDc1MDEyODY4NjEwJmM9eTd5MSZlPTAmYj0xNTI1NzE4MjU1JmQ9ajZjM3YyaA==.PY8Sn5pqsmDBPd43fbgpYBFGweprA7bL0G2HpAi1rwc> 

The symposium is free to attend, but you must register by EOD April 13, 2026: https://sos-vo.org/group/hotsos/registration <https://click.mlsend.com/link/c/YT0yOTYzNTQ1MDc1MDEyODY4NjEwJmM9eTd5MSZlPTAmYj0xNTI1NzE4MjU2JmQ9cDRnM2wxdQ==.sDEtIvuN4eHl_YRTdaivhiJ5hQlzHmDTvJ5f75SwaYg>  

The 2026 HoTSoS event, scheduled for April 14-16, 2026, will bring together researchers from diverse disciplines to promote the advancement of work related to the Science of Security. The virtual symposium will feature invited talks, work-in-progress papers, work-already-published papers, and posters and demos. 

We are pleased to announce the following keynote speakers:

Taesoo Kim (Georgia Tech)
Deian Stefan (UC San Diego)
Bo Li (UIUC)

Should you have any questions, please contact the conference organizers at hotsos2026@sos-vo.org <mailto:hotsos2026@sos-vo.org> .

Sincerely,
HotSoS 2026 Organizers

General Chair: Adam Tagert (National Security Agency)
Program Chairs: Benjamin Erichson (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and ICSI) and Jonathan Aldrich (Carnegie Mellon University)

____________________________________________________________________

Emma Rasiel, PhD, Associate Chair, Dept of Economics, Duke University

Richard Y. Li Professor of the Practice

Social Science Building, 228D (in the DFE Center)

Duke Financial Economics Center <http://www.econ.duke.edu/dfe> 

Walk-in Office Hours: see my website <http://people.duke.edu/~ebr4/erasiel.htm> .

Thank you, and we look forward to hearing back from you.

Sincerely, 


Credit Agricole CIB Early Careers

✏️ President Trump saw the Supreme Court as an ally. That sense of harmony shattered yesterday. A decision that struck down the president’s global tariffs marked his biggest high-court defeat <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkdhd-hrkusddg-h%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cfb07d0b354df459d4d1208de71437278%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639072731699574497%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=YOP8mPfqoHYp%2F3jKjWfsRFRgnULosUlaBfsX9PLNYPk%3D&reserved=0> , and he took it personally. Now, Trump has a plan for new tariffs—and it puts his trade agenda on a collision course <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkdhd-hrkusddg-k%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cfb07d0b354df459d4d1208de71437278%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639072731699595645%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=59cJkUPLOHCMaXWk5w341Hl61pZKJlQnLlbx%2FBop4K0%3D&reserved=0>  with the midterm campaign season.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal


TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

*	After the Supreme Court ruled that Trump’s global tariffs are illegal <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkdhd-hrkusddg-u%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cfb07d0b354df459d4d1208de71437278%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639072731699619112%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=kLG5w1CmVbhh2SHTkljCRnDdCMZ8o29o%2B9wOcbiPEeI%3D&reserved=0> , the president vowed to impose a 10% global tariff under a different authority; here’s what to know about the decision <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkdhd-hrkusddg-o%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cfb07d0b354df459d4d1208de71437278%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639072731699637621%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=JgaoZMpOCgSt8SD8oGhrFyYUk5xwQp4ZQxsnTs%2Blc10%3D&reserved=0> .

The Supreme Court blunted a tool that Trump has aggressively wielded to remake trade. Reporter Gavin Bade wrote about the president’s new plan <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail19.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gdhkdhd-hrkusddg-yu%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cfb07d0b354df459d4d1208de71437278%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639072731700017571%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0rGyasF%2FRLShgLQIBvy1%2FsHhlCxrdaP1fdypBcxTsj4%3D&reserved=0> —and what it could mean for the midterms and beyond.

A: Just hours after his main tariff rationale was invalidated by the Supreme Court, Trump said he’d implement new levies under two separate legal authorities—one short term, another longer lasting.

Some of the new tariffs Trump wants to impose require congressional approval to extend beyond five months. Others require months of investigations before they can be put into place. In both cases, that pushes key tariff decisions into the summer, just months before November’s midterms when many Republicans are likely to be especially sensitive to complaints about inflation and affordability.

In a sign of growing anxiety toward Trump’s trade tactics, six GOP lawmakers voted with Democrats in an attempt to rein in Trump’s tariff powers in the House of Representatives last week. The Senate passed three similar resolutions last year on narrow bipartisan votes. Now, Republicans running for re-election will have to grapple with tariff drama along with other attacks from Democrats on the economy.

The Supreme Court ruling also left many questions about Trump’s past and future trade policies unanswered. There could be years of litigation to determine what happens to more than $130 billion in tariffs collected under the now-invalid policy.
