Q: How does the federal investigation of Alex Pretti’s death differ from past cases? 


The Department of Homeland Security is leading an investigation into the killing of Pretti by a Border Patrol agent, amid objections from Minnesota officials who say they are being shut out. Justice Department reporter Sadie Gurman explains the state of play. <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gikudhk-hrkusddg-e%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cc81b9cd0481445738e4008de5d95d594%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051095305566864%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0%2FBCOspFSmlUtkLvpFmZz8s%2FpH1n47hAdfnkavs2beg%3D&reserved=0> 

A: U.S. officials said Homeland Security Investigations, an agency within DHS, is leading the probe, with the Federal Bureau of Investigation serving in an assisting role. Usually, the FBI takes the lead.

HSI agents have the authority to arrest people if they have probable cause. But any potential prosecution would have to be handled by the Justice Department.

Most shootings by officers involve local police, rather than federal agents. Federal authorities work alongside local investigators to determine whether an officer engaged in obstruction of justice or violated someone’s civil rights.

The Justice Department typically reviews any shooting involving a federal agent. What’s more, the FBI and DOJ normally investigate almost every high-profile officer-involved killing because prosecutors consider them incidents of national significance that warrant such inquiries.

Minnesota officials want to conduct detailed investigations in the killings of Pretti and Renee Good, who was shot in her car by an agent with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. But they say federal authorities are interfering with their sovereign right to investigate possible violations of state law.

The Trump administration says the state has no legal right to information in what were federal incidents. Both sides have said they don’t trust each other to conduct a fair investigation.

A new study explores whether people would use online shopping the same way if they knew how much of their personal data was being collected along the way without their knowledge. 
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif>

The friends and family dilemma <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fenpst9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596316022%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=szSC3r4OSkraWhxnJkT1pshZ6ebKV%2B0uR%2FLpKC2AOjU%3D&reserved=0> 

A Fuqua podcast covers the ways social media mines our information through interactions with friends’ platforms, even if we try to keep ours private. Professor Ali Makhdoumi explains why individuals can’t wholly control their own data. 
	
 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fufqst9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596333121%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=50NR66rCeFhRLMO%2FOtCTSP%2BfK8juQTWMewJj7aPd8Ms%3D&reserved=0> 

The inside scoop on a cybersecurity case <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fa8qst9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596348438%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=LfNRXTpcBLqieoQTgS6hySbFXe9s8qPXfym%2BVYKJFN8%3D&reserved=0>  

Guest speakers in a joint Duke Law–Sanford Cyber Law and Policy class shared how legal strategy and ethics shaped one of 2025’s most influential privacy verdicts. The case addressed a series of thorny issues around cybersecurity and personal data. 
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 

Flush with data: How the poker bug led to a career in statistical analysis
<https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fq0rst9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596364606%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=6ODEdXsH30SbbkvPFvGfLMlz1FB1AumlAwvOHjTpSDE%3D&reserved=0> 

Lasse Vuursteen became fascinated by game theory and statistics in an unusual way — poker.  He began playing the game as a teen and was gripped by the analytical side of it. Now an assistant professor of statistical science, Vuursteen helps companies analyze data more efficiently, including when privacy restrictions are imposed.
 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2F6ssst9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596384513%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=81ohGSyhzEdmQF2I5%2FPErMlAjBZHvG0Di8a5DCuBosM%3D&reserved=0> 
 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 

Nita Farahany wants to protect your brain data <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fmltst9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596401597%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=VH%2BHCr34%2FtKAKulffIK0QF4JOxsf5HCcVL08WJq1BRk%3D&reserved=0> 

	
 <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2F2dust9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596419074%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=7hMs13JWb0rPHLphrO6xyaoki0U2pQwpgPjjHNaiHrE%3D&reserved=0> 	
Mental privacy is a core issue in Nita Farahany’s AI Law and Policy class, which she has opened up to the public via her Substack page. Each week, Farahany posts lessons that give subscribers a virtual seat in her class on what she calls “the revelations, the confusion, the ‘aha’ moments, and yes, actual legal education” on cognitive liberty in the digital age.

 <https://images.e2ma.net/images/spacer.gif> 
	

	“Business education needs to show that AI technology is not something to be feared, nor does it have to replace face-to-face discussion. Used thoughtfully, it can make human connection more meaningful and human judgment sharper.”

Scott Dyreng,
senior associate dean of innovation at Fuqua School of Business, writing in Poets & Quants <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fejqibt%2F6wjoz54f%2Fi6ust9b&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C9ce49319c2b04ed733f508de5d944746%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639051088596439807%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=cSx6COmTD5wYw%2FpZAxM3k93sH3Jx8emWYT1xuNkudqs%3D&reserved=0>  about efforts at Fuqua to use AI to improve the classroom experience.

Web Scraping is Complex. We make it Simple.


Four ways to scrape Amazon product pages


There are multiple ways to get product data from Amazon with ScraperAPI.

Besides differences in the result format and the scaling, all the options ensure a smooth scraping experience thanks to our advanced Amazon anti-bot bypassing. 

Scraping API

Use the API if you want to get the raw HTML of the product page:

curl
http://api.scraperapi.com?api_key=APIKEY&url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CB847XCK

Structured Data Endpoint

Want to skip manual parsing and receive JSON with well-structured data? Use our Amazon Product Page endpoint to get data from any ASIN: 

curl 

https://api.scraperapi.com/structured/amazon/product?api_key=API_KEY&asin=B0CB847XCK 

Async Structured Data Endpoint  

Want to scrape Amazon at a scale and receive well-structured  JSON data? Use the async structured endpoint like this:

import requests 

r = requests.post(url = 'https://async.scraperapi.com/structured/amazon/product', json={'apiKey’:APIKEY, ‘asins’:[ B0CB847XCK, ASIN2, ...' ] }) print(r.text)

Subject: DFE Student News & Events for the Week of January 26, 2026
Body:
Hi, students! Please see below for this week’s DFE Student News and Events newsletter.

 

DFE News & Events:

 

Markets Discussion Group with Mike Aguilar <https://www.fuqua.duke.edu/faculty/michael-aguilar> 

Thursday, January 29, 5-6 PM in Gray 228 - open to all class years, all majors  REGISTER <https://dukefinance.wufoo.com/forms/z1wl1ief0s0r1le/> 

Participate in lively discussions on current events and how they impact financial markets and the broader economic environment. Learn how to watch the markets and formulate informed views about economic and business trends. Previous knowledge of the markets is not required. You’ll get something out of it whether you’re a first-year or a senior. Stay informed using the following resources available to all Duke students at no cost: The Wall Street Journal <https://education.wsj.com/?s=Duke&user_type=students&cat=2&page_type=searchresults&search_type=b> , Bloomberg for Education <https://guides.library.duke.edu/c.php?g=289830&p=1931454> , and The New York Times <https://www.nytimes.com/activate-access/edu-access> .

 

AmplifyME Finance Simulations
Explore roles in banking, markets, and Quant while building real-world skills, tracking performance, and accessing potential recruiting opportunities with top firms. AmplifyME’s live, virtual simulations are open to all Duke undergraduates and will be available through April. Learn more at https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/finance-simulations-amplifyme <https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/finance-simulations-amplifyme> .

Create an account <https://pathways.amplifyme.com/uni/signup/S58GKIE>  on the AmplifyME platform with verification code 779495 and your Duke email address. Onboarding instructions <https://econ.duke.edu/sites/econ.duke.edu/files/documents/Pathways%20Onboarding%20Instructions%20PDF_0.pdf> 

Dzialga Women in Finance Initiative – Class of 2029: Apply starting February 2
Info Session: Tuesday, February 10 at 6:00-7:00 PM in Social Sciences 136  REGISTER <https://dukefinance.wufoo.com/forms/k1fb4ywn051vrui/> 

Join the initiative co-directors and current fellows at the Feb. 10 info session to learn more about the program. Applicants are highly encouraged to attend. 

Sophomore through senior year, Dzialga Fellows engage with dozens of alumni in the finance space, are mentees and mentors, and develop professional skills within a supportive cohort. Sophomores take a trip to NYC over fall break to network with alumni at a variety of firms. Read more about the benefits of being a Dzialga Fellow and the application process at econ.duke.edu/dfe/dzialga-women-finance-initiative <https://econ.duke.edu/dfe/dzialga-women-finance-initiative> . The deadline to apply is March 4 at noon. 

 

 

DFE Advising Opportunities:

Alumni Advising with Mark Augusti – open to all undergraduates  REGISTER <https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0F44ABAE29A7F5CF8-59754216-finance> 

Mondays, 12:00 – 1:00 PM, in the DFE Conference Room (Social Sciences 228A) 

Mark Augusti ‘87 holds weekly in-person advising hours for undergrads. Augusti is also teaching FMKT 390S-04: Financing Health Care Companies this spring. Read his bio below:

Mark Augusti, MBA, is Founder and Managing Owner of Kenmore Advisors, an advisory and consulting firm focused on compliance, governance, and commercial strategy in the medical technology sector. Previously, Mr. Augusti was President and Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors at Conformis, Inc., a public orthopedic device company. Prior to leading Conformis, Mr. Augusti was Integra LifeSciences Corporation’s Corporate Vice President and President of Orthopedics and Tissue Technologies. Mr. Augusti served as Chief Executive Officer at Bioventus LLC, and was a member of the Bioventus’ Board of Directors. Prior to that Mr. Augusti spent nine years with Smith & Nephew, in a series of leadership roles within the orthopedics and biologics businesses. Prior to that, he spent 13 years at GE Medical Systems, where he held various sales, marketing and strategic management roles, both in the U.S. and internationally. Mr. Augusti serves as a director of the Massachusetts Health Policy Forum and has served as a director of the AdvaMed Accel Board. Mr. Augusti received his M.B.A. from the UCLA Anderson School of Management, and his B.S. in Computer Science and Economics from Duke University.

Career Everywhere Drop-In Advising – open to undergraduates and graduate students
Tuesday, January 27, 1:00-3:00 PM in the DFE Conference Room (Social Sciences 228A)

Meet with Duke Career Center for 15-minute Drop-In Advising for quick questions, document reviews, etc. Time slots will be on a first-come, first-served on-site basis, the day of the event. NO REGISTRATION REQUIRED. Available to all undergraduate students and graduate students from the Duke Graduate School, Duke’s Pratt School of Engineering (PhD only), Duke Divinity School, Duke Medicine School’s Master of Biostatistics and Population Health Sciences programs. Visit Handshake <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/duke.joinhandshake.com/login__;!!OToaGQ!sk-RdI6xAUFbKi-pEqMVGqNWp8LL5pL2orS6SxyEUOAXo0Iq48WBf43IsyVW9CEwTsrDWji9b5r4hTNSWpo5$>  or CareerHub <https://careerhub.students.duke.edu/>  for additional information on the Duke Career Center.

 

Student Club News & Events:

 

Spring 2026 ITP Classes sponsored by Duke Investment Club
Sunday, February 1, 1:30-2:30 PM - open to all class years  REGISTER <https://tinyurl.com/s26-itp-registration> 

ITP is 8-week course covering an introduction to financial markets, basic accounting, fundamental investment analysis, and valuation methods that is free and open to the entire Duke community regardless of experience. Contact Laura <mailto:lsh37@duke.edu>  with questions. 

 

 

A reminder to student groups: If you have a finance-focused event that you would like to promote in this weekly Monday newsletter, please submit your request <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/dukefinance.wufoo.com/forms/dfe-listserv-advertising-request-form/__;!!OToaGQ!sfM03G0AnBQYD2LAri4An71HHV0PvMm0se10YCaE4F6DCC5QqUiUbfDuYo4zgQo9Dkjap_N1vUKt0FCjYkzngA$>  by 11:59pm on Sunday. As stated on the form, all submissions are subject to approval by DFE.

2026 Schedule Is Here!
 <https://img.goduke.com/EloquaImages/clients/PACduke/%7Ba6702e08-92d7-4ef1-8dd3-2288cfc04019%7D_2026_Duke_Football_Schedule_GoDuke.png> 	
Six home dates, eight contests against 2025 bowl game or College Football Playoff participants and three tilts versus programs that finished ranked in the top 25 a season ago highlight the 2026 Duke football schedule released Monday evening by the ACC office.

The Blue Devils begin the campaign hosting Tulane on Saturday, September 5 at Brooks Field at Wallace Wade Stadium before traveling to Big Ten foe Illinois on September 12. The Green Wave made a College Football Playoff appearance after capturing the American championship and ended the 2025 season ranked No. 18 in the final Associated Press (AP) poll.

Duke returns home for two games to close September, hosting Stanford to begin ACC play on September 19 and William & Mary on September 26.

The Blue Devils have an open date on October 3 and travel to Georgia Tech on October 10. Duke welcomes rival North Carolina to Durham on October 17 before traveling to Virginia for an ACC Championship Game rematch on October 24. The Cavaliers checked in at No. 16 in the final AP poll of the 2025 campaign. The Blue Devils close October by hosting Boston College on the 31st. 

Four November contests begin with back-to-back road games at NC State (Saturday, November 7) and Miami (Saturday, November 14). The Hurricanes finished No. 2 to end 2025 after their national championship game appearance. 

Duke hosts Clemson on November 21 before capping the regular season at Wake Forest on November 28.

Be on the lookout in the upcoming weeks for ticket information to secure your seats for 2026 Duke Football.

On-Demand Video Interview

If you are a candidate or you are assisting someone with that requires accessibility assistance or an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please click this link for instructions on how to submit an accommodation request. <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wellsfargojobs.com%2Fen%2Finclusion%2Fdisability%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C6b5019b2d66144128d4b08de5d2487c2%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050608641564591%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=WrXnvhHJX0oaDznVNHhRSVvElR4qSn6ltd%2Bumm6jnLA%3D&reserved=0> 

DIRECTIONS

1.	Set aside approximately 30 minutes in a distraction free environment to complete your video interview. Although you will be able to complete the interview over more than one sitting, and you will be provided the opportunity to re-record a response, if necessary, your best responses typically result from a single sitting where you can fully focus your attention on your interview.
	
	
2.	Questions will be presented as written text, with one question appearing at a time. Each interview question will remain on the screen while you record your response, so it is not necessary memorize or write down the interview question. A countdown timer will also be present on the screen during your response recording.
	
	
3.	You will be provided a practice or warm-up question, that will not be considered in the hiring decision. Use this question to check your camera settings, voice quality, and to familiarize yourself with the video interview process.
	
	
4.	Click BEGIN to access the Wells Fargo foyer, which is the landing page. To sufficiently prepare yourself, watch the videos and review the additional resources. Please follow the instructions carefully and review each question in full prior to recording your response.

DO your homework, you have a limited amount of time to convey your knowledge, research current deals and initiatives ahead of time

Hi! You're invited to take the PI Cognitive Assessment. Please read the instructions below and click the link when you're ready to take the assessment. Thank you!

You have been invited to complete the Predictive Index (PI) Cognitive Assessment. In order to have a good experience, it is important that you know the following: 

*	The PI Cognitive Assessment is a 12-minute timed assessment consisting of 50 questions.
*	The results are based on the number of correct answers within the 12-minute time frame, so try to answer as many questions correctly as possible. You will not be penalized for incorrect answers, but random guessing is not recommended.
*	Being able to focus is important. Please make sure you can dedicate sufficient time and can take it in a distraction free environment. 
*	It is compatible with most computers and tablets, but taking it on a smart phone or small-screen tablet is not recommended.
*	You must complete the assessment in one sitting. You cannot take a break or shut down the browser and continue later.
*	You will have an opportunity to practice on three sample questions. We strongly encourage you to take advantage of this.

Subject: DukeALERT -- Update on Severe Weather Policy for University & DUHS
Body:
Duke University, including the School of Medicine and the School of Nursing, will extend the severe weather and emergency conditions policy until 11:30 a.m. Tuesday. All in-person classes that start before 11:30 a.m. will be cancelled. Classes beginning afterward will be held as scheduled.

The severe weather policy will end at 7 p.m. Monday for Duke University Health System.

University employees in “essential service” roles should report to or remain at work during this time, and managers should notify staff and implement departmental severe weather plans as appropriate.

Contractors and crews continue to clear and treat roads, parking lots and walkways on campus. Temperatures will drop into the single digits overnight, and wet surfaces will likely refreeze. Individuals coming to campus should allow for extra time for travel and use extreme caution when traveling to and around campus in case of icy spots.

For safety reasons, the roof levels of all garages will remain closed on Tuesday. Bus routes will depend on weather conditions. Every effort will be made to continue the C-1 bus route, weather permitting. Duke community members should monitor Duke TransLoc for real-time updates on transit routes.

Duke community members are encouraged to stay informed by checking the DukeALERT website (https://emergency.duke.edu), as well as the Campus Service Updates web page for additional updates on parking lots, busing routes, dining facilities, and stores.

This Week in IB Recruiting


Before we dive in, a quick note on why we built AskStanley:




Recruiting has become more staggered, more opaque, and more school-/group-specific than ever. Stanley exists to help you track what’s happening in real time, prep the way interviews are actually run, and stay organized across dozens of moving pieces. At this point in the process, most candidates don’t fail technicals from lack of knowledge. They fail on follow-ups. 30 minutes a day on AskStanley is designed to close that gap before Superdays hit.

Try AskStanley Completely Free <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgxhch.r.a.d.sendibm1.com%2Fmk%2Fcl%2Ff%2Fsh%2FSMK1E8tHeFuBo0idTdIeuGeJ268H%2FIQPwLAI_iYFS&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cdc2ec6e22f234ec4a99308de5d19426b%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050560520374378%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C80000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=fSr%2Fg3dus%2BZNrfz3JdYG8sKhDXuDHENnTUdMqqXg5eE%3D&reserved=0>  	

1. Where Recruiting Stands Right Now


Bulge Brackets (GS / MS / JPM / Citi / BofA / WF)





General trend: Second & third waves of superdays/first-rounds have started to come out. These firms are far from being done, but a good chunk of offers have been given.




More granular details:

*	GS has given out their first round of offers, and probably only has 1/2 rounds of SPD → offer left based on historical info.  

*	MS has released offers at target schools and will have 1 or 2 waves of SPD → offer. 

*	JPMorgan has issued multiple offer waves. If you’re still waiting, this is normal. JPM historically continues rolling decisions into mid-February.

*	Citi is wrapping up parts of the first rounds while continuing accelerated Superdays for certain groups and schools.

*	BofA is largely following HireVue → accelerated Superday for NYC and HireVue → regular Superday for non-core offices. More invites are expected shortly.

*	Barclays has begun rolling Superdays and is expected to remain active through February.

*	Wells Fargo has released a round of offers, and more superday invites are expected to go out in the next 2 weeks.




What matters for candidates now:
If you haven’t heard back, you are not out. Most BB offices (especially non-core) will continue running waves into February and early March. If you are core, continue to reach out to your contacts and update them. 






Elite Boutiques (Evercore / Lazard / CVP / PJT)


General trend: Like BB's, second-wave interviews are starting to roll out. The first batch of Superdays and offers has been given out (NYC). Outside of NYC, the timeline is sped up, with a larger number of offers made. 




More granular details:

*	Evercore is in the full swing of things. Many offers in NYC/regional have come out. They are the earliest boutique. 

*	PJT - no update

*	Lazard - no update

*	CVP has released some regional/NYC offers, but as we mentioned last time, runs later than the rest. 





MMs & Regionals (RBC / Baird / William Blair / Truist / BMO / Oppenheimer / Stifel / etc.)





General trend: This is still where the most opportunity exists if you’re waiting on outcomes. These firms recruit more slowly and lean far more on networking.

2. The Biggest Technical Mistake Candidates Make


One of the most common technical mistakes we’re seeing this cycle is around enterprise value vs. equity value mechanics — specifically, how operating changes actually flow through valuation.




A lot of candidates can recite the definitions:

*	EV represents the value of the core business

*	Equity value is what shareholders own




But they struggle when asked things like:

*	Why EV can stay flat, while EQV increases? Or the other way around?

*	Why EBITDA growth doesn’t always translate to equity value growth

*	How changes in net working capital or capex affect valuation outcomes

*	Why two companies with identical EBITDA can have very different equity values

HAPPY New Year Graham!

Kickstart Your Spring Semester at Spark Your Career!

Friday, January 30th

Programming Kickoff: 12:00 p.m. | Penn Pavilion

Headshots Available : 10:30-noon, 036 Bryan Center

Join us for the 4th Annual Spark Your Career event to connect with resources and sharpen your career skills!

Opening Session:

Personal Branding  (12:00 p.m. - 1:00 p.m.)

This dynamic and hands-on workshop is designed to help participants create a compelling personal brand that will stand out in any industry. This session will equip students with the tools to identify the branding strategies that align with your unique expertise, values, and goals.


Presented by: Shep Moyle, Senior Lecturing Fellow at Duke University, seasoned entrepreneur, and expert in innovation and leadership.

 

Breakout Sessions:

Choose one topic per session:

*	Session I: 1:15 p.m. - 2:15 p.m.
*	Session II: 2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.

Topics:

1.	Interviewing; Strategies from Employers: Students will get first hand tips and strategies from local employers and the Career Centers Employer Relations team as they prepare for the interview. Areas of discussion will include: application materials, reaching out to recruiters, understanding job descriptions as well as qualifications. Be sure to think of some questions to ask as well!
2.	“Showing Up Authentically You”:  This interactive workshop invites students to explore what it truly means to show up authentically in professional spaces while navigating identity, opportunity, and career growth. Through reflective activities, scenario discussions, and student involvement exercises, participants will unpack common myths about authenticity, examine how visible and invisible identities shape workplace experiences, and consider the strategic choices often required early in a career. By the end of the workshop, participants will leave with practical strategies for navigating career decisions, supporting inclusive workplaces, and aligning professional aspirations with their true selves, recognizing that authenticity is a spectrum, not a single destination.
3.	AI Is Not Your Career Advisor (But It Can Help you Move Forward): In this hands-on session, you’ll learn how to use Large Language Models (ChatGPT or Copilot) as a thinking partner to support your career development. We’ll walk through practical frameworks for asking better questions, explore common career case studies (like recruiting prep, exploring industries you know nothing about, and building a sustainable job-search plan), and practice using AI tools in ways that are ethical, authentic, and actually useful!

Resume Review Session and Resource Fair: (3:45 p.m. - 5:15 p.m.)

The Career Center Staff as well as Career Influencers will be available during this time to look over your resume and offer recommendations as necessary. Please be sure to either bring a printed copy (no printer available on site) or a digital copy of your resume.

This event is open to all undergraduates, with a focus on sophomores

We are excited to share a unique opportunity to gain real-world exposure to commercial real estate through the Spring 2026 Commercial Real Estate Virtual Internship Program, powered by Project Destined. [Learn more here <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fprojectdestined.us17.list-manage.com%2Ftrack%2Fclick%3Fu%3D6a7623e661b782123cb167aba%26id%3Db64d165e37%26e%3Dfe75a3a393&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C1bf82eced64c482848c008de5ce34841%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050328416944662%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=VDJYCxO0mIdrihtlff4j45Dg353nI5spoz8z56FB%2FTo%3D&reserved=0> ]

What You’ll Gain

*	Work on a live commercial real estate deal in your local community

*	Build financial modeling and investment analysis skills through interactive workshops

*	Receive mentorship from senior real estate professionals and executives from PGIM, WX Real Estate, AEW, and other leading firms

*	Compete in a Shark Tank–style investment pitch and earn a scholarship stipend

*	Join a global alumni network of 30,000+ students who have launched careers at Blackstone, Brookfield, CBRE, Greystar, JLL, JPMorgan, KKR, Wells Fargo, and more

Program Details

*	Dates: Mondays & Wednesdays, February 9 – March 25, 2026

*	Schedule: Twice per week | Evening sessions (5:30–7:30 PM ET)

Application Deadline: Tuesday, January 27th at 5:00 PM ET

Whether you are exploring careers in real estate investments, asset management, capital markets, or consulting, this program will equip you with the skills, network, and confidence to stand out.

Subject: Short Duke Libraries survey – chance to win $150 gift card
Body:
Dear Graham, 

You are invited to participate in a brief Duke University Libraries Student Survey, which should take approximately 5 minutes to complete. The Libraries has entered your name in a survey drawing for a $150 Visa gift card. After the Libraries’ survey closes at midnight on Sunday, February 15th, we will notify you if you have won the raffle.
 
Note that you will only be eligible to receive the $150 gift card if you complete the survey below. If you are the winner of the gift card but you have not completed the survey, you are not eligible to receive the gift card.   

Follow this link to the Survey:
Take the Survey <https://duke.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_afwuawuiEWNHSya?Q_DL=IS4SlWFdXm9TX66_afwuawuiEWNHSya_CGC_HHw8OZFq0N57Cuc&Q_CHL=email> 

You can also copy and paste the survey URL below into your internet browser:
https://duke.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_afwuawuiEWNHSya?Q_DL=IS4SlWFdXm9TX66_afwuawuiEWNHSya_CGC_HHw8OZFq0N57Cuc&Q_CHL=email

The survey will give you an opportunity to share your thoughts about using the Duke University Libraries and provide suggestions for improving current library spaces, collections, and services. The Libraries only conducts a university-wide survey every three years, and your responses will help us enhance existing services and develop innovative programs. Check out some of the changes we implemented as a direct result of our past surveys <https://blogs.library.duke.edu/blog/2026/01/26/students-take-our-2026-survey/> . 
 
Your responses are anonymous, and results will only be reported in the aggregate. Thank you in advance for sharing your thoughts about the Duke Libraries.
 
Joseph Salem
Rita DiGiallonardo Holloway University Librarian & Vice Provost for Library Affairs

A showdown


State and federal authorities faced off in Minnesota yesterday, after Border Patrol agents killed a U.S. citizen on Saturday.

The state wants to investigate the shooting, in which officials tackled Pretti, a registered nurse from the city’s Veterans Affairs hospital who had been filming them on his phone. Then they stripped him of a handgun, for which he had a permit, and shot him again and again.

The federal government does not want that inquiry to happen. Agents have refused to give state investigators access to the crime scene, even though they had a search warrant. Late on Saturday night, a judge barred federal officials from destroying evidence in the case.

Then, yesterday, the Trump administration pushed groundless accusations against the victim. Gregory Bovino, the official in charge of President Trump’s Border Patrol operations, told CNN that Pretti wanted to “perpetrate violence, obstruct, delay or obfuscate Border Patrol in the performance of their duties in an active crime scene.” The agents were the victims, he said. Videos analyzed by The Times contradict those claims. Brian O’Hara, the Minneapolis police chief, said on CBS that Pretti appeared to be “exercising his First Amendment rights to record law enforcement activity, and also exercising his Second Amendment rights to lawfully be armed in a public space in the city.” He described the city and his department as being at a breaking point. “People have had enough,” he said.


No respite


Residents of Minneapolis, tens of thousands of whom have been protesting in the streets this month, are grieving together and experiencing “a profound sense of solidarity,” said Ernesto Londoño, a Minneapolis-based Times reporter with whom I spoke yesterday. With Minnesota officials powerless to push ICE out of the city, he said, “ordinary people are looking out for one another in every conceivable way.”

Ernesto noted a strand of communal grief. “Minnesota is a state that has a lot of trauma from 2020 and its aftermath,” he told me, referring to the killing of George Floyd and the violent protests that followed it. Last June, two state legislators were shot, as were their spouses. One of the legislators died, as did her husband. In August, a mass shooting at a Catholic church in Minneapolis left two children dead. Federal agents killed Renee Good on Jan. 7. And then Pretti on Saturday.

The bond formed by residents was evident yesterday. It was cold in Minneapolis this past weekend, dangerously so, with lows in the negative teens. It’s painful to be outside for more than a couple of minutes at a time. Ernesto said he’d seen protesters handing out hand warmers and bundling up to cover as much of their skin as possible. Some lit fires for warmth. Local residents have opened their doors to others, giving them a respite from the punishing chill. Yesterday afternoon, members of the Minnesota National Guard, clad in yellow vests to differentiate them from federal agents, brought protesters coffee, hot chocolate and doughnuts.

But that sense of fellowship comes at a cost. “We think of Minnesota as generally peaceful, filled with civic-minded and nice people,” Ernesto said. “But they have been put through the wringer. This has been hard on them personally.” The whole situation in Minneapolis, he said, “feels unsustainable.”

It’s the Little Things

 

Stop us if you’ve heard this one before: Small cap stocks are finally breaking out.

 

The most widely followed benchmark for small U.S. companies, the Russell 2000 Index, just did something it hasn’t in decades <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43731063.475986%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2Uvc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LXRvZGF5LWRvdy1zcC01MDAtbmFzZGFxLTAxLTIyLTIwMjYvY2FyZC9ydXNzZWxsLTIwMDAtd2lubmluZy1zdHJlYWstaXMtaXRzLWxvbmdlc3QtaW4tbmVhcmx5LTMwLXllYXJzLVJudVowbGZERGtrREh6VFVVWFhzP21vZD1kamVtTWFya2V0c0FN%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dB6a8b9914&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C93515c4270014c16086908de5ccea9b6%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050239871967146%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=9aa4ni3jAkHy9%2FUS%2Bh5J0Kenxwiy%2Byw4mnBwTVroivs%3D&reserved=0> . It beat the large cap S&P 500 for 14 days in a row through last Thursday.

 

The more diminutive the firm, the better its performance was over that stretch. A group of even tinier microcaps outperformed the S&P 100, made up of the largest companies, by almost 12 percentage points.

 

That’s remarkable, but small stocks have broken a lot of hearts the past few years. They took off during 2021’s meme-stock mania and as recently as July 2024, sparking hope the neglected category was finally getting some love. December or early January often see brief rallies too after tax-loss selling <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43731063.475986%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9saXZlY292ZXJhZ2Uvc3RvY2stbWFya2V0LXRvZGF5LWRvdy1zcC01MDAtbmFzZGFxLTEwLTMxLTIwMjUvY2FyZC93aHktdGhlLW5vdmVtYmVyLWVmZmVjdC1jb3VsZC1saWZ0LXRoZXNlLXN0b2Nrcy1Fb015NWVtY0JmN0N4UE5UdTJ5NT9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBc0128011&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C93515c4270014c16086908de5ccea9b6%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050239871981546%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=zOOi5ibj9ltDHXi758ig1ZAR%2BJuEhF%2FqaC6LcKqtpyE%3D&reserved=0>  wraps up.

 

Nobody can say whether the momentum will continue this time, but small stocks look like an opportunity for patient investors <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftrk.wsj.com%2Fclick%2F43731063.475986%2FaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9maW5hbmNlL2ludmVzdGluZy9zbWFsbC1zdG9ja3MtYmFyZ2Fpbi04NTAzNDIzMz9tb2Q9ZGplbU1hcmtldHNBTQ%2F6965299853e1c001a97cb68dBdafecee1&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C93515c4270014c16086908de5ccea9b6%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050239871995456%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=T7Yl2BkisRUNuUQuRjQAEmSdMvb6YYiJiW0p%2BszepaY%3D&reserved=0> . The S&P 600 small-cap index trades at around a 25% discount on forward earnings to its large-cap stablemate, the S&P 500, and an even bigger one compared to the Magnificent Seven companies that have led market gains.

 

That gap might be appropriate if it means accepting slower growth. It probably won’t this year, according to Francis Gannon, a small-cap veteran and co-chief investment officer at Royce Investment Partners. 

 

“The earnings story is the reason to own small caps,” says Gannon, who points to tailwinds like the profit boost from new depreciation rules and a greater benefit from falling interest rates. Smaller companies are more likely to have floating-rate borrowings so the 2022 rate hiking cycle was much harder on them.

 

Despite their recent sad-sack reputation, small caps have long been a fruitful part of the market. A dollar invested in them since the late 1920s has grown nearly five times as much as one in the S&P 500 or its predecessor index.

 

That isn’t ancient history either: Between 2000 and 2021, the S&P 600’s total return was more than twice that of the S&P 500.

 

But the last four years, beginning when the Fed started raising rates, have been abysmal. Since late 2022 in particular, the mega-cap Magnificent Seven has provided much of U.S. stocks’ overall return.

 

Whether or not that concentration concerns you, owning the entire market, maybe even with an extra nod toward its overlooked small-fry, could be a profitable decision.

Q: What new rules could get you a bigger refund this tax season? 


Taxpayers can file 2025 returns starting today. Reporters Ashlea Ebeling and Richard Rubin explain the most important changes <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2F10point.cmail20.com%2Ft%2Fd-l-gikiyly-hrkusddg-g%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cc66b2ddde6ef44b609d508de5ccad0a2%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050223339138859%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=38nrXkJQUG6YXkbmnKu47EM3S7cG2fzKT2UctPYZ6B4%3D&reserved=0>  you need to be aware of.

A: Americans can expect smaller tax bills and bigger refunds this year—after they navigate a pile of new rules from last year’s tax law.

The standard deduction for 2025 is $15,750 for single filers and $31,500 for married couples filing jointly. Last year’s tax law raised those by $750 and $1,500, respectively, on top of the Internal Revenue Service’s normal year-to-year inflation adjustments.

Taking the standard deduction is still the best option financially for nearly 90% of taxpayers. Still, this year’s changes might mean you would be better off itemizing your deductions.

Another change to be aware of: The maximum state-and-local-tax deduction for property taxes plus income or sales taxes is $40,000 for 2025, up from $10,000. As a result, many taxpayers will be better off itemizing instead of taking the standard deduction this year.

Be aware, however, that the maximum SALT deduction begins phasing down to $10,000 once a taxpayer’s modified adjusted gross income crosses $500,000, whether single or married filing jointly.

Other tax laws offer credits and deductions for parents, seniors and those with overtime pay, among other categories.

Just because you get a new federal tax break doesn’t mean it also applies to your state income-tax return. California, for example, doesn’t have its own versions of the tax law’s new deductions for people 65 and up, tipped and overtime workers or auto-loan interest.

January 26th - February 1st



The Short List is the Office of Undergraduate Education's weekly newsletter highlighting events, information, and deadlines that you need to know for this week.


1/26


Climate Cafe


Join the Office of Climate and Sustainability and Duke Campus Farm for Climate Cafe, an informal gathering that offers a supportive space for the Duke community to engage in conversations about the emotional, social, cultural, and political dimensions of climate change. This Climate Cafe will specifically focus on food, agriculture, and labor justice. Lunch will be provided. 

 

Date: Monday, January 26, 1:00 pm - 2:00 pm

Location: Gross Hall 100 C

More Information <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fouskli%2Fw0yzscmd%2Fc9bs3mb&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cebf75a2aa5ba4c4c295208de5cc45a33%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050195570562739%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=EMN%2BPEUecBiTz2%2BHgLEedB4b9VeHJhEQ%2BVhvCyXnfXY%3D&reserved=0> 
 	

1/26


Roundtable on the Anthropocene and Biodiversity 


The Center for French and Francophone Studies at Duke University, in partnership with Columbia University and Villa Albertine, is delighted to welcome Corine Pelluchon, Professor of Philosophy at Université Gustave Eiffel, and Cyrille Barnérias, Director of International Relations at the French Biodiversity Office, for a roundtable talk. Pelluchon and Barnérias will be in conversation with Dr. Lori Bennear and Dr. Felwine Sarr. Together, they will reflect on the idea of a “New Enlightenment” for the Anthropocene, exploring emerging forms of interdependence among human, animal, and plant life amid biodiversity loss. 

 

Date: Monday, January 26, 5:00 pm - 8:00 pm

Location: Rubenstein Library, Holsti-Anderson Room

More Information <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft.e2ma.net%2Fclick%2Fouskli%2Fw0yzscmd%2F8tds3mb&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7Cebf75a2aa5ba4c4c295208de5cc45a33%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050195570606295%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=hxTufo7W0mnPljtf5DePdncxusMfVYIjFcmqgtxXqIA%3D&reserved=0> 
 	

1/27


Intro to the AI Suite


Curious about AI but not sure where to begin? Join the Innovation Co-Lab for this free, beginner-friendly class that offers a guided, hands-on introduction to today's AI tools. You will be exploring machine learning, large language models, and generative AI through demos, creative play, and clear, jargon-free conversations about what artificial intelligence can and cannot do.

 

Date: Tuesday, January 27, 1:30 pm - 3:30 pm

Location: The TEC - Technology Engagement Center

1/29


Freeing Joan Little: Gender, Incarceration, and Struggles for Justice


Join Duke Libraries, the Sallie Bingham Center for Women's History and Culture; History; Gender, Sexuality, and Feminist Studies; African and African American Studies; and the Franklin Humanities Institute for this panel on Joan Little, in recognition of the fiftieth anniversary of this landmark case that still offers lessons in the struggle for justice. The panel will focus on a discussion of Joan Little and what her story tells us about gender, incarceration, and state violence then and now. Historian Christina Greene, Ph.D. ’96, author of Free Joan Little: The Politics of Race, Sexual Violence, and Imprisonment and death penalty lawyer, Shelagh Kenney, will lead the panel. An exhibition of items related to Joan Little, including one of her handwritten, illustrated poems, will be on display in Perkins Library until the end of January.  



Date: Thursday, January 29, 5:00 pm - 6:30 pm

Location: Smith Warehouse, Ahmadieh Family Lecture Hall Bay 4

LOOKING AHEAD


2/15


The 23rd Annual Valentine's Jazz Festival


Celebrate the joy, energy, and community spirit of big-band jazz at the 23rd Annual Valentine's Jazz Festival, a beloved tradition that unites three of the Triangle's most vibrant jazz programs and is hosted by the Department of Music at Duke. This year's festival brings together the powerhouse ensembles of Duke University, North Carolina Central University, and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill for an afternoon filled with swing, soul, and electrifying ensemble playing. The Valentine's Jazz Festival is a celebration of collaboration and community and is a place where students from across campuses come together to share their passion, creativity, and musical voice. Whether you're a longtime jazz lover or new to the genre, this annual tradition promises an afternoon of joyful energy and unforgettable performances. This event is free for Duke students, claim your tickets below. 

Date: Sunday, February 15, 2:00 pm - 3:30 pm
Location: Reynolds Theater

In this intro to cloud computing, readers will learn about a wide variety of topics related to cloud computing, including the command line, Linux operating systems, open-source software development, setting up servers and stacks, using version control, security best practices, and the basics of the Domain Name System.

Helpful Developer & Cloud Tutorials

*	A Linux Command Line Primer <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGfmGbsOcgScdRGdbEJ36k2Dcq8KOSRimhqQfeC5qD5ucxZrqkyIxdPsoQB5ejRHoGYvYbuPkY%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2a2c2e709d524e15a83508de5cb55a46%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050131144927110%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=mOP7V3Jj0Mlkwsbt%2FmlrLgjaUFRHDePZp5hi8q%2Frnn8%3D&reserved=0> 
	The command-line interface is a powerful method for issuing commands to your computer or a remote cloud server. This tutorial introduces the command line with an interactive terminal you can launch in your browser.
	
	
*	How To Use SQL <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGfmGbsOdDWv_O4G8vd_p93lCkNgIBKYreGI8_aV0ovJ165jp7UgUVAq-XR-EJyV5i-d7MSHWc%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2a2c2e709d524e15a83508de5cb55a46%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050131144960753%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=1B39W7uPpnJ1wDKsXkNin6dDciKjxM1gdgu40LWC%2FVg%3D&reserved=0> 
	Structured Query Language — commonly known as SQL — is used to define, control, manipulate, and query data held in a relational database. Ideal for managing structured data (data that can fit neatly into an existing data model), SQL is an essential tool for developers and system administrators in a wide variety of contexts.
	
	
*	How To Deploy a Static Website to the Cloud with DigitalOcean App Platform <https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwaves.digitalocean.com%2FMTEzLURUTi0yNjYAAAGfmGbsOWjH6pdtEHis2H6m1nPdUMEuuhkmUcKc2a9w80DgVNUlpuaNnVR6hYhx6Q4IM_nY60g%3D&data=05%7C02%7Cgraham.mills%40duke.edu%7C2a2c2e709d524e15a83508de5cb55a46%7Ccb72c54e4a314d9eb14a1ea36dfac94c%7C0%7C0%7C639050131144981258%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=5OiZhwWkJdU5yB7SzScOgRiayPFvn%2B%2FSGC%2B9JvlYVdw%3D&reserved=0>

Body:
Crazies,


#5 DUKE vs #23 LOUISVILLE | Monday, January 25th — TICKET ORDER INFORMATION 


Your tickets will indicate your order of lining up by "row" and "seat" in numeric order.  If you order 12 tickets and they are not all in the same "row" – that is ok, you will still be lining up in that order so will all be able to stand together. This "row" and "seat" on your ticket is only to indicate your order of lining up and not where you'll be standing in the student section.  We will fill Section 17 with our normal process.


Please bear with us in the circumstances and feel free to reach out with further questions. 


Courtney Butash & Elliot Beamer
Co-VPs of Gameday Operations 2025-2026
Krzyzewskiville Policy 2025-2026 <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1E8hpHwPPRQd6T3LhNSGlKSMWQ-P7gwsoYlIV9hjDDuw/edit?usp=sharing> 



On Sun, Jan 25, 2026 at 5:10 PM Gameday Operations <operationsgameday@gmail.com <mailto:operationsgameday@gmail.com> > wrote:


	Crazies,

	
	

	#5 DUKE vs #23 LOUISVILLE | Monday, January 25th — TICKETS LIVE

	
	

	Due to the Severe Weather Policy, undergraduate students must claim tickets through their Duke Athletics ticket account linked here <https://goduke.evenue.net/students/events/STU-MBB> , as you do for other ticketed athletics events (football, women’s basketball, etc.). Never claimed a ticket before? Be sure to find all the information on how to do so here <https://goduke.com/feature/StudentTickets> .

	
	

	Tickets are LIVE. Students are able to claim as many as TWELVE tickets. If you have a group interested in attending, please designate one person from your group to claim the tickets. Perhaps your tent captain, or your most reliable friend. To ensure fair access for everyone, please do not join multiple groups or claim extra tickets. Tickets are non-transferable. If you want to attend by yourself, feel free to claim just one ticket.

	
	

	As mentioned in yesterday’s email, we will not be lining up outside tomorrow due to weather. Doors to the Hall of Fame, located up the ramp from K-Ville, will open exclusively for students with a ticket at 4pm tomorrow afternoon. From 4pm-5pm, there will be free pizza, water and beer, first come, first served. IDs will be required for beer, and there is a limit of 2 per person while supplies last. At 5pm, we’ll start lining up in the K Center Practice Facility. To guarantee entry, you must arrive in the Hall of Fame by 4:30pm.

	
	

	Let’s get Cameron rocking again on Monday!

	
	

	SI6HTS DDMF GTHC

	
	

	Courtney Butash & Elliot Beamer
	Co-VPs of Gameday Operations 2025-2026
	Krzyzewskiville Policy 2025-2026 <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1E8hpHwPPRQd6T3LhNSGlKSMWQ-P7gwsoYlIV9hjDDuw/edit?usp=sharing>

Subject: TICKETS LIVE!!!!!!!! DUKE vs LOUISVILLE 1/26
Body:
Crazies,




#5 DUKE vs #23 LOUISVILLE | Monday, January 25th — TICKETS LIVE




Due to the Severe Weather Policy, undergraduate students must claim tickets through their Duke Athletics ticket account linked here <https://goduke.evenue.net/students/events/STU-MBB> , as you do for other ticketed athletics events (football, women’s basketball, etc.). Never claimed a ticket before? Be sure to find all the information on how to do so here <https://goduke.com/feature/StudentTickets> .




Tickets are LIVE. Students are able to claim as many as TWELVE tickets. If you have a group interested in attending, please designate one person from your group to claim the tickets. Perhaps your tent captain, or your most reliable friend. To ensure fair access for everyone, please do not join multiple groups or claim extra tickets. Tickets are non-transferable. If you want to attend by yourself, feel free to claim just one ticket.




As mentioned in yesterday’s email, we will not be lining up outside tomorrow due to weather. Doors to the Hall of Fame, located up the ramp from K-Ville, will open exclusively for students with a ticket at 4pm tomorrow afternoon. From 4pm-5pm, there will be free pizza, water and beer, first come, first served. IDs will be required for beer, and there is a limit of 2 per person while supplies last. At 5pm, we’ll start lining up in the K Center Practice Facility. To guarantee entry, you must arrive in the Hall of Fame by 4:30pm.




Let’s get Cameron rocking again on Monday!




SI6HTS DDMF GTHC




Courtney Butash & Elliot Beamer
